name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: My thoughts on AI
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Last weekend, Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, one of the largest AI companies in the world, publicly asked his industry to slow down AI development.
Shortly after, Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, followed suit. Then Elon Musk.
This all came days after an Anthropic researcher quit, citing his belief that this technology could wipe out humanity and that AI companies are “gambling with our lives.”
For years, people have warned that generative AI could slip out of our direct control.
Those safety concerns must be taken seriously.
And this is why I have advocated for strict safety standards on how AI is built and deployed, public oversight over this technology, and using existing laws to hold these companies accountable when they cause harm.
But I want to draw your attention to another reality: Right now, the U.S. economy and our financial futures are riding on Silicon Valley’s bet that AI will soon be immensely profitable and pay off. And that bet isn’t looking good.
The formula for a profitable business isn’t complicated: make more money than you spend. But the biggest AI companies aren’t doing that. They are spending hundreds of billions per year on data centers, chips, and other costs while their ability to make revenues that exceed their already-immense sunk costs are unclear. Experts estimate that these AI companies will require another $600 billion of debt just to finance themselves in 2026 alone. That is more than the entire budgets of the U.S. Departments of Justice, Transportation, and Education combined.
Meanwhile, despite almost every single one of these companies not turning a profit and having sunk billions of investor dollars in development of data centers and other infrastructure, AI companies are also on a spending spree of hundreds of millions of dollars in lobbying and dark money in our elections.
It would be one thing if we were discussing a few private companies with a poor business model. But last year, virtually all stock market gains - 80% - rested entirely on just a handful of AI companies.
That tells us two things:
1. Nearly the entire U.S. economy outside the AI industry is relatively stagnating and faring poorly and the gains from these few companies are disguising it; and
2. Millions of people’s retirements - including their pensions, 401ks, and investments - are potentially exposed to this risk.

That’s why these AI companies’ dubious financial positions matter to working people.
These companies argue that debt is necessary. They’ll tell you that building transformative technologies requires upfront capital, and that massive borrowing today will pay off in generating unprecedented prosperity tomorrow.
But this is not the typical debt that startups take on while they build out a company. We are talking about billions going on trillions of dollars leveraged with no indication that these companies will be able to recoup these funds profitably. And they are increasingly looking to the government as their source of cash.
In an effort to hide their debt, tech companies have been relying on “circular financing” where tech giants like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft give billions to AI startups like OpenAI and Anthropic, only for those startups to hand that money right back to buy AI processing power.
In other words, these AI companies are luring in new investors by making it look like their financials are healthier than they really are.
What’s even worse is that retirement and pension funds are key to supporting this illusion.
When the AI companies issue bonds to raise more money, your pension funds and retirement accounts are some of the biggest buyers. When Musk’s AI business went public, it became part of index funds where millions of Americans invest our savings. Many Americans don’t even know that their retirement investments are tied up in these companies at all.
From Big Tech’s perspective, that’s a feature, not a bug. By tying our futures to their reckless gambling, AI billionaires are trying to make themselves too big to fail. They think they can take such dangerous risks because we will bail them out if things go wrong.
Sound familiar? This scene is dangerously reminiscent of the rampant speculation, corruption, and broken incentives leading up to the 2008 financial crisis that plunged millions of working class Americans into financial chaos that we never fully recovered from.
It is no accident that these warnings from Altman and Amodei come months - if not weeks - before these companies were meant to go public.
When companies go public, they have to be more transparent about how they are doing financially. And after a waiting period, they typically have to let private investors - like their own employees - sell their shares.
_The New York Times_ recently confirmed that OpenAI has postponed going public for this very reason. They are in no rush for the truth about their finances to come out.
But the moment these oligarchs began to seek our public tax dollars and public contracts while exposing their companies to public pension funds and investments, they opened themselves to public accountability and scrutiny.
Silicon Valley billionaires have rigged the game and are attempting to shift their financial risk to working people: If they’re right about AI’s potential, they reap the profits. If they’re wrong and the bubble bursts, they are setting up the American people to pick up the tab.
Heads, they win; tails, we lose.
We can stop this, and we shouldn’t play their game. Together we can address both the economic and safety threats of unrestricted AI development and prevent financial chaos and stabilize market risk.
We must make it clear now that should the AI bubble pop, Congress should not bail out Big Tech.
And across our federal agencies, we have the authorities and tools to hold AI companies and their leaders accountable for releasing dangerous, unvetted, and defective products. We must not wait.
Silicon Valley billionaires want us to believe that AI robots will destroy humanity.
But the biggest threat to humanity are the tech oligarchs themselves.
It’s time we hold them accountable.
Thank you for reading.
In solidarity,
Alexandria
**One last thing before you go...**
Alexandria refuses all corporate lobbyist money and she doesn’t believe elected officials should be bankrolled by special interests at all. Each cycle the big dark money interests rotate - NRA, AIPAC, fossil fuel lobby, etc.
**This cycle it’s the AI lobby.**

A divided federal appeals court on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, upheld the dismissal of a lead-contamination lawsuit brought by Jackson, Mississippi residents. -- Bloomberg Law
JACKSON, Miss. -- The U.S. Constitution does not guarantee Americans clean drinking water -- nor even a right to accurate information from public officials during a public-health crisis. That is the blunt conclusion of a 10-5 ruling issued Friday by the full Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals (covers federal appeals from district courts in three states: Texas, Louisiana, and Mississippi**)** , as first reported by Bloomberg's Jacqueline Thomsen.
The decision in Sterling v. City of Jackson affirms dismissal of a 2022 class action brought by residents who say the city's chronically failing water system delivered lead-contaminated tap water to their homes while officials assured them it was safe to drink. Lead plaintiff Priscilla Sterling, a longtime Jackson school teacher, says several of her children were diagnosed with lead poisoning; the suit sought to represent nearly all residents of Hinds County.
The plaintiffs argued that city and state officials violated the 14th Amendment's due process guarantee both by allowing lead into the municipal supply and by falsely telling residents the water was safe. The en banc majority disagreed, holding that there is no cognizable substantive-due-process right to uncontaminated water and no constitutional right to truthful statements from officials -- even in a drinking-water emergency. Water quality, the judges reasoned, is the business of statutes and regulators -- the Safe Drinking Water Act, EPA oversight, and the Mississippi State Department of Health -- not the federal courts.
Five judges dissented, pointing to what the majority conceded: ingesting lead causes serious, lasting harm. An earlier Fifth Circuit panel had allowed the residents' "state-created danger" claim to proceed in 2025 before the full court vacated that opinion and took the case en banc.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/245b5788-4f3c-48c1-afc3-7f647e6dedb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The ruling lands amid Jackson's years-long water emergency -- decades of underinvestment, repeated boil-water notices, and the near-total system collapse after flooding in 2022. It echoes Flint, Michigan, where residents likewise discovered that lead in tap water carried no federal constitutional remedy. It also fits a broader pattern: the Supreme Court narrowed Clean Water Act protections in its 2023 *Sackett* decision, the Iowa Supreme Court rejected a public-trust challenge to Raccoon River pollution in 2021, and Florida appellate courts have twice struck down voter-approved local clean-water measures as beyond local power.
What's left for residents who get sick? Attorneys for the plaintiffs can seek Supreme Court review, though the high court has never recognized an environmental right in the Constitution. Advocates point instead to the levers the ruling leaves untouched: Congress, EPA enforcement, and state constitutions -- Montana and Pennsylvania among them -- that explicitly protect the right to clean water.
For now, the Fifth Circuit's message is unambiguous: in America, clean water is a policy choice, not a constitutional promise.

Meet Mark Harris:
**Mark Harris is a father, grandfather, pastor, and now a sitting member of Congress who has spent his life in service to his faith, his family, and the people of North Carolina.

Born and raised in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and a graduate of R.J. Reynolds High School, Mark earned a Bachelor of Science in Political Science from Appalachian State University. Maine Attorney General Aaron Frey (D) has signed Maine onto another national Democratic lawsuit against the Trump administration -- this one filed to stop Washington from asking a question that has been in federal immigration law since 1882: can this person support himself, or is he going to live on the taxpayer?
The rule Frey is trying to kill took effect Friday.
On July 20, the Department of Homeland Security published a final rule rescinding the Biden-era public-charge regulation of 2022. That 2022 rule had been a gift to the welfare-and-migration complex. It told immigration officers they could treat an applicant as a "public charge" only if the person was on cash welfare or parked in a government-funded institution. Food stamps didn't count. Medicaid didn't count. Public housing didn't count. The form was designed so that a green-card applicant could be drawing half the American safety net and still look, on paper, like a model of self-sufficiency.
This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..pTun9Ao5nNBfXIFP_ZBaYc6mfzdlNKqx5g5cGAR7jxk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=216305806)
The Trump rule puts those programs back on the table. Starting with applications postmarked or filed electronically on Friday, Sept. 18, USCIS officers may weigh any means-tested public benefit the applicant receives from that date forward -- Medicaid and CHIP, SNAP, housing assistance, and the rest -- when they decide whether the person is "likely at any time to become a public charge."
Maine is currently one of the more generous states when it comes to handing out welfare to noncitizens, including illegal aliens.
Maine uses state money to give full Medicaid to noncitizen children and to pregnant women, including people with no legal status.
Maine also runs a parallel Food Stamp (SNAP) program for some legally present noncitizens federal law now excludes.
Maine towns pay General Assistance to asylum seekers and other people "pursuing a lawful process," for up to two years, though it's unclear whether there's any enforcement of immigration rules in GA.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..9sAziCpATiZoer6Jyz41_bM_A8J4VzkA_e38UGaGn2g?)
In 2025, Gov. Janet Mills proposed eliminating the Food Stamp "Hardship Exemption" for 5,000 non-citizens who were authorized to work but were not working. Those individuals were collecting Food Stamps at a cost to taxpayers of more than $2 million per biennial budget.
Democrat lawmakers killed that provision of Mills' budget.

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241073%2E444211%2EBm8UZv)
Before I joined Powered by People, I spent years working as a Director at Tableau — a company whose entire mission was to help people see and understand data. And if my time in tech taught me anything, it’s this — **data doesn’t lie.**
Right now, our numbers tell an extraordinary story: **today, with 46 days until Election Day, we officially crossed 50,000 voters reached in 2026 year-to-date.**
We’ve built personal relationships with more Texans this year than in the last two years combined, and next week we’re on track to pass **100,000 total voters all-time.**
These aren't just numbers on a dashboard, and they aren’t family or friends already in our bubbles likely to vote the way we will. They are 50,000 eligible Texans — perfect strangers before we connected — who we met face-to-face, registered to vote, and are personally staying in touch with through Election Day.
While other political organizations rely on generic mass texts or impersonal mailers, we build real trust one voter at a time. This is the work that works, and it will be the difference in electing James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa, and democratic candidates down the entire ballot.
Organizing this way takes real resources. As we enter our home stretch, we need our donors to step up so we can close out these final 46 days strong.

Wilson previously had the CCTV cameras turned off. Wilson has shifted her stance on surveillance since taking office, having previously opposed camera expansion during her campaign but now pausing further rollout pending a privacy audit expected by month's end, while allowing existing cameras to remain active. The exchange drew online backlash, with critics noting the apparent contradiction between Wilson calling cameras "useful" during the interview despite her earlier decision to halt their expansion, fueling broader criticism of her handling of the city's public safety strategy. James Talarico 's spiritual mentor exposed for using "Inclusive Bible" Undercover footage shows Rev. Jim Rigby, longtime pastor at Texas Senate candidate James Talarico's church and his spiritual mentor, saying the congregation typically gives new members a copy of the "Inclusive Bible," a translation that removes gendered language and avoids calling Jesus the "Son of God." Talarico has deep ties to the church and Rigby, who baptized him, married his parents, and has mentored him since childhood; Rigby's theology has diverged from traditional Christian doctrine, including questioning core tenets like the Virgin Birth and Resurrection. Talarico 's own public comments -- including calling God "non-binary" and describing himself as a "Christian who hates Christianity" -- echo the church's approach to gender and faith, as he runs a closely contested Senate race against Ken Paxton. * You're currently a free subscriber to . The hum of the grid dies, and the water stops. Troughs are dry. Hezekiah, my long-haired bull, ambles toward one and finds nothing. Gratitude then is the sight of a full rain barrel. He struts toward it. The old red drums, fifty-five gallons apiece, are scattered along fence lines, tucked away from their easy reach for a day such as this. When desire strikes him, Hezekiah knocks them about -- but always he drinks first.
The corporation has a handful of studies and no thirst. That is why it pumps leachate into the deep water, poisoning the very earth we stand on.
Clean, pure water has been our right since the beginning of time.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Now Refuel.**

He runs a boxing federation financed by the Russian state energy giant Gazprom. Days before the celebration, he was in China as part of Putin's delegation. name: GIFFORDS
subject: Making sure you saw this
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Gabby asked us to share this with you.
#

Team: Gabby wanted to make sure you saw her message from yesterday. The gun lobby’s allies are pummeling our endorsed candidates in attack ads. We need your help to close our $7,500 budget gap before the weekend begins.
[**Thank you in advance for anything you can donate to GIFFORDS PAC. Your donation will be put to work to reach the most persuadable voters and stand up the gun lobby’s influence on our politics.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260918-1-b&t=1&akid=11826%2E3935704%2Em2P_f1)
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260918-1-b&t=2&akid=11826%2E3935704%2Em2P_f1)**

* * *
Team —
Gabby Giffords here. I made a difficult decision last night that I need to share with you.
We wrapped up a meeting where it was clear that if we had a little bit more money in our budget, we could make one more play to reach undecided voters before the November elections.
We don’t have the money yet, but I gave the green light anyway.
Let me explain why: We only have 45 days until Election Day. Polls are close — and reaching even 1,000 more voters right now could mean the difference between winning and losing the most competitive of races.
It’s a risky decision, no doubt. But if we want to defeat the NRA’s handpicked candidates and win back a gun sense majority, then we need to take big risks before it’s too late.
[**I made this decision because I know the strength of this grassroots team. I’m hoping you can help us fill our $7,500 budget gap and reach more undecided voters. Will you please chip in to GIFFORDS PAC before the clock strikes midnight?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260918-1-b&t=3&akid=11826%2E3935704%2Em2P_f1)
_If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly:_

| **[Donate $100](https://go.giffords.org/go/17011?c0=giff-em-q32026.oWYbFY&refcode=em260918-1-b&t=25&akid=11826%2E3935704%2Em2P_f1)**
---

---
****
We have an incredible slate of gun sense champions on the ballot this November — but it’ll take all of us to get them into office. Let’s do all we can to make our voices heard. 💪
Gabby Giffords

**Please, take a second to read this...**
GIFFORDS has been on the front lines to save lives from gun violence for more than a decade, but we can’t do it alone.
If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to pass commonsense gun safety legislation across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can.
**If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to stand with Gabby Giffords and donate to GIFFORDS PAC today.**
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/61660?c0=giff-em-q32026.QDXtSy&refcode=em260918-1-b&t=28&akid=11826%2E3935704%2Em2P_f1)**

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. We try to send only the most important information and opportunities to participate via email, but click [here](https://go.giffords.org/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=29&akid=11826%2E3935704%2Em2P_f1) if you'd like to unsubscribe. Giffords PAC was started to support elected officials who step up to fight the gun violence epidemic. Thank you for standing with Gabby and the Giffords team.

| | | | | A Personal Message From Mike
---
Peter,
---
I am reaching out to you directly because, quite frankly, I don't know where else to turn. I've spent the last few hours pacing the room, trying to process what is happening. The latest developments are incredibly daunting, and my heart is heavy with an overwhelming sense of urgency.
---
| [ The threat we warned everyone about has arrived at our doorstep. It is no longer a warning.
**It is reality.** ](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/9URfY5_L_baZe64nhE_vIf7gZ2ErWPnpokhiJRADpdp1EynBWWAVDll-FE5noZnbmatzQdFEqSg4UY4G1DQmSvNUmwE6vcKNw1Q7Rk7KvQH148yl8KKOyczt7W3lJo0QH8JEsqAApYs2YcTCBAW3zTO5LVLLquq-pNLHUQ53Knso6mKYCPPxkBesijEmObCzWZPjVtRRxTGltIrbJk2EVzzkoUvHTsvN2X1AX51fzQLiCSsToRspmoBx7Sffaw5ZEq4WQrM220cdN6UhcR8m9lP_iKZ2qSYEbZAZdY7nBhOTMRK--Wocrg88hYlXM7lT68COJjFk4P6TzSsRn8_DvCqXCI9n70xUXSawnmg-W-M9-GfaE28UsSLOvZ2osriwgMvZ_V0DEIJeA4cAZJcgVUbNZ22luiW9cByeJE4vwNmyArTicrHhFvXuu4bN5u6s_ZgInoZ4Anv8PpIoig_0Pw-d_02Zsieu08cRNgipzhxCN7FVcXM_6AqkiQMQcgf78Lj-mWt6fBw5ydRrEG1SyiOHbLpwwT3JfHV5BiKWVkrDACkDQCZ09YabJPeeYyiyXwDvp82X96c-aSubjEe8r8KHqELhGGdiXApRANUyX8QAt4YPozdeKfOpzng88kw7rtqTAgb6HubfM7kiBR1kJve4aXt0P7AbyHEe2K9VsoBZKXzG_mOeVpRStlGtmffDx5OE1L7D5u9UmOHqQTJ3arkzEqh1nriGo1A2GkXbJYCdcjEb3L4NzfFAI0QZd-To_hEZk9fgcZaHyQ82W38PxjOsbWF8mXaRtchiJkEmW4rbgsY7MVyOgUrbO0B175iHgcoBYCrmV78y2Oja47T2rajO094Fc-JkHi11bKmBuK7wZmUDqBDBjrzXyjklzOpWGsAzHIJz0KGB9NtcOvPTfzqrPecr-cq7262mtSOGOe3rKqiqALorAHtxeVJ2K9a7IgwlMFgB5axzQrn3PYb3V5qDOlyr5QUOlTFbZ2W2k6NHC1qd7llPh0ZaiAG66tYInGa8gQsNQvndevJ32t3J1JpHxdouVX2MFw/BcNLSh9tuZ-qUAbVeLBSp9gmRT7xsU-W/24)

If we do not act immediately, the damage to our country will be completely irreversible. The very fabric of America is beginning to unweave before our eyes, and the clock is ticking down to zero. Republican leadership told me that you are someone who stands strong when everything is on the line. I am coming to you today not with flashy political slogans, but as a humble servant asking for your help. | Turning Point PAC | | | | | [](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDN9AAwAAAAAAwf13KMsHWo25s0-Dt_nf14D2H6-dzmObUbT1FE2QrjQ2jSj8J9NjE2X6vvIcv0FfPrF3zhrBcEo03Ge_mnCmye_-_mt2w8DfmR_jfERRQ)

| | Patriot,
---
The Supreme Court has spoken: mail-in ballots will continue this cycle.
States can still count properly postmarked ballots that arrive after Election Day. The system is locked in.
_That reality changes the math._
**[When more voters cast ballots by mail, the advantage goes to the side that is organized enough to follow those ballots all the way home.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDN9AAwAAAAAAwf13KMted_1dgnYLI0H_WjzmQFYyCwYzzyvGLDRoIIYTNgnykBr-4Y7J-jvXH2_BbCmb3u3UUqZU9RqvdL-0RtFlBu7RN0zOcmzvD0kDQ)**
The side that identifies low-propensity conservatives, gets them to request or complete a ballot, follows up when it sits unfinished on the kitchen table, and makes sure it is returned and counted.
_That is exactly what ballot chasers do_...and the more of them we put in the field, the more voters we reach.
**Here’s how the scale works in practice:**

* One full-time chaser can build relationships with dozens of conservative voters in a precinct who rarely show up.

* Ten chasers can cover multiple neighborhoods and turn isolated contacts into early ballots.

* Fifty or a hundred chasers across key districts create a web of follow-ups that the other side simply cannot match door-for-door.

**[Every additional pair of boots on the ground](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDN9AAwAAAAAAwf13KMuEE7-BxRVnKV-f7et8U7nDNhPO2WaNDoyHbpZW8fa2Bl00V4z9Cx2kTXOYQjt2SnPDvM8Uma8Yj_BBsRuEZZf8FEiM_ewt159qg)** multiplies the number of conversations, the number of ballots requested, the number of reminders delivered, and the number of votes that actually get banked.

[SUPPORT THE CHASERS](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDN9AAwAAAAAAwf13KMvKfJkojpjwJ4B8QVTv2dXPisHEVPsvooIrJ4w6yzQEqJY3X1fjSj03KKVXfFCnWhHaRNFz_JsVOuclCEMBoNiToaoUWbz8jPxFQ)

**[Your support](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDN9AAwAAAAAAwf13KMwfbq4DIbBcId-p1hQ9FMGSZe6KluQcV03h-zV2q96d25Q6s1PYOeOggWoK61YoWSL7wh_1Ql9U8JMbavgSNBVp4J_xSrta0yx8g)** now doesn’t just “support the ground game.” It directly adds capacity.
More people knocking, more flyers and information in the hands of unheard and underrepresented conservatives, more encouragement to vote early and return those ballots.
This midterm is not a normal election.
Control of Congress hangs on a handful of close races. The side that treats mail voting as an afterthought will lose those races. The side that treats it as the main battlefield has a real chance to win.
We still have time to build that capacity. But only if we move now.
**[Put more ballot chasers in the field so we can reach more voters and bank more votes>>](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDN9AAwAAAAAAwf13KMxGsSVZo9b17IqeJpz8yj7WNg1x1-2baK7rYnlGwaO-LSUOmzPgzA2iMPerl8TpPIExA2oKRWOj9fl2JaXqiCeQuaq1-OIDl4Vmw)**

[FUND THE GROUND GAME](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDN9AAwAAAAAAwf13KMyCmivwrvSOZwi-6GHilOf6JDrpDsbEEd0eKJ-Y7TgXTu-YmYZHo9y7SayG2MEBsDwQbpQ-plIuYVqh8QYTotNWbsc8isjI2AgWA)

Every dollar expands the map of doors we can knock and the number of conservatives we can bring into the process.
Let’s do the work that wins,

Tyler Bowyer
Executive Director, Turning Point PAC

Fellow Conservative: You won't find "RINO" in the dictionary. If we wrote the entry ourselves, it would read something like this:
**RINO** , n. /Rye-No/: _A career politician who runs as a "Republican" but cuts deals with Democrats, abandons conservative principles the moment it's convenient, and won't work more than 2.5 days a week to fight for the country._

That's not a joke. That describes far too many Republicans right now.
Case in point: the SAVE America Act. It simply requires people to prove they're citizens before they vote. It's supported by 80% of Americans. President Trump has championed it. The House has passed it multiple times. One version even got 50 votes in the Senate.

In his four campaigns for governor, Greg Abbott has _never_ _once_ been shown trailing in a statewide Texas poll. _That changed yesterday._
**A brand-new poll just showed us ahead of Abbott by four points,** while he's asking Texans for a fourth term. Not within range. Not closing the gap. Ahead. For the first time.
Here’s what’s happening: Texans are getting a clear look at what twelve years of Greg Abbott has actually cost them. Rising grocery bills. Rising property taxes. Data centers flooding the state while the people footing the bill get nothing back. And when they look at me, they’re seeing someone who’s spent her career fighting for Texas families — not just for the people at the top.
**None of this happens without you.** We are competitive in this race because of the 170,000 people who've chipped in to build this campaign. Our people-powered movement is working. We are clearly breaking through.
But Abbott has a firehose of money aimed at us — $67 million in the bank, and he's already outspent us 10-to-1. He's never had to run from behind before. With this poll out there, he's going to open that firehose all the way to drown out our campaign before Texans vote.
We can't match him dollar for dollar. But we can outnumber him — that's how we got here. You haven't joined the 170,000 donors who've built this campaign yet. We need you to become one today by joining this movement with your first gift right now.
**[Can you chip in $5 right now to help us keep building a campaign that can defeat Greg Abbott and take Texas back?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260918_1_sienapoll.N6GCz2&refcode=em20260918-2151&amount=5&t=2&akid=2151%2E299639%2EklmYaT)**

Gratefully,
Gina

Peter, it's
Mallory McMorrow — I ran against Abdul El-Sayed in the Democratic primary.

For a year-and-a-half we were on the same debate stages, chasing the same
voters. I wanted to win, and I ran hard.

This race went down as the most expensive Democratic primary in US
history, and some would argue the most bruising one too.

But the moment the race was called, I endorsed Abdul. No hesitation. And I
was proud to be the first to stand alongside him to introduce him as the
Democratic nominee to be Michigan’s next US Senator at a press conference
the next morning.

Why? Just because I was no longer running didn’t mean the work was done.

That’s because I didn’t get into this work just to win a race or hold a
title. I got into this to fix what’s broken, in Michigan and across this
country.

Donald Trump didn't create this mess. It was the result of years — decades
— of policy decisions under both parties that left more and more Americans
outside of the American dream. People did everything right and kept
getting screwed. And it left the door wide open for a strong man like
Donald Trump who promised to blow it all up.

We need to elect people relentlessly focused on restoring that American
Dream, not for the wealthy few, but for everyone.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260918-1-ak.CBX9rX&amount=10&refcode=em20260918-3221&t=1004&akid=3229%2E251025%2Ek-lsxb ]That’s why I’m asking: Will you join me and chip in $10
to Abdul's campaign today?

Abdul and I both rejected corporate PAC funding in our races. We both
share the belief that nothing in this country will be fixed until the
underlying systems are fixed.

But let me tell you from experience, it’s not an easy decision.

Because it means you watch the checks you turned down go to someone else.
And you hope that people (like you) will have your back.

He made that decision. And he still won.

But it cost every penny he had in his campaign account, meaning his
campaign funds were emptied. At exactly the wrong moment.

Mike Rogers — Trump's handpicked candidate — has $51 million from the
GOP's Senate Leadership Fund to define Abdul before Michigan gets to know
him. The polls have this race inside the margin of error. In 2024,
Michigan’s Senate race came down to just 20,217 votes.

I’ve been on the receiving end of the kind of attacks that kind of money
buys, Peter.
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260918-1-ak.CBX9rX&amount=10&refcode=em20260918-3221&t=1005&akid=3229%2E251025%2Ek-lsxb ]So I'm asking you to help Abdul fight back: chip in $10

I'm not leaving this fight. Together, we’ll send a fighter to the Senate.

Thank you,

Mallory McMorrow
Michigan Senate Majority Whip

**Tales from the Trail:**
Team Knickerbocker went to the Beavercreek popcorn festival on Saturday to talk to voters and enjoy the Ohio weather. Team Knickerbocker is out there rain or shine! Our favorite future congresswoman did what she does best and talked to voters of both parties. She is ready to serve people, not political parties.

Team Knickerbocker joined OhioWins at University of Dayton (GO FLYERS) to talk to students about voting in the upcoming election. Check out Kristina’s social post about the event.
This is also your friendly reminder to check your [voter registration](https://us.list-manage.com/12Z_kRAu5HJ?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d) by October 5th, make a plan to vote, and mark your calendars for the first day of early voting on October 6th.

# DNC Coalitions Partner Briefing
---
| | Dear Partner,
We’re inviting you to our monthly **Partner Briefing on Wednesday, September 23, from 4:00 - 4:30 PM ET**! This is your opportunity to connect with the DNC team for an exclusive update on our momentum and strategic initiatives ahead of the midterms. Here is what we’ll be covering:
* **🗳️ Election Overview** : Get the latest on topline results and an inside look at how we’re building crucial infrastructure.
* **👥 Coalitions Impact & Action: **Discover the latest on our key engagement efforts.
* **🤝 Program Engagement:** Discover our latest programs and how you can get involved.

**EVENT DETAILS:**
* **Date:** Wednesday, September 23, 2026
* **Time:** 4:00 - 4:30 PM ET
* **Location:** ZOOM Webinar
* **Registration Link:** [win.dnc.org/september-partner-briefing](https://us.list-manage.com/nlh7Q8qTZpl?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah leader claims U.S. is directly supporting Saudi Arabia, rejects accusations of striking Mecca:** Ansarallah leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi claimed the U.S. is directly supporting Saudi military operations against Yemen, saying Washington has deployed "a joint force of 200 military experts" who are "managing the operations" from Saudi Arabia. He said Saudi forces are fighting "with aircraft obtained from America" and "bombs purchased from America," and claimed Riyadh is seeking greater direct U.S. involvement in the war.
* On Sunday, Ansarallah told U.S. officials it would limit Red Sea attacks to Saudi ships**** and continue to uphold the**** U.S.-Ansarallah ceasefire during Oman-facilitated talks in Muscat, Reuters reported.
* Al-Houthi said that an end to the conflict requires Saudi Arabia to halt its attacks on Yemen and lift its blockade. "This is what we want, this is our issue: for Saudi Arabia to stop its aggression against us," he said, adding that Riyadh must "end its blockade of our people" and stop depriving Yemenis of the country's oil and gas resources.
* Al-Houthi also rejected Saudi allegations that Ansarallah had targeted Mecca, calling the accusation "a great lie" and accusing Riyadh of using it to encourage other countries to join the conflict. "Our lives, our souls, our wealth, and everything we possess are a sacrifice for Mecca and the Islamic holy sites," he said.
* **Fighting continues in Taiz as government forces claim 30 Ansarallah fighters killed:** Yemeni forces, backed by Saudi airstrikes, are attempting to regain a foothold in the contested mountainous district of Al-Waziyah in western Taiz governorate, along the approaches to Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Saudi-backed forces claimed 30 Ansarallah fighters were killed and 60 wounded, figures that could not be independently verified. They also reported airstrikes on positions around Al-Dhikra Junction, Al-Damna and Al-Rahida.
* In nearby Mocha, a strategic Red Sea port captured by Ansarallah last week, Saudi-backed forces said airstrikes targeted Ansarallah movements, reinforcements, and supply routes as they seek to regain territory along the coast.
* **One killed, two wounded after Saudi intercepts drone over Taif:** one person was killed and two others wounded, one critically, by falling debris after an Ansarallah drone was intercepted and destroyed over Taif, Saudi Civil Defense [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3b1f0df0-d900-46c7-b8d7-6ac323bd8481?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday. Several buildings and vehicles were also damaged.
* **Over 112,000 displaced in Yemen:** More than 112,000 people have been displaced in Yemen in the last two weeks amid renewed fighting between Ansarallah and Saudi-backed government forces, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/35ea7a45-022c-4c21-99cb-3a966c763f17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the UN migration agency. Nearly 3,000 others have fled by sea to Djibouti, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said.
* "Our resources are very, very, very limited and our stocks will be depleted very soon," Abdusattor Esoev, IOM's Chief of Mission in Yemen, said in a statement.
* **Saudi Aramco tells European customers they will receive no crude next month after pipeline attack:** Saudi Aramco [told](https://substack.com/redirect/c6794a6e-3c4f-4516-994f-efca0e626edb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least two European refiners they will receive no Saudi crude under their regular contracts next month, with the decision applying to all European buyers, Bloomberg reported on Friday.
* The move follows last week's drone attack that forced Saudi Arabia to shut its key East-West pipeline to the Red Sea. The pipeline is expected to partially restart within days but could take up to six weeks to return to full operation.
* **U.S. clears possible $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia:** The State Department approved a possible Foreign Military Sale of 48 F-35 Lightning II fighter jets and related equipment to Saudi Arabia and notified Congress of the proposed deal.
* The Saudi Embassy in Washington welcomed the proposed sale, saying, in a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/1445b41d-a57f-47ae-b420-c8c02e6e6ad9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, it reflects the "strength and enduring nature of the Saudi-U.S. strategic partnership" and the continued advancement of defense cooperation between the two countries.
* **Italy prepares naval mission, calls for more ships in Red Sea:** Italy is [preparing](https://substack.com/redirect/ef6e2f0c-46d3-42cb-8f32-570d925ae196?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to deploy additional naval assets to the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab amid concerns over merchant shipping, Al-Monitor reported.
* Italy, which participates in Aspides, the European Union's naval mission to protect commercial shipping in the Red Sea, said Thursday it was preparing its own naval mission rather than waiting for a broader EU response. "After what I said, something moved within Aspides, but we need more ships," Defense Minister Guido Crosetto told Reuters, adding that "the only nations really supporting [security efforts] are Italy and Greece."
* Rome has not specified how many ships it could send or detailed the measures under consideration.

# Iran
* **Iran strikes tanker in Hormuz:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it struck a Togo-flagged oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, according to the state broadcaster. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations separately said a tanker had been hit by an unknown projectile in the strait, though it was unclear if it was referring to the same incident.
* **Massive government rally in Tehran:** Hundreds of thousands of Iranians rallied in Tehran on Friday in the biggest government-organized demonstration since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on Iran in February. The state broadcaster estimated over 300,000 people in the demonstration, which featured drones and weaponry on parade.
* Tens of thousands of Iranians who have registered with volunteer units, or who wish to sign up, joined the rally. Tehran's Republican Guard chief, Gen. Hassan Hassanzadeh, told the state broadcaster that over 600,000 had registered to participate in the training.
* **U.S. approves visas for Iranian president, foreign minister to attend UN General Assembly:** The Trump administration approved visas for Iran's "core delegation," including President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, to attend next week's UN General Assembly meetings in New York.
* The decision comes more than six months into the U.S.-Iran war, with negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz and returning to nuclear talks remaining stalled.
* On Wednesday, the Trump administration denied visas to a high-level Palestinian delegation, including Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, for the same UN General Assembly gathering, marking the second consecutive year Palestinian officials have been denied entry. The State Department cited, among other reasons, the Palestinian Authority's pursuit of legal action against Israel at the International Court of Justice and International Criminal Court.
* The U.S. is barring Iranian officials attending the UN General Assembly from purchasing luxury goods or obtaining wholesale club memberships. "On one side stands a brutal economic war, deliberately designed to inflict maximum pain and suffering on every Iranian citizen," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei wrote on X, criticizing the measure. "On the other stands the theatrical announcement of measures to stop Iranian officials from supposedly shopping at an American wholesale club."
* **South Korea rules out involvement in Hormuz "conflict," says "minimum level" of action needed to protect shipping: **South Korean President Lee Jae Myung [said](https://substack.com/redirect/2014dac3-b936-467c-8b8b-b34527e7b491?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday that Seoul will not deploy troops in a way that could involve the country in an overseas conflict, Yonhap reported.
* Lee said South Korea nevertheless needs to undertake a "minimum level of activities" to protect its citizens, vessels, and crude oil transportation routes. Seoul is reviewing ways to strengthen those measures, while its Cheonghae naval unit has expanded the scope of its activities in the region.
* Last week, a South Korean assessment team returned from the United Arab Emirates after reviewing security conditions in the region. U.S. President Donald Trump is pressing allies to contribute to securing freedom of navigation through the Strait.
* **FT: Iran shifts trade overland as U.S. blockade disrupts Gulf routes:** Iran is [increasingly routing](https://substack.com/redirect/2ecced1d-80e4-4418-85d1-de9ea0eeeeb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) trade through its land borders, particularly Turkey, after the U.S. naval blockade and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz curtailed maritime trade, the Financial Times reports.
* Before the war, more than 80% of Iran's roughly 180 million tons of annual trade moved by sea from its Gulf coast. Iran's non-oil exports fell 28% and imports 26% in the five months ending August 22 compared with last year.
* Trade with Turkey rose 19% to $3.2 billion in the first half of the year, while imports through the Gurbulak-Bazargan land crossing surged 250% in the five months to August 12.
* But long border delays and limited infrastructure mean even doubling overland and Caspian trade cannot replace lost maritime trade, experts told the FT. Moving Iran-China trade overland rather than by sea could also add an estimated $18 billion a year in costs.
* **Iran-U.S. war and Hormuz disruption cost Arab economies nearly $150 billion in the first month, UN agency says:** The ongoing conflict and disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz caused losses equivalent to roughly 4% of Arab states' combined GDP during the first month alone, according to the UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA).
* ESCWA Executive Secretary told a UN Security Council meeting on maritime security that the disruption is affecting far more than oil and gas, driving up freight and insurance costs, threatening food security, and weighing on investment across the region.
* Around 25% of global seaborne oil trade and 19% of LNG shipments have historically passed through Hormuz.
* **U.S. sanctions on Iranian airlines threaten supply chain for essential medicines, researchers warn:** The Trump administration's latest sanctions on Iran's aviation sector [threaten](https://substack.com/redirect/e45de496-8cdc-453d-a856-1a4ce66f8ce1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the supply chain for essential medicines and medical supplies in Iran, Bourse & Bazaar Foundation researchers wrote.
* Over 60% of Iran's medical imports arrive by air, making them roughly seven times more dependent on aviation than Iranian imports generally.
* Over 30% of medical imports through Tehran's main airport are hormone-based medications, including insulin and cancer treatments, the report noted. Another 10% are vaccines and 6% blood products.
* **U.S. offers up to $15 million for information on IRGC financial networks:** The State Department's Rewards for Justice program [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/199a0259-df20-4567-9db2-9a6c6434a242?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a new appeal for information about Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps's (IRGC) alleged use of digital asset exchanges and other financial mechanisms to evade sanctions and access international financial systems. The reward offers up to $15 million for information leading to the disruption of the IRGC's financial mechanisms.
* **Amnesty: Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity in 2022 protest crackdown:** A new [report](https://substack.com/redirect/51a93110-5205-4f63-89ba-a96c6f865a06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Amnesty International has found that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during their suppression of the nationwide "Woman Life Freedom" uprising in 2022. The report, more than 1,000 pages long, details the use of "murder, torture, enforced disappearance, imprisonment, rape and persecution on political, gender, ethnic and religious grounds." It also identifies 87 officials it says should be criminally investigated for crimes against humanity.
* "[Iranian authorities] waged a widespread and systematic attack against a civilian population demanding dignity, human rights and fundamental political change, pursuant to a state policy of using lethal force to obliterate dissent," Agnes Callamard, Amnesty International's Secretary General, said in a statement. "This report is being published at a time when people in Iran are also facing the devastating consequences of unlawful attacks by the USA and Israel. Amnesty International unequivocally opposes violations of international law by all parties and rejects any attempt to instrumentalize the suffering of victims of human rights violations in Iran to justify unlawful attacks that inflict further civilian harm."

# Palestine
* **Two women shot by Israeli forces in central Gaza:**
* Two Palestinian women were [wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/4da54323-396e-4e3c-82c9-527e2b3a8045?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Israeli gunfire toward residential homes and tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps in Central Gaza on Friday, according to WAFA.
* **Five children rescued from damaged home as Gaza government announces emergency plan for buildings at risk of collapse:**
* Civil Defense crews rescued five children who became trapped on the second floor of their home after its staircase collapsed in the Sabra neighborhood, south of Gaza City. The families were evacuated and warned not to return to the house, which had been damaged by Israeli attacks and remains at risk of collapse.
* Two days ago, the collapse of another residential building in Gaza City killed 21 Palestinians, including 12 children and five women.
* The IDF [responded](https://substack.com/redirect/250e4379-4289-4984-aff1-6ebf8a31b668?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Drop Site on the collapse, saying "the IDF did not strike the building in question during the war." The building, however, showed visible cracks and signs of damage from Israel's assault on Gaza, which damaged 80% of structures across the Strip, including two-thirds that were destroyed, according to the UN.
* More than 2,000 damaged buildings across Gaza are at risk of collapse, according to Civil Defense. Gaza authorities and representatives from international, UN, and Arab organizations agreed Friday on an emergency plan to address hundreds of war-damaged buildings at risk of collapse across the Strip, according to Gaza's Government Media Office. The meeting called for the immediate entry of heavy machinery, specialized equipment, fuel, and oil, as well as the allocation of land for shelters for residents living in unsafe buildings.
* **Israeli settler attacks injure at least six Palestinians across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Hebron:** Armed Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli forces, [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/b7f3a28d-250d-4f8f-bf7f-a6234f963859?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian farmers trying to reach their land in Wadi Al-Shannar, east of Halhul, on Friday. The settlers assaulted and detained several farmers, according to WAFA.
* **Ramallah:** Five Palestinians were injured after Israeli settlers [threw stones](https://substack.com/redirect/33d6b187-c77e-419b-9901-d0042a7e18bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at their vehicle near the entrance to Yabroud, east of Ramallah, causing the vehicle to overturn.
* **Jericho:** A Palestinian was injured when Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/8f3fc2b1-403e-4e10-afe3-7f866b33c919?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) families in Khirbet Allan, north of Jericho in the Jordan Valley. The settlers attempted to steal sheep, attacked residents with stones, and damaged a Palestinian-owned vehicle.
* **East Jerusalem:** Israeli forces [beat](https://substack.com/redirect/35ffc4c4-0033-42a0-86e5-5cd168595872?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian man outside Lions' Gate, one of the entrances to Al-Aqsa Mosque.
* **Israel adds 2,167 units to E1 settlement plan, bringing total to 3,401:** Israel added a tender for 2,167 housing units to its E1 settlement expansion plan in the occupied West Bank, Reuters reported, on top of 1,234 units announced in August.
* The E1 project would cut the occupied West Bank off from East Jerusalem and disrupt territorial contiguity between its northern and southern areas. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has said the plan would "bury" the idea of a Palestinian state.
* Bidding is scheduled to open October 25, two days before Israel's parliamentary election.
* **" The whole case is related to her journalistic work": Palestinian-American journalist detained by Israel at Hasharon: **Palestinian-American journalist and Drop Site contributor Naqaa Hamed is [being held](https://substack.com/redirect/ca8f4240-928f-42d6-a0c4-4ff26cc8308f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Hasharon, a temporary detention facility in central Israel, and is expected to be transferred to Damon Prison, where most Palestinian female prisoners are held.
* Hamed's lawyer told Drop Site she was accused of incitement against Israeli settlers and the army, communicating with the enemy, and cooperating with the enemy during a military court session on Thursday.
* Her lawyer argued that Hamed was a professional journalist and her arrest came solely because of a campaign targeting her by Israeli settlers. He told Drop Site "the whole case is related to her journalistic work." The military court ruled to extend her detention by six days to complete their "investigation." Mahajneh submitted an appeal.
* The Committee to Protect Journalists condemned Hamed's detention, saying "Unsubstantiated espionage allegations must not be used to criminalize journalism, and the systemic harassment and intimidation targeting her work in the occupied West Bank must end."
* Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen called for her immediate release, saying in a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/492f2346-2520-4c4f-84a9-f322904e1ca0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, "Another American citizen wrongfully detained by the Israeli govt."
* **Report: Israel kills one, wounds 15 on Thursday, total ceasefire violations reach 4,931:** Israel committed 19 ceasefire violations in Gaza on Thursday, killing one Palestinian and wounding 15 others, bringing the total documented violations since the ceasefire took effect to 4,931, according to a [document](https://substack.com/redirect/1df5140b-5813-4e3a-804c-49ece2ea063b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) shared by the Palestinian side with mediators and obtained by Drop Site News.
* Since the ceasefire took effect, 1,387 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks--including 297 children, 140 women, and 42 elderly people--and 4,784 wounded, nearly half of them children, women, or elderly.
* Only 35% of the agreed humanitarian and commercial aid has entered Gaza since the ceasefire began, according to the document, while overall movement of people through the crossing has reached just 39.1% of the agreed level.
* **Qatar pledges 1.3 million liters of fuel for Gaza, enough for just 16 days of health sector needs:** Qatar [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/93708ea4-d2cc-4dba-9b21-307589397c97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an agreement with the United Nations to provide Gaza with approximately 1.3 million liters of fuel, its Foreign Ministry announced on Thursday. The grant is intended to keep hospitals, medical centers, and other essential humanitarian infrastructure operating, amid severe shortages resulting from Israel's restrictions despite the nominal ceasefire.
* The World Health Organization estimates that Gaza's health sector needs about 80,000 liters daily. At that rate, Qatar's 1.3 million-liter grant would cover only about 16 days of healthcare operations. If shared with water, sanitation and other humanitarian services--as Qatar says it will be--it will last considerably less.
* The announcement provides no delivery schedule.
* **Trump 's "Board of Peace" to brief countries at UN on stalled Gaza reconstruction and governance plans: **The U.S.-controlled Board of Peace will [brief](https://substack.com/redirect/cb23dec0-9f18-476b-9f8c-547e3bbac557?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) representatives from dozens of countries, the EU, and UN agencies on September 23, during the UN General Assembly, on its stalled plans to rebuild and govern Gaza, The Times of Israel reported.
* The meeting will cover negotiations over Hamas's weapons and hear from the Palestinian technocratic committee (NCAG) about 71 projects for its first six months.
* None of the projects has a start date as the initiative remains frozen because Israel rejects the Board's plan to decommission the weapons of all armed factions, despite Hamas accepting its terms on July 30.

# U.S. News

* Earlier this week, the Supreme Court rejected President Donald Trump's bid to restrict mail ballots.
* One tenth of all Americans this year is a resident of a different congressional district than in 2024, according to a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/459b76e6-4b1f-4fd1-97a7-b25fc2f4c5ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Project Democracy, following an unprecedented flurry of redistricting in the House that has redrawn the congressional map**.**

* **White House withdraws Lance Schroyer 's nomination to lead ICE: **The White House [withdrew](https://substack.com/redirect/35227db0-9e9e-4658-a0c1-2a26d51653f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its nomination of **Lance Schroyer,** a former Oklahoma Highway Patrol major and ally of DHS Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** , to lead Immigration and Customs Enforcement on Thursday, less than three months after President Donald Trump nominated him.
* The nomination's rescission surprised officials in the Department, according to several DHS insiders cited by the Washington Post.
* Schroyer faced mounting resistance in the Senate, where Homeland Security Committee Chairman **Rand Paul** had not scheduled a confirmation hearing, and border czar **Tom Homan** had suggested the role should go to someone "who knows the job." ICE has not had a Senate-confirmed director in over a decade.
* **Trump administration weighs at least 12 data center projects on federal public lands:** The Bureau of Land Management is [reviewing](https://substack.com/redirect/eb12f31d-8c76-4aea-b0eb-20b2c5e71018?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) proposals covering more than 17,600 acres across Arizona, Idaho, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, and Wyoming for data centers and related infrastructure, an unprecedented use of public land that local officials in several states told The Washington Sun they were unaware was under consideration.
* The largest proposal, a 10,200-acre project from nuclear startup Valar Atomics near Green River, Utah, would co-locate a data center with small nuclear reactors.
* Another case involves the Idaho-based firm Rhea Data, which has proposed a 4,000,000-square-foot data center near Boise powered partly by a new natural gas facility. Only one such project, on federal land in Nevada, has been approved so far. It remains on hold amid a legal challenge.
* **Microsoft executive calls AI "largest theft of labor in human history": **Microsoft's director of applied science called the training of large language models the "largest theft of labor in human history" and "an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions," the Washington Post[ reported](https://substack.com/redirect/f84337ae-efd2-45d3-ad6f-e94e28caadc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), according to a document unsealed Thursday as part of a lawsuit filed by the New York Times against Microsoft and OpenAI. The unsealed legal brief quotes internal documents obtained via legal discovery.
* Separately, Anthropic[ said](https://substack.com/redirect/8e53e519-bf5a-48f5-b27a-09fcd0d48726?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) yesterday in a blog post that its Claude chatbot "'leads' 26% of Anthropic's AI R&D work," and that "AI systems are increasingly being used to build the next version of themselves," The Post [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/11bce4e7-a2c8-4e8b-bf4b-215b9155031c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **Man who sprayed Rep. Ilhan Omar with vinegar sentenced to 14 months in prison:** **Anthony Kazmierczak** , 56, was [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/7c610453-18f7-496a-a1f2-cdc62c1b77c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday to 14 months in prison and three years of supervised release, during which he cannot make contact with Rep. **Ilhan Omar,** who he assaulted with a water-and-apple-cider-vinegar spray during a Minneapolis town hall in January.
* U.S. District Judge **Joan Ericksen** noted that the attack "wasn't a spur-of-the-moment act," given that Kazmierczak had secured tickets weeks in advance. He also texted acquaintances before the attack indicating he planned to "do something" involving Omar.
* Kazmierczak, who has Parkinson's disease and whose attorney argued that he had not taken his mental health medications prior to the attack, apologized to Omar in court on Thursday.
* **Pentagon reinstates mandatory testosterone screening for male service members over 30** : The Pentagon [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/3a63a561-6c43-47e5-be7a-e32487489595?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) updated guidance Thursday requiring mandatory testosterone deficiency screening for male active-duty and reserve service members over 30, after temporarily rescinding earlier guidance this month. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said in July the screening and testosterone replacement therapy initiative was an effort to keep troops "on the leading edge of lethality."
* The screening will reportedly assess military personnel for symptoms including erectile dysfunction, reduced sexual desire, and diminished physical performance, and will also document risk factors like obesity and diabetes.
* A corresponding clinical guideline for female service members remains under review, the director of the Defense Health Agency added.

# Other International News
* **Pakistan mosque bombing kills at least 16:** A suicide car bomb [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/81167ec7-b126-477e-add2-e86e241e0e44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a mosque inside a police headquarters in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, during Friday prayers, killing at least 16 people and injuring more than 56.
* After the bombing, gunmen then tried to enter the police complex and exchanged fire with officers. At least five police officers and 10 civilians were among those killed, and several of the wounded were reported in critical condition.
* No group immediately claimed responsibility. Both the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, and an ISIL affiliate are active in the region and regularly attack security forces.
* **Spanish police clear migrants from Ceuta:** Spanish riot police and military personnel began [clearing](https://substack.com/redirect/04031f1b-f183-4f58-8159-6504612d88b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) migrants from beaches in the North African enclave of Ceuta on Friday, using batons and firing rubber bullets into the air as crowds competed for limited places in temporary accommodation.
* Spain estimates about 10,000 migrants remain in the territory after more than 72,000 people crossed from Morocco during an unprecedented border rush at the end of July.
* Authorities have opened temporary housing in Ceuta's port for about 1,700 adult men, but aid groups say thousands remain homeless and sleeping on beaches and pavements.
* **Russians vote in first parliamentary election since Ukraine invasion:**
* Russians began [voting](https://substack.com/redirect/174637b3-4d64-470d-ba2a-9f177709fefe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday in a three-day parliamentary election that will determine the makeup of the 450-seat State Duma, with the ruling United Russia party expected to retain power.
* President Vladimir Putin has framed the vote as evidence of public backing for the military campaign in Ukraine, saying it would demonstrate that "millions of people stand behind our soldiers." Most explicitly anti-war candidates were excluded from the ballot, while the liberal Yabloko party was barred from competing nationally after Russia's Supreme Court ruled it had violated electoral rules, a decision the party disputes.
* **Belarus continues military drills near NATO border:** Belarus has [deployed](https://substack.com/redirect/b8a28e25-30a6-4659-9ed4-67d3e4028976?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tanks, artillery, and drone units for exercises in the Brest and Grodno regions bordering Poland and Lithuania, close to the Suwalki Gap--the roughly 40-mile corridor connecting the Baltic states to the rest of NATO.
* For several days, Belarusian forces are practicing counter-sabotage operations, dispersed command posts, artillery fire and drone warfare. Minsk says the exercises are defensive and rejects suggestions that they are preparations for an attack.
* The drills come amid heightened tension along NATO's eastern flank. Poland has recently scrambled aircraft during Russian strikes near its border, while an Italian NATO fighter shot down a suspected Russian explosive-laden drone that entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus on September 14.
* **Chinese coast guard ship collides with Philippines government vessel near Palawan:** The Philippines Coast Guard [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/667e896c-bf4d-452e-a600-6559c4460f31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Chinese coast guard vessel of deliberately ramming a Philippines government ship in the South China Sea on Friday during a mission to deliver fuel to Filipino fishermen.
* China disputed the account, saying the vessel ignored warnings, changed course and accelerated into the Chinese ship's path.
* The incident is the latest in a series of confrontations between Beijing and Manila in disputed waters, including recent water-cannon incidents near Scarborough Shoal. The Philippines rejects China's sweeping sovereignty claims in the South China Sea, while Beijing continues to assert jurisdiction over most of the waterway.
* **Philippines school shooting leaves three dead in third deadly attack since June:** At least three people, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman, were killed in a [shooting](https://substack.com/redirect/d337cc40-e65b-42cf-920a-c0747dc563d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at a school in Banga, South Cotabato, in the southern Philippines. Eight students aged 14 to 17 were injured, four of them critically, according to local officials.
* The attack is the Philippines' third deadly school shooting since June. In August, a student in Zamboanga live streamed himself killing another student before taking his own life, while a June shooting at a public high school in Tacloban left three students dead and 20 injured.
* **Washington insiders are positioning themselves to take over business inside Cuba:** Trump- and Rubio-linked investors, lobbyists, and political allies are [jockeying for access](https://substack.com/redirect/46f6b699-787b-4d23-8064-d0e6a6593162?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Cuban assets as foreign companies are forced out amid Washington's maximum pressure campaign. Reporting from Ed Augustin and Lee Schlenker points to potential deals involving mining, hotels, shipping, and humanitarian aid, while foreign companies pushed out by U.S. sanctions leave openings for U.S.-linked investors and businesses.
* Washington continues to intensify sanctions aimed at forcing political change in Cuba, with Rubio [announcing](https://substack.com/redirect/ec0d4d67-565f-4ca7-86be-c40e8f777b85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a new wave of sanctions on Thursday targeting state-run enterprises, military enterprises and officials. The latest sanctions come as a new report reveals thousands of shipping containers--filled with food, medicine and humanitarian aid--destined for Cuba are [stranded](https://substack.com/redirect/493de779-ca07-460e-91fa-79ec3ec797ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) throughout the Caribbean as shipping companies aim to avoid U.S. sanctions.

Friday, September 18, 2026 -** Ansarallah leader claims U.S. is directly supporting Saudi Arabia, rejects accusations of striking Mecca. Fighting continues in Taiz as government forces claim 30 Ansarallah fighters killed. One killed, two wounded after Saudi intercepts drone over Taif. Over 112,000 displaced in Yemen. Amnesty: Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity in 2022 protest crackdown. Two women shot by Israeli forces in central Gaza. Five children rescued from damaged home as Gaza government announces emergency plan for buildings at risk of collapse. Israeli settler attacks injure at least six Palestinians across the occupied West Bank. Israel adds 2,167 units to E1 settlement plan, bringing total to 3,401. "The whole case is related to her journalistic work": Palestinian-American journalist detained by Israel at Hasharon. Qatar pledges 1.3 million liters of fuel for Gaza, enough for just 16 days of health sector needs. Two wounded as Israeli ceasefire violations continue in southern Lebanon. Ilhan Omar with vinegar sentenced to 14 months in prison. Pentagon reinstates mandatory testosterone screening for male service members over 30. Pakistan mosque bombing kills at least 16.
