This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Ansarallah leader claims U.S. is directly supporting Saudi Arabia, rejects accusations of striking Mecca: Ansarallah leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi claimed the U.S. is directly supporting Saudi military operations against Yemen, saying Washington has deployed "a joint force of 200 military experts" who are "managing the operations" from Saudi Arabia. He said Saudi forces are fighting "with aircraft obtained from America" and "bombs purchased from America," and claimed Riyadh is seeking greater direct U.S. involvement in the war. On Sunday, Ansarallah told U.S. officials it would limit Red Sea attacks to Saudi ships** and continue to uphold the U.S.-Ansarallah ceasefire during Oman-facilitated talks in Muscat, Reuters reported. Al-Houthi said that an end to the conflict requires Saudi Arabia to halt its attacks on Yemen and lift its blockade. "This is what we want, this is our issue: for Saudi Arabia to stop its aggression against us," he said, adding that Riyadh must "end its blockade of our people" and stop depriving Yemenis of the country's oil and gas resources. Al-Houthi also rejected Saudi allegations that Ansarallah had targeted Mecca, calling the accusation "a great lie" and accusing Riyadh of using it to encourage other countries to join the conflict. "Our lives, our souls, our wealth, and everything we possess are a sacrifice for Mecca and the Islamic holy sites," he said. Fighting continues in Taiz as government forces claim 30 Ansarallah fighters killed: Yemeni forces, backed by Saudi airstrikes, are attempting to regain a foothold in the contested mountainous district of Al-Waziyah in western Taiz governorate, along the approaches to Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Saudi-backed forces claimed 30 Ansarallah fighters were killed and 60 wounded, figures that could not be independently verified. They also reported airstrikes on positions around Al-Dhikra Junction, Al-Damna and Al-Rahida. In nearby Mocha, a strategic Red Sea port captured by Ansarallah last week, Saudi-backed forces said airstrikes targeted Ansarallah movements, reinforcements, and supply routes as they seek to regain territory along the coast. One killed, two wounded after Saudi intercepts drone over Taif: one person was killed and two others wounded, one critically, by falling debris after an Ansarallah drone was intercepted and destroyed over Taif, Saudi Civil Defense on Thursday. Several buildings and vehicles were also damaged. Over 112,000 displaced in Yemen: More than 112,000 people have been displaced in Yemen in the last two weeks amid renewed fighting between Ansarallah and Saudi-backed government forces, to the UN migration agency. Nearly 3,000 others have fled by sea to Djibouti, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said. "Our resources are very, very, very limited and our stocks will be depleted very soon," Abdusattor Esoev, IOM's Chief of Mission in Yemen, said in a statement. Saudi Aramco tells European customers they will receive no crude next month after pipeline attack: Saudi Aramco at least two European refiners they will receive no Saudi crude under their regular contracts next month, with the decision applying to all European buyers, Bloomberg reported on Friday. The move follows last week's drone attack that forced Saudi Arabia to shut its key East-West pipeline to the Red Sea. The pipeline is expected to partially restart within days but could take up to six weeks to return to full operation. U.S. clears possible $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia: The State Department approved a possible Foreign Military Sale of 48 F-35 Lightning II fighter jets and related equipment to Saudi Arabia and notified Congress of the proposed deal. The Saudi Embassy in Washington welcomed the proposed sale, saying, in a on X, it reflects the "strength and enduring nature of the Saudi-U.S. strategic partnership" and the continued advancement of defense cooperation between the two countries. Italy prepares naval mission, calls for more ships in Red Sea: Italy is to deploy additional naval assets to the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab amid concerns over merchant shipping, Al-Monitor reported. Italy, which participates in Aspides, the European Union's naval mission to protect commercial shipping in the Red Sea, said Thursday it was preparing its own naval mission rather than waiting for a broader EU response. "After what I said, something moved within Aspides, but we need more ships," Defense Minister Guido Crosetto told Reuters, adding that "the only nations really supporting [security efforts] are Italy and Greece." Rome has not specified how many ships it could send or detailed the measures under consideration. Iran Iran strikes tanker in Hormuz: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it struck a Togo-flagged oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, according to the state broadcaster. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations separately said a tanker had been hit by an unknown projectile in the strait, though it was unclear if it was referring to the same incident. Massive government rally in Tehran: Hundreds of thousands of Iranians rallied in Tehran on Friday in the biggest government-organized demonstration since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on Iran in February. The state broadcaster estimated over 300,000 people in the demonstration, which featured drones and weaponry on parade. Tens of thousands of Iranians who have registered with volunteer units, or who wish to sign up, joined the rally. Tehran's Republican Guard chief, Gen. Hassan Hassanzadeh, told the state broadcaster that over 600,000 had registered to participate in the training. U.S. approves visas for Iranian president, foreign minister to attend UN General Assembly: The Trump administration approved visas for Iran's "core delegation," including President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, to attend next week's UN General Assembly meetings in New York. The decision comes more than six months into the U.S.-Iran war, with negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz and returning to nuclear talks remaining stalled. On Wednesday, the Trump administration denied visas to a high-level Palestinian delegation, including Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, for the same UN General Assembly gathering, marking the second consecutive year Palestinian officials have been denied entry. The State Department cited, among other reasons, the Palestinian Authority's pursuit of legal action against Israel at the International Court of Justice and International Criminal Court. The U.S. is barring Iranian officials attending the UN General Assembly from purchasing luxury goods or obtaining wholesale club memberships. "On one side stands a brutal economic war, deliberately designed to inflict maximum pain and suffering on every Iranian citizen," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei wrote on X, criticizing the measure. "On the other stands the theatrical announcement of measures to stop Iranian officials from supposedly shopping at an American wholesale club." South Korea rules out involvement in Hormuz "conflict," says "minimum level" of action needed to protect shipping: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung Friday that Seoul will not deploy troops in a way that could involve the country in an overseas conflict, Yonhap reported. Lee said South Korea nevertheless needs to undertake a "minimum level of activities" to protect its citizens, vessels, and crude oil transportation routes. Seoul is reviewing ways to strengthen those measures, while its Cheonghae naval unit has expanded the scope of its activities in the region. Last week, a South Korean assessment team returned from the United Arab Emirates after reviewing security conditions in the region. U.S. President Donald Trump is pressing allies to contribute to securing freedom of navigation through the Strait. FT: Iran shifts trade overland as U.S. blockade disrupts Gulf routes: Iran is trade through its land borders, particularly Turkey, after the U.S. naval blockade and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz curtailed maritime trade, the Financial Times reports. Before the war, more than 80% of Iran's roughly 180 million tons of annual trade moved by sea from its Gulf coast. Iran's non-oil exports fell 28% and imports 26% in the five months ending August 22 compared with last year. Trade with Turkey rose 19% to $3.2 billion in the first half of the year, while imports through the Gurbulak-Bazargan land crossing surged 250% in the five months to August 12. But long border delays and limited infrastructure mean even doubling overland and Caspian trade cannot replace lost maritime trade, experts told the FT. Moving Iran-China trade overland rather than by sea could also add an estimated $18 billion a year in costs. Iran-U.S. war and Hormuz disruption cost Arab economies nearly $150 billion in the first month, UN agency says: The ongoing conflict and disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz caused losses equivalent to roughly 4% of Arab states' combined GDP during the first month alone, according to the UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA). ESCWA Executive Secretary told a UN Security Council meeting on maritime security that the disruption is affecting far more than oil and gas, driving up freight and insurance costs, threatening food security, and weighing on investment across the region. Around 25% of global seaborne oil trade and 19% of LNG shipments have historically passed through Hormuz. U.S. sanctions on Iranian airlines threaten supply chain for essential medicines, researchers warn: The Trump administration's latest sanctions on Iran's aviation sector the supply chain for essential medicines and medical supplies in Iran, Bourse & Bazaar Foundation researchers wrote. Over 60% of Iran's medical imports arrive by air, making them roughly seven times more dependent on aviation than Iranian imports generally. Over 30% of medical imports through Tehran's main airport are hormone-based medications, including insulin and cancer treatments, the report noted. Another 10% are vaccines and 6% blood products. U.S. offers up to $15 million for information on IRGC financial networks: The State Department's Rewards for Justice program a new appeal for information about Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps's (IRGC) alleged use of digital asset exchanges and other financial mechanisms to evade sanctions and access international financial systems. The reward offers up to $15 million for information leading to the disruption of the IRGC's financial mechanisms. Amnesty: Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity in 2022 protest crackdown: A new by Amnesty International has found that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during their suppression of the nationwide "Woman Life Freedom" uprising in 2022. The report, more than 1,000 pages long, details the use of "murder, torture, enforced disappearance, imprisonment, rape and persecution on political, gender, ethnic and religious grounds." It also identifies 87 officials it says should be criminally investigated for crimes against humanity. "[Iranian authorities] waged a widespread and systematic attack against a civilian population demanding dignity, human rights and fundamental political change, pursuant to a state policy of using lethal force to obliterate dissent," Agnes Callamard, Amnesty International's Secretary General, said in a statement. "This report is being published at a time when people in Iran are also facing the devastating consequences of unlawful attacks by the USA and Israel. Amnesty International unequivocally opposes violations of international law by all parties and rejects any attempt to instrumentalize the suffering of victims of human rights violations in Iran to justify unlawful attacks that inflict further civilian harm." Palestine Two women shot by Israeli forces in central Gaza: Two Palestinian women were by Israeli gunfire toward residential homes and tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps in Central Gaza on Friday, according to WAFA. Five children rescued from damaged home as Gaza government announces emergency plan for buildings at risk of collapse: Civil Defense crews rescued five children who became trapped on the second floor of their home after its staircase collapsed in the Sabra neighborhood, south of Gaza City. The families were evacuated and warned not to return to the house, which had been damaged by Israeli attacks and remains at risk of collapse. Two days ago, the collapse of another residential building in Gaza City killed 21 Palestinians, including 12 children and five women. The IDF to Drop Site on the collapse, saying "the IDF did not strike the building in question during the war." The building, however, showed visible cracks and signs of damage from Israel's assault on Gaza, which damaged 80% of structures across the Strip, including two-thirds that were destroyed, according to the UN. More than 2,000 damaged buildings across Gaza are at risk of collapse, according to Civil Defense. Gaza authorities and representatives from international, UN, and Arab organizations agreed Friday on an emergency plan to address hundreds of war-damaged buildings at risk of collapse across the Strip, according to Gaza's Government Media Office. The meeting called for the immediate entry of heavy machinery, specialized equipment, fuel, and oil, as well as the allocation of land for shelters for residents living in unsafe buildings. Israeli settler attacks injure at least six Palestinians across the occupied West Bank: Hebron: Armed Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli forces, Palestinian farmers trying to reach their land in Wadi Al-Shannar, east of Halhul, on Friday. The settlers assaulted and detained several farmers, according to WAFA. Ramallah: Five Palestinians were injured after Israeli settlers at their vehicle near the entrance to Yabroud, east of Ramallah, causing the vehicle to overturn. Jericho: A Palestinian was injured when Israeli settlers families in Khirbet Allan, north of Jericho in the Jordan Valley. The settlers attempted to steal sheep, attacked residents with stones, and damaged a Palestinian-owned vehicle. East Jerusalem: Israeli forces a Palestinian man outside Lions' Gate, one of the entrances to Al-Aqsa Mosque. Israel adds 2,167 units to E1 settlement plan, bringing total to 3,401: Israel added a tender for 2,167 housing units to its E1 settlement expansion plan in the occupied West Bank, Reuters reported, on top of 1,234 units announced in August. The E1 project would cut the occupied West Bank off from East Jerusalem and disrupt territorial contiguity between its northern and southern areas. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has said the plan would "bury" the idea of a Palestinian state. Bidding is scheduled to open October 25, two days before Israel's parliamentary election. " The whole case is related to her journalistic work": Palestinian-American journalist detained by Israel at Hasharon: Palestinian-American journalist and Drop Site contributor Naqaa Hamed is in Hasharon, a temporary detention facility in central Israel, and is expected to be transferred to Damon Prison, where most Palestinian female prisoners are held. Hamed's lawyer told Drop Site she was accused of incitement against Israeli settlers and the army, communicating with the enemy, and cooperating with the enemy during a military court session on Thursday. Her lawyer argued that Hamed was a professional journalist and her arrest came solely because of a campaign targeting her by Israeli settlers. He told Drop Site "the whole case is related to her journalistic work." The military court ruled to extend her detention by six days to complete their "investigation." Mahajneh submitted an appeal. The Committee to Protect Journalists condemned Hamed's detention, saying "Unsubstantiated espionage allegations must not be used to criminalize journalism, and the systemic harassment and intimidation targeting her work in the occupied West Bank must end." Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen called for her immediate release, saying in a on X, "Another American citizen wrongfully detained by the Israeli govt." Report: Israel kills one, wounds 15 on Thursday, total ceasefire violations reach 4,931: Israel committed 19 ceasefire violations in Gaza on Thursday, killing one Palestinian and wounding 15 others, bringing the total documented violations since the ceasefire took effect to 4,931, according to a shared by the Palestinian side with mediators and obtained by Drop Site News. Since the ceasefire took effect, 1,387 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks--including 297 children, 140 women, and 42 elderly people--and 4,784 wounded, nearly half of them children, women, or elderly. Only 35% of the agreed humanitarian and commercial aid has entered Gaza since the ceasefire began, according to the document, while overall movement of people through the crossing has reached just 39.1% of the agreed level. Qatar pledges 1.3 million liters of fuel for Gaza, enough for just 16 days of health sector needs: Qatar an agreement with the United Nations to provide Gaza with approximately 1.3 million liters of fuel, its Foreign Ministry announced on Thursday. The grant is intended to keep hospitals, medical centers, and other essential humanitarian infrastructure operating, amid severe shortages resulting from Israel's restrictions despite the nominal ceasefire. The World Health Organization estimates that Gaza's health sector needs about 80,000 liters daily. At that rate, Qatar's 1.3 million-liter grant would cover only about 16 days of healthcare operations. If shared with water, sanitation and other humanitarian services--as Qatar says it will be--it will last considerably less. The announcement provides no delivery schedule. Trump 's "Board of Peace" to brief countries at UN on stalled Gaza reconstruction and governance plans: The U.S.-controlled Board of Peace will representatives from dozens of countries, the EU, and UN agencies on September 23, during the UN General Assembly, on its stalled plans to rebuild and govern Gaza, The Times of Israel reported. The meeting will cover negotiations over Hamas's weapons and hear from the Palestinian technocratic committee (NCAG) about 71 projects for its first six months. None of the projects has a start date as the initiative remains frozen because Israel rejects the Board's plan to decommission the weapons of all armed factions, despite Hamas accepting its terms on July 30. Lebanon Two wounded as Israeli ceasefire violations continue in southern Lebanon: Bint Jbeil: Two people were in Israeli shelling in the Chaqra area on Friday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli artillery also targeted Wadi Nahle on the outskirts of Chaqra. Marjayoun: Israeli forces Deir Mimas and searched several homes. Israeli troops also six stun grenades around the position they had taken near the town's inner entrance, as the Lebanese army deployed reinforcements nearby. Tyre (Sour): Israeli artillery shelling the towns of Mansouri and Majdal Zoun on Friday morning, following intense shelling before and after midnight. U.S. News Early voting begins in midterm elections: In-person voting early voting for the midterm election began on Friday in a handful of states. More expansive early voting is scheduled to begin in the coming weeks. Earlier this week, the Supreme Court rejected President Donald Trump's bid to restrict mail ballots. One tenth of all Americans this year is a resident of a different congressional district than in 2024, according to a by Project Democracy, following an unprecedented flurry of redistricting in the House that has redrawn the congressional map. 46 Senate Democrats demand Pentagon accounting of Iran war costs: Forty-six members of the Senate Democratic caucus, by Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin , sent a letter demanding Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth provide a full breakdown by Sept. 30 of costs incurred in the Iran war and details on the administration's $67 billion supplemental funding request. The lawmakers accused the Pentagon of failing to provide "basic information," despite its requests for tens of billions in additional funding. The letter, signed by every Democratic caucus member except Sen. John Fetterman , comes a day after the Congressional Budget Office put the war's cost at $38 billion through its first five months and projected ongoing costs of $2 to 3 billion monthly. White House withdraws Lance Schroyer 's nomination to lead ICE: The White House its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma Highway Patrol major and ally of DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin , to lead Immigration and Customs Enforcement on Thursday, less than three months after President Donald Trump nominated him. The nomination's rescission surprised officials in the Department, according to several DHS insiders cited by the Washington Post. Schroyer faced mounting resistance in the Senate, where Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul had not scheduled a confirmation hearing, and border czar Tom Homan had suggested the role should go to someone "who knows the job." ICE has not had a Senate-confirmed director in over a decade. Trump administration weighs at least 12 data center projects on federal public lands: The Bureau of Land Management is proposals covering more than 17,600 acres across Arizona, Idaho, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, and Wyoming for data centers and related infrastructure, an unprecedented use of public land that local officials in several states told The Washington Sun they were unaware was under consideration. The largest proposal, a 10,200-acre project from nuclear startup Valar Atomics near Green River, Utah, would co-locate a data center with small nuclear reactors. Another case involves the Idaho-based firm Rhea Data, which has proposed a 4,000,000-square-foot data center near Boise powered partly by a new natural gas facility. Only one such project, on federal land in Nevada, has been approved so far. It remains on hold amid a legal challenge. Microsoft executive calls AI "largest theft of labor in human history": Microsoft's director of applied science called the training of large language models the "largest theft of labor in human history" and "an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions," the Washington Post, according to a document unsealed Thursday as part of a lawsuit filed by the New York Times against Microsoft and OpenAI. The unsealed legal brief quotes internal documents obtained via legal discovery. Separately, Anthropic yesterday in a blog post that its Claude chatbot "'leads' 26% of Anthropic's AI R&D work," and that "AI systems are increasingly being used to build the next version of themselves," The Post . Man who sprayed Rep. Ilhan Omar with vinegar sentenced to 14 months in prison: Anthony Kazmierczak , 56, was Thursday to 14 months in prison and three years of supervised release, during which he cannot make contact with Rep. Ilhan Omar, who he assaulted with a water-and-apple-cider-vinegar spray during a Minneapolis town hall in January. U.S. District Judge Joan Ericksen noted that the attack "wasn't a spur-of-the-moment act," given that Kazmierczak had secured tickets weeks in advance. He also texted acquaintances before the attack indicating he planned to "do something" involving Omar. Kazmierczak, who has Parkinson's disease and whose attorney argued that he had not taken his mental health medications prior to the attack, apologized to Omar in court on Thursday. Pentagon reinstates mandatory testosterone screening for male service members over 30 : The Pentagon updated guidance Thursday requiring mandatory testosterone deficiency screening for male active-duty and reserve service members over 30, after temporarily rescinding earlier guidance this month. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said in July the screening and testosterone replacement therapy initiative was an effort to keep troops "on the leading edge of lethality." The screening will reportedly assess military personnel for symptoms including erectile dysfunction, reduced sexual desire, and diminished physical performance, and will also document risk factors like obesity and diabetes. A corresponding clinical guideline for female service members remains under review, the director of the Defense Health Agency added. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Pakistan mosque bombing kills at least 16: A suicide car bomb a mosque inside a police headquarters in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, during Friday prayers, killing at least 16 people and injuring more than 56. After the bombing, gunmen then tried to enter the police complex and exchanged fire with officers. At least five police officers and 10 civilians were among those killed, and several of the wounded were reported in critical condition. No group immediately claimed responsibility. Both the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, and an ISIL affiliate are active in the region and regularly attack security forces. Spanish police clear migrants from Ceuta: Spanish riot police and military personnel began migrants from beaches in the North African enclave of Ceuta on Friday, using batons and firing rubber bullets into the air as crowds competed for limited places in temporary accommodation. Spain estimates about 10,000 migrants remain in the territory after more than 72,000 people crossed from Morocco during an unprecedented border rush at the end of July. Authorities have opened temporary housing in Ceuta's port for about 1,700 adult men, but aid groups say thousands remain homeless and sleeping on beaches and pavements. Russians vote in first parliamentary election since Ukraine invasion: Russians began Friday in a three-day parliamentary election that will determine the makeup of the 450-seat State Duma, with the ruling United Russia party expected to retain power. President Vladimir Putin has framed the vote as evidence of public backing for the military campaign in Ukraine, saying it would demonstrate that "millions of people stand behind our soldiers." Most explicitly anti-war candidates were excluded from the ballot, while the liberal Yabloko party was barred from competing nationally after Russia's Supreme Court ruled it had violated electoral rules, a decision the party disputes. Belarus continues military drills near NATO border: Belarus has tanks, artillery, and drone units for exercises in the Brest and Grodno regions bordering Poland and Lithuania, close to the Suwalki Gap--the roughly 40-mile corridor connecting the Baltic states to the rest of NATO. For several days, Belarusian forces are practicing counter-sabotage operations, dispersed command posts, artillery fire and drone warfare. Minsk says the exercises are defensive and rejects suggestions that they are preparations for an attack. The drills come amid heightened tension along NATO's eastern flank. Poland has recently scrambled aircraft during Russian strikes near its border, while an Italian NATO fighter shot down a suspected Russian explosive-laden drone that entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus on September 14. Chinese coast guard ship collides with Philippines government vessel near Palawan: The Philippines Coast Guard a Chinese coast guard vessel of deliberately ramming a Philippines government ship in the South China Sea on Friday during a mission to deliver fuel to Filipino fishermen. China disputed the account, saying the vessel ignored warnings, changed course and accelerated into the Chinese ship's path. The incident is the latest in a series of confrontations between Beijing and Manila in disputed waters, including recent water-cannon incidents near Scarborough Shoal. The Philippines rejects China's sweeping sovereignty claims in the South China Sea, while Beijing continues to assert jurisdiction over most of the waterway. Philippines school shooting leaves three dead in third deadly attack since June: At least three people, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman, were killed in a at a school in Banga, South Cotabato, in the southern Philippines. Eight students aged 14 to 17 were injured, four of them critically, according to local officials. The attack is the Philippines' third deadly school shooting since June. In August, a student in Zamboanga live streamed himself killing another student before taking his own life, while a June shooting at a public high school in Tacloban left three students dead and 20 injured. Washington insiders are positioning themselves to take over business inside Cuba: Trump- and Rubio-linked investors, lobbyists, and political allies are to Cuban assets as foreign companies are forced out amid Washington's maximum pressure campaign. Reporting from Ed Augustin and Lee Schlenker points to potential deals involving mining, hotels, shipping, and humanitarian aid, while foreign companies pushed out by U.S. sanctions leave openings for U.S.-linked investors and businesses. Washington continues to intensify sanctions aimed at forcing political change in Cuba, with Rubio a new wave of sanctions on Thursday targeting state-run enterprises, military enterprises and officials. Here's why that matters more than you know. | | | | Friend, Angie Nixon won the Florida Democratic Senate primary. She raised a fraction of what her opponent had. She was outspent 16 to 1. And she won anyway, by 12 points. That should stop every Republican in their tracks. Because here's what that result tells me: For the first time in history, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) has won a major-party nomination for statewide office. The DSA , the same movement that swept New York and is reshaping the Democrat Party from the inside, just planted their flag in Florida. And they did it without the money. Nixon's win caught many off guard. Now the party has a DSA-aligned Senate candidate on the ballot in one of the most watched races in the country. This is the moment I've been warning about all summer. The conventional wisdom in Washington has always been that socialism can't win in Florida. That the money would win. That the establishment would hold. Friend, I am not writing to you today to ask for a dollar. I am writing because what happened in Florida is a signal, and as Senate majority leader, I cannot ignore it. And neither can you. That is exactly what they are doing right now in Florida. And in Michigan. And in Maine. And in North Carolina. The money doesn't matter if we don't show up. That's why I am personally asking you to verify your 2026 Voter Profile right now. Not because it costs anything. Not because we need your donation. Because the only way Ashley Moody holds that seat in November is if every verified Republican in this country is counted, ready, and impossible to ignore. Angie Nixon proved that this fight is about people, not money. | Thank you for always showing up when it matters most. Senator John Thune | Paid for by the NRSC. Donate $50 or more and get a free copy of "Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas

Fellow Conservative: In 1991, the mob came for Clarence Thomas. They smeared him. They tried to destroy his name, his reputation, and his honor. As Justice Thomas himself has put it, critics in Washington _"don't bomb you, necessarily, but they bomb your reputation or your good name or your honor."_ **He refused to cave.** And because he did, he became one of the four giants of the modern Supreme Court — alongside Justices Scalia, Alito, and Rehnquist. Senator Ted Cruz has just released a remarkable new book: _**Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas**_ , built on exclusive interviews with the Justice himself.

---
|
---
[](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=53cf8a12c0a842e9886fe142791eb1e4&_e=kqID-qcgsks3VHi6T6idSIWCeoSSE3aKCkF-OEqgsSb5SpgcGKrB-CWRbnhhFW9QhbSCaU1NJFJ8UxAPrJ6oHb8KlEVcexlX2tFt_pALcdIajmv1UBI608ynVBsjJyBLwWE7NGX-P1ChcOkFYjaTSptLe-gQHmjJYAlbRvQjqFTy8Iy6KTxHKkwkPo6ORIYzsV6Wgl4018DVzqU5Z-6zu0fcmGy0faDEw-oZ6tOGJFC3GBoEln19Sq-kDeU5bf9A1x_TRONOgVB16CXfNuA3bhhNaCBv4HqXBDb_NbizZ0VtIBi6rBJN2gzHtonyhBnuWlRFSW6PWXeVjXcaTtd3YUIdardMu7hnfY9emtr4m8r7Zv0XGGPKAw0DBylnSZDs0-bHePdUsHtVXpzJqD2qXw%3D%3D)
---
|
---
It tells the story of a man who rose from grinding poverty in Pin Point, Georgia — raised by a grandfather he calls _"the single greatest human being I've ever met"_ — to become, in Cruz's words, the justice _"more willing to go back to the original Constitution... and to overturn precedent" than any other in history._

There's a moment in the book that says everything. When Justice Scalia told Thomas he was _"tilting at windmills"_ by trying to overturn bad precedent, Thomas shot back: _"Nino, windmills are dangerous."_

That is the kind of courage we need on the federal bench. And here is the part every conservative must understand:

**Clarence Thomas only reached the Supreme Court because the Senate confirmed him by just two votes.**

Presidents nominate judges. But the Senate confirms them. Every originalist on the bench, and every one we hope to see there, depends on having conservative senators willing to fight. When we lose the Senate, we lose the courts. It's that simple.

That's the mission of the Senate Conservatives Fund: electing principled conservatives to the U.S. Senate so we can confirm the next generation of Clarence Thomases, and stop the Left from ever again turning a confirmation hearing into a character assassination.

So today, we want to put Senator Cruz's book in your hands.

**When you contribute $50 or more to the Senate Conservatives Fund, we'll send you a copy of _Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas_ as our thank-you.** [**Please join us in the effort to build a conservative Senate by making a contribution today.**](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=53cf8a12c0a842e9886fe142791eb1e4&_e=kqID-qcgsks3VHi6T6idSIWCeoSSE3aKCkF-OEqgsSb5SpgcGKrB-CWRbnhhFW9QhbSCaU1NJFJ8UxAPrJ6oHb8KlEVcexlX2tFt_pALcdLGx1y-aIHI-nXNwB-NXS5Cqy7qrEfJPWXKCQnhSB-otAQ9_fRqTkxiuVedp2oSpIJkzlOsek1qWmsOeHKKMf8RIEuzk54-QDw13xD1HqUqXpId_yDzy7E0jnVvIBpeqb5wWIRmJ25WLqkT0scdmipfAwe-xsDUQw7KaH9MX3mjN4okwuymMpFlGnZEsfMgTa98ZwRyOXt4DkQth2wZIFzgWYsVF0lAqbNnSLGg7AV1GIX8XPp5q660WVXvlm5y55RXon__PQ_a_39sEj47vlWwy0SF5O89XYc43LBluW0pnw%3D%3D) Your support will help elect the conservative senators who will confirm judges like Justice Thomas — and will help make sure the next conservative nominee who refuses to bow to the woke mob has the votes to win. Clarence Thomas went further. Now it's our turn.

name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: All Around America: Come with us to the Okefenokee!
body:
Celebrate America’s incredible wilderness this summer
Celebrate America’s incredible wilderness this summer
| [](https://support.defenders.org/s/6035080/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
###
North America is home to some of the most incredible landscapes on Earth – and this summer, Defenders is taking you there! Join us as we celebrate the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States by bringing you to our most incredible wildlife refuges, national forests and more, including some in your own neck of the woods!
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
[](https://support.defenders.org/s/6035081/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Let’s go to the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge!_**
Stretching north from the border between Florida and Georgia, the Okefenokee is one of the largest and richest national wildlife refuges in the country! This refuge covers almost 400,000 acres of pine islands, cypress forests and blackwater wetlands, inhabited by all manner of wild creatures.
#
This incredible refuge was threatened by mining interests, until a land acquisition deal saved the Okefenokee and its wildlife. Today it’s a swamp like no other – it’s been nominated to become a UNESCO World Heritage Site in recognition of its unparalleled wild character, thriving biodiversity!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Meet the Okefenokee’s wildlife_**
A rich tapestry of wild animals can be found in the Okefenokee, including many threatened and endangered species. Wood storks and red-cockaded woodpeckers fly through its skies, while American alligators swim between the lily pads that dot its waters. The Okefenokee also hosts an incredible variety of amphibians – an indicator of a healthy ecosystem.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_What can I do there?_**
The Okefenokee has to be seen to be believed – and you’ll rarely find a better location for wildlife and nature photography! If you’re a birder, grab your binoculars and check out some incredibly rare birds on the wing that you might not see anywhere else. Canoeists and kayakers can explore its waters from a number of recreation areas. And everyone can visit one of several local guides and visitor centers to learn more about the Okefenokee and what makes this refuge an incredible American treasure!
#
|

| | |
---

# **RPVI Launches St. Croix and St. Thomas Radio Ads**
---
| |

Dear Friends,
For 30 years, one party has controlled the Virgin Islands Legislature. The result has been unaffordable WAPA bills, unsafe communities, struggling schools, a housing crisis and a government that too often escapes accountability.
The Republican Party in the Virgin Islands has launched two new radio ads presenting a different direction for our islands.
**On St. Croix, Raymond James is ready to lead the charge to reopen the refinery safely and responsibly.**
The refinery once supported some of St. Croix’s best-paying jobs and generated $25 million annually in tax revenue. Reopening it will require direct communication with the White House, federal agencies, Port Hamilton and potential investors. Raymond James is the best person to give St. Croix that voice and bring jobs, opportunity and revenue back to the island.
---

---

**On St. Thomas and St. John, Eric Tillett and Derrick Callwood are running to end one-party rule and restore accountability.**
They will work to fix WAPA, make our communities safer, and demand better from the government. When the next major storm reaches our shores, Tillett and Callwood will ensure the Virgin Islands has leaders who can pick up the phone—and make sure Washington answers.
---

body:
I taught high school for 20 years. You learn pretty quickly that a kid who hasn’t eaten isn’t going to get much out of third period.
#
Peter,
I taught high school for 20 years. You learn pretty quickly that a kid who hasn’t eaten isn’t going to get much out of third period.
That’s why making school breakfast and lunch free for every kid in Minnesota was one of the proudest things we did. No forms. No stigma. No child sitting through class hungry.
This month we crossed 450 million meals served. The program saves families about $1,000 a year for each student. That’s a lot of full kids — and a little more breathing room at home.
Every one of those meals is one less child worried about hunger and one more student ready to learn. As a teacher and a parent, I know what a difference that makes.
That’s the kind of leadership I want more of — people who will fight for good schools and make life a little easier for working families. It’s why I started Small Town PAC: to back people who understand what their communities actually need, and who will fight for change that shows up in people’s daily lives.
**[We’ve got a little over six weeks. These are tough races, and the other side is going to spend whatever it takes. Will you chip in $5 today to help elect that kind of leadership?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260918-1.cbFoMe&amount=5&refcode=em20260918-1105&t=2&akid=1105%2E34582%2EJmlKOs)**

## **Sandinista Jim Himes**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/59d9f2b1-f835-4090-a016-bba8b5402804?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

_In 1988 Harvard senior Jim Himes packed a notebook and flew to revolutionary Nicaragua. He returned with his honors thesis: The Sandinista Defense Committees and the Transformation of Political Culture in Nicaragua. Thirty-five years later Congressman Jim Himes voted NO when the House was asked to denounce the horrors of socialism._
_Socialism does not fail because it is poorly staffed. It fails because it requires a concentration of power that, sooner or later, treats the neighbor as an informant and the citizen as a problem to be managed._
**The Thesis**
Harvard's catalog lists the paper as a 1988 A.B. honors thesis by James Andrew Himes. He spent two months in Nicaragua studying the Comites de Defensa Sandinista -- the CDS -- block committees built by the Sandinista Front after it took power in 1979.
The Front had promised political pluralism, a mixed economy, and non-alignment. After Somoza fell, the moderates were pushed aside. The Sandinistas kept the army and the police. The CDS filled the neighborhoods. On paper they ran literacy drives and food distribution. In practice they watched the block. Neighbors were rewarded for reporting neighbors. Many of Himes' interview subjects asked to remain anonymous. Why anonymous? It is how people talk when their neighbors can punish them.
Read the thesis, [Part 1 (PDF)](https://substack.com/redirect/0e4609cc-3a5b-4a92-bb44-151bdc9bebb3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) * [Part 2 (PDF)](https://substack.com/redirect/cbe49e21-d14c-4457-8c25-e7a4fcff0be6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**What Happened Next**
Daniel Ortega led the Sandinistas then. He leads Nicaragua now. In March 2022, Alma Guillermo Prieto wrote in _The New Yorker_ that Ortega and Rosario Murillo had crushed civil society and jailed their former comrades. The title was "The Revolution Eats Itself in Nicaragua."
Hundreds of thousands of Nicaraguans have left. Recent counts put about 13 percent of the population living abroad; the outflow sped up after the 2018 crackdown. Nicaraguans who reached the United States often still will not speak on the record. They have relatives at home. Independent surveys in the Ortega years find that most people feel watched in their own streets. The heirs of the CDS still run that system.
The pattern is clear. Socialism promises equality while delivering a monopoly of force. Once the party owns the army, the police, the food line, and the neighborhood list, opposition disappears.
**The Vote**
On February 2, 2023, the House considered H. Con. Res. 9, "Denouncing the horrors of socialism." It said socialist ideology "necessitates a concentration of power that has time and time again collapsed into Communist regimes, totalitarian rule, and brutal dictatorships." It named the dictators, including Lenin, Stalin, Mao, Pol Pot, Castro, the Kims, Daniel Ortega, Hugo Chavez, and Nicolas Maduro. It named the crimes that have driven so many Latinos to the United States, and the death toll; more than 100 million. It resolved that Congress denounces socialism in all its forms and opposes socialist policies in the United States.
The resolution passed 328-86, with 14 members voting present. Every Republican who voted, voted yes. A majority of voting Democrats joined them. **Jim Himes voted Nay. He declined to state that the system which produced Ortega, Castro, and Maduro is a horror.**
**Celebrated by Communists and Socialists**
When Himes beat Republican Chris Shays in 2008, the **Communist Party USA** 's paper did not treat it as a loss. _People 's Weekly World_ reported on the Party's New Haven anniversary gathering that December: "Folks pounded the pavement in Bridgeport, Conn., to defeat the last standing congressional Republican, Chris Shays. His replacement, newly elected **Jim Himes, is vowing to take the people 's agenda forward**." That is their sentence, not his. **Connecticut 's Working Families Party** put him on a fusion line. The socialist **Council for a Livable World** contributed to the race. While not proving secret party membership, it does show that the organized left saw Himes as a man it could live with.
**Why It Matters Here**
"Democratic socialism" is not Nordic socialism. Nordic social democracy is a market economy with a large welfare state, sitting on the cultural capital of high-trust, high-work societies. Classical socialism is something else: public ownership of the commanding heights, political monopoly justified as class justice, and the systematic weakening of the private associations that stand between the citizen and the party. It is how the plan is enforced. You can only plan a society if you can see the building blocks of society -- the people. You can only see those blocks if someone is reporting on those blocks.
Fairfield County is not Managua. It is one of the most successful capitalist landscapes on earth -- property rights, open trade, and the rule that a family's house is not the party's business. Himes does not have to nationalize a bank to do damage. He only has to keep protecting socialism.
That 1988 Harvard student gets credit for actually going to see a revolution instead of only talking about one. The congressman has had four decades to watch Ortega jail old comrades and empty the country. He has had Nicaraguans living among us who will not use their names. He had a resolution that asked only for moral clarity. He voted no. Ideas travel farther than armies. The least a member of Congress can do is vote as if he noticed.
Dr. Michael Goldstein is running against Sandinista Jim. He is a strong Republican who understands the danger of socialism and its inevitable slide into communism. That is why he is committed to preserving the freedom and liberty promised in the U.S. Constitution and Bill of Rights.
Connecticut is worth fighting for. America is worth fighting for. Support Republican candidates.

**Editor’s Note:** Make time for this today – Porter’s [explosive new documentary](https://track.mail.easyinvestbase.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinked.easyinvestbase.com%2F6a183375410969846edf7ed2%3Flid=mnqipk5n4sz1%26email=dpwillis67@gmail.com%26domain=629ESE%26type=B%26product=PCTN19/1/010001a0b525b67f-80b4abe1-aa93-42c0-95de-3b66be7a3c0c-000000/A_eI7DAFRGYU1sCXes2HrDm3N-UtqDinfPWhaOouaj8=452) exposes the President’s plans to replace the U.S. dollar. If you have retirement savings, a stock portfolio, or a family depending on you financially, [you need to watch it right now.](https://track.mail.easyinvestbase.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinked.easyinvestbase.com%2F6a183375410969846edf7ed2%3Flid=g7knqab8lxv1%26email=dpwillis67@gmail.com%26domain=629ESE%26type=B%26product=PCTN19/1/010001a0b525b67f-80b4abe1-aa93-42c0-95de-3b66be7a3c0c-000000/0WTZv2ILOsjVFvtg3EhBwD6U99s5b5d7RYFvXEratUE=452)

—

In the early 19th century, whale oil was among the most valuable commodities on Earth.

It lit the lamps of America. It lubricated the machines of the Industrial Revolution. Entire coastal economies like New Bedford, Nantucket, and New London thrived because of it.

The scarcity was real. Whales were finite after all – and the expertise to hunt them, process them, and bring the oil to market took decades to develop.

That scarcity underpinned an entire monetary ecosystem.

Then in 1859, Edwin Drake struck oil in Titusville, Pennsylvania.

Kerosene arrived. It was cheaper, more abundant, and much more powerful.

The whalers didn't disappear overnight. The compression was gradual – and then suddenly catastrophic. Within two decades, the whaling industry had effectively collapsed.

The scarcity hadn't disappeared. It had migrated. And the fortunes built on whale oil migrated with it – to the men who understood where scarcity had moved.

This is what a great repricing looks like.

A friend of mine, financial writer Garrett Baldwin, has a phrase for what happens to the people who don't move in time. He calls it the "flooding layer."

The idea is simple – every time the scarcity underpinning an entire industry evaporates, it creates two groups of people:

Those who own the new chokepoint. And those standing in the flooding layer – watching everything they built get washed away.

The brutal truth is that the people in the flooding layer almost never see it coming. Not until the compression is irreversible.

For a more recent example, let’s look at Kodak.

In 1988, Eastman Kodak employed nearly 150,000 people.

It was one of the most valuable companies in America. Its business was built on a form of scarcity that seemed unassailable – the chemistry, the film, the paper, the processing infrastructure required to capture and develop a photograph.

That scarcity evaporated when the smartphone put a camera in every pocket.

Kodak didn't fail because folks stopped taking pictures – it failed because the scarcity that underpinned its entire business model migrated.

In 2012, Kodak filed for bankruptcy.

That same year, Facebook acquired Instagram – a company with 13 employees – for $1 billion. Instagram had captured the value that Kodak lost.

The scarcity had migrated from chemistry to connectivity and the people who understood that got very rich. Those left standing in Kodak's flood plain did not.

Today I’d like to show you that we’re living through [another great repricing](https://track.mail.easyinvestbase.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Flinked.easyinvestbase.com%2F6a183375410969846edf7ed2%3Flid=6np8ep5nwadl%26email=dpwillis67@gmail.com%26domain=629ESE%26type=B%26product=PCTN19/1/010001a0b525b67f-80b4abe1-aa93-42c0-95de-3b66be7a3c0c-000000/Tk0qPI5Slk7rgzXw06iXAULTjtt0bOFWKwxFlvTpXiM=452) – one that is already making millions of dollars for those who understand where the scarcity is migrating once again.

To understand what’s unfolding we have to rewind to a secret deal that’s profoundly shaped everything about our lives, for more than half a century.
**Kissinger’s Dollar Reset**
In July 1974, Treasury Secretary William Simon boarded a secret flight to Saudi Arabia.

Under the orders of Nixon’s top national-security advisor Henry Kissinger, what he proposed to King Faisal in the coastal city of Jeddah would become the greatest financial arrangement in the history of the world.

Saudi Arabia would price its oil in dollars.

Within a year, every other OPEC nation followed suit. The U.S. dollar was now backstopped by the one commodity the entire modern world could not function without.

That scarcity minted fortunes on an almost unimaginable scale – creating an environment that allowed America to spend trillions, with the rest of the world picking up the tab.

On Wednesday night in Gastonia, the President of the United States, Donald Trump, actually told the people of North Carolina that their home is "one of the worst [states] in the whole nation." A sitting president, standing in our state, asking for votes while insulting our home.
I've spent my career serving this state, as Attorney General, and as Governor. For those of you who live here or visit frequently, you know he's wrong. He's wrong about **who we are**.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/abaa8d93-3c5f-4a0d-a3b7-f6d03a9858de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
North Carolina's story isn't one of decline. It's one of firsts.
We opened the doors to the first public university in the nation. The people of our Outer Banks helped propel the first flight in human history. We've led the country in critical research and innovation, especially with the groundbreaking public-private Research Triangle Park. North Carolina's early childhood education program Smart Start has been emulated across the county.
I believe that the spirit of North Carolina is perfectly described in our state toast -- a unique tradition to our state. If you grew up here, you likely learned the words as a child. And if you moved here, you might have heard it recited and been curious about it.
The first verse reads:
> "Here's to the land of the long leaf pine,
> The summer land where the sun doth shine,
> Where the weak grow strong and the strong grow great,
> Here's to 'Down Home,' the Old North State!"
One line has always stuck with me: "where the weak grow strong and the strong grow great."
**That is the spirit of North Carolina.**
It never ceases to amaze me that this line of poetry written about our state more than a hundred years ago could just as easily have been written yesterday.
It's that very line that reminds us we can and we will continue to do better. It drove me toward my work in public service and it's how I got to wake up every morning for eight years getting the chance to lead the state I love so much.
When I left the Governor's office in January, the first thing I did was take off my tie and exchange my dress shoes for Jordan (let's not forget the basketball GOAT is a North Carolinian). I spent time back on the family farm, caught up on some reading and movies and enjoyed being with my family.
But in the months after, I watched how the people of our state were being treated by politicians in Washington DC. What I saw was unacceptable.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/abaa8d93-3c5f-4a0d-a3b7-f6d03a9858de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I told my children that my parents left me a better country but we have work to do to leave them a better country. I couldn't sit back and watch so many people in my state get left behind this way.
And I can't sit back today after the President took the stage in Gastonia and used his rally to spew lies about North Carolina.
So let's set the record straight because his claims do not survive basic fact-checking. No, we are not "one of the most violent and one of the worst [states] in the nation." No, we haven't lost our beauty. And, last time I checked, we were still as American "as apple pie."
Among all these lies though is one critical truth: President Trump wouldn't be coming to North Carolina if the Republicans didn't think they had a real shot at keeping this Senate seat. But if he thinks he can get away with disparaging North Carolina and its hardworking families, all while promoting policies in Washington that continue to hurt them, he's sorely mistaken.
The North Carolina state motto is "Esse Quam Vederi" which is Latin for "To be rather than to seem." We North Carolinians are authentic. We are who we say we are. And there's one thing we know: North Carolina is not the worst. In fact, it's the best.
I'm running for this Senate seat because I love this state, and I have hope for a better future.
We are a state where the weak grow strong and the strong grow great. It's been true for over a hundred years, it's true today, and if we work hard, it will be true tomorrow.

#### _**[Endless Urgency exists because paying attention isn't enough. The point of this work is to understand what's happening, refuse to look away when it gets scary, and turn that fear into something useful. We keep this work free for everyone because everyone deserves to be informed, prepared, and ready to act. * * *
I woke up this morning the way I wake up too many mornings: reaching for my phone before my feet hit the floor, bracing for whatever fresh horror the country cooked up overnight. Instead I got a barrage of polling **updates** so good it made me suspicious.
Angie Nixon tied in Florida. Democrats leading in Kansas **and** Idaho. Places that have no business being competitive are competitive. And you can tell it's real because of how the other side is behaving -- Republicans are dumping **massive amounts of** money into races they should be able to sleep through, and they're putting the Vice President of the United States on a plane to go beg for votes in states they won by twenty.
It is an absolute mess over there, and I am delighted. **Call it schadenfreude if you want. I 've earned a little.** **Because this** is **precisely** what the natural consequences of unprecedented corruption look like. A year and a half of Donald Trump back in office, a year and a half of wrecking things faster than anyone can catalog them, and the bill is finally coming due. Watching them panic is the closest thing to joy I've felt in months.
And still. Sitting behind all of that, in the back of my skull where it always sits, is the fear. **I'm delighted. And I am** _**terrified**_**.**
Because we've been here before. We've had the good polls. We've felt the energy, the enthusiasm, the sense that the country was finally turning toward something decent -- toward a nation that works for working people and leads with empathy and intelligence instead of whatever stupidity falls out of the Republican Party on any given Tuesday. We've felt all of that, and we've had our hearts broken anyway.
So I don't trust it. I refuse to believe certain races are actually competitive. I struggle most days to believe James Talarico is going to win in Texas. **Maybe that 's what political scar tissue looks like after you've worked in this field for two decades. You stop knowing how to experience hope without waiting for the other shoe to drop.**
**But maybe I don 't need to believe any of it yet. Maybe belief isn't the job. The work is the job.**
But here's the thing about that fear: **fear is energy, and energy demands movement. Our instinct is to run from it, but fear doesn 't disappear when we turn away. It stays inside us. It festers. It turns to poison.** Fear that you sit with for eight hours, thumb scrolling, jaw tight, learning nothing and doing nothing -- that fear eats you and produces exactly zero votes. **But convert that fear into** _**motion**_**and it becomes an edge.** Knock on a door. Call a friend. Give twenty bucks to somebody you actually believe in. **Volunteer. Organize. Learn something that makes you useful.**
Do that and the fear becomes fuel instead of a disease. **You don't have to become fearless. You have to become dangerous to the thing you're afraid of.**
* * *
#### **[That's why I built Endless Urgency. Not to give you one more thing to be afraid of, but to make sure fear doesn't become paralysis. We pay attention. We connect the dots. We prepare for what's coming. And then we do something with what we know. If that kind of work matters to you, become a paid subscriber and help us keep it free for everyone.](https://substack.com/redirect/521967b3-cdf0-4fee-b4b4-9ee1c6efcf00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
**So I 'll tell you what I did with my fear this morning:** I spent thirty minutes this morning with my staff putting together an election integrity event here in Chicago for the beginning of October, with a stack of partner organizations and some genuinely brilliant people who know this stuff cold. The agenda is the ugly hypotheticals nobody wants to say out loud: What happens if Trump sends ICE agents to polling locations? What happens if they truly screw with mail-in ballots? What happens if the FBI shows up to take ballots away because he doesn't like how the count is going?
Those are the scary things. **Good. They should scare us.** And the answer to scary things is not to whisper about them -- it's to get people in a room, get them informed, and get them ready. **You learn. You organize. You prepare. That 's what useful fear looks like.**
**And if the polls are even half right, we 're going to need that preparation. Because desperation doesn't make these people less dangerous. It makes them more dangerous.** Republicans are going to get more desperate, not less. You can smell it on them. Last week Donald Trump tried to straight-up bribe the American people: five thousand dollars, a "dividend," if Republicans win back the House. I have been doing this for twenty years and I have never seen polling where Americans overwhelmingly rejected free money. That's not a policy failure, that's a character verdict. It made him look weak and stupid and craven, even by his standards.
Meanwhile the Vice President of the United States -- God's perfect idiot -- is out there explaining that you've just got to give these guys two more years. It's so hard to fix the Biden economy, they say. Funny. In 2024 they said everything would get cheaper on day one. They said they wouldn't be launching illegal foreign wars like every other Republican president. They were going to be different. And now it's two more years and everything will be sunshine and farts.
How many times are these people going to lie before they finally get punished for it? **Here 's the good part: that's the part we control. Not the polls. Not Trump's behavior. Not whatever Republicans try next. The consequences.**
That's what November is. **That 's where all of this fear finally gets somewhere to go.** Is the Democratic Party perfect? God, no. But it is the last organized group of people in this country still trying to make it better. If you want real accountability, if you want to end this war, if you want to end these tariffs, if you want to end the rampant corruption metastasizing through Washington, there is one lever and you know what it is. Vote Democratic, and fight like hell to protect your right to do it. **And don 't you dare convince yourself the work is finished because a poll made you feel good.**
I'm hardly the first person to say this, but if your vote didn't matter, they wouldn't work this hard to take it from you.
They are running scared. Ignore the bluster. Ignore the attacks. Ignore the fear-mongering, which is the only product they have left to sell. Be ready for what's coming and keep your head on a swivel. **Because** **favorable polls aren 't permission to relax. They're an invitation to double down and push harder.** Make the calls. Send the texts. Give what you can. Talk to your neighbors.
Especially the ones who got caught up in MAGA. There are more people than ever quietly ready to admit that Trump failed them, and the single dumbest thing you can do right now is tell them you told them so. Give them an on-ramp. Let them be part of the solution instead of making them defend the worst decision of their life. If they're your friends, your family, the guy three doors down -- give them the opportunity. They deserve that.
That's what I'm doing today. I hope it's what you do too.
With urgency,
--Mike

A Personal Message from Senator John Thune
Friend,
There is one race on the national map that will determine who holds power in Washington. Right now, this critical race is sitting at a dead-heat coin flip. If it slides the wrong way, an extreme radical candidate will take power in the United States Senate--and our conservative majority will be lost.
| [I’m reaching out to you personally because we cannot afford to fly blind in the critical weeks ahead. I need our most dedicated and dialed-in supporters to see what we are up against and give us direction immediately.](https://links.rogersforsenate.com/u/click?_t=293de5a6223e4436ab53fb8020578890&_m=74418ef4b9284601b45060c6d289bf7b&_e=6E_gsENWjIJjyrHvdQ3CkinzklsmoGoMOOb_GcoUlwFCN59XmOKv6ULNulgOF2i48jhgCn42kGGBn1ZdOWZnMF4tW0rUcXardcfhF6aPDpjHvG5WUhvKQarVo7nnVWE9VIJYSuWLkJggIuV-p_E5p5Vv3PZzj5sS_MNM0ra4QgKUQE5zCdwtc9QjrGK9k7yTNDmN_GkHP2M_O8-1paTsJ67VDOafLplRlvIhuNVWE4Ob2IQ6U5mJ422GrU9LwJr66464aCN42KeFUufclKZb-xQlboqeD-xN8u_WiXGJwRXe_kF83MHZOofWnjPDRXrO5Ya8v-VkzXi76YwlKzQ70lcIvSloakFuPrgocPSw-C3oDcP8FaC1INUNBzB36yXNNKmG4XdJUDdhbveXWethEmP1K2VT7mHw_7pdTF-9PSIzjQqyfVs4zW1Y3uzzexLmXWi9pxTK-3BlpJFLjYWhhgdzmTx6p94F8szbDEXldFnKAIzuLyfByJUf1j_sqY8346Mn1JTy5PSDh_r6Sm31U-PEmxMxVSZF08qg0Bfv3ecB8w9tE30cToNSIj1Qy0z5VmPwJcPTHQzQO4mGaVyNg5Sa6vUH177bt5ESwONUkz6MMWjRPt01VvjpuSplDnkKCMBkX0HGX5ELXsazSQ5v-830PVObD1nvRr26QFSmZKMC18uQcFnv31tR7B1ug3VkMjNbrfR75fs1oUZDscK1UxEF7gTxwAyowSXL_t8SSNKC-3SALzEfYIbmgzgHOl9O)

body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
| Friends,
The midterms are no longer a distant calendar date. Early ballots go in the mail September 28. In-person early voting begins October 5. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3.
Between now and then, this newsletter has one job: give you the Republican candidates, a plan to vote, and a clear-eyed look at how this race is being run against us. Because it is being run against us, and not in the way you might expect.
Nebraska is on the board
On Thursday, September 17, U.S. Senator John Kennedy (R-LA) said he was heading to Iowa, Nebraska, and Kansas to campaign for Republican Senate candidates. He said he never expected to spend time in states he once treated as "fat guy layups." He now says those races are close.
Take him at his word. Nebraska is being treated as contestable, and every trick is on the table. Here are three you should recognize on sight.
Trick one: the cleared lane
Democrats had a nominee against Senator Pete Ricketts. That nominee stepped aside, and the party did not put another Democrat on the ballot. That cleared a lane for Democrat-supported independent Dan Osborn. Do not treat it as an accident. It is a strategy: run a candidate without the label so voters who would never pull the lever for a Democrat might pull it for him.
Trick two: the demoralizing poll
Do not take Democrat and Democrat-leaning polls at face value. Many are designed to convince Republicans the race is already lost so they stay home. Look at them with a skeptical eye, then go vote anyway.
Trick three: the fake conservative party
Do not be taken in by Nebraska's new "America First Party." The website looks conservative. The party was founded and is chaired by John Cartier, a far-left Lincoln attorney. The wrapping is meant to peel Republican votes away from actual Republican candidates. The wrapping covers a stinky fish.
Notice the pattern. None of these tricks work by persuading you. They work by confusing you, discouraging you, or splitting your vote. Which means the counter is simple: know the candidates, make a plan, and bring the people around you with you.
Step one: know the candidates
Start at [vote.ne.gop](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_psxKJhyIO-0_4Eh0omMyEmy9A9qhAbiERxdvpbTf8C8uYPkFYPfpznoKAHWoEgfec-E3BAXM3QArXAYwg2PUJeA1spSlP863_vcdfdFEdSl1cYNX3PPtaUWsd_X2BgwpyBSFt2H9uLOlgAD4uBakA==&c=uraBZjntO-q_r0z2H76EOy8M_DxvF1KCyOABEIgwDkxHl52bu7VICw==&ch=Ppo8A7_s2Qa9vVIeqad3BEvpmphdctfZjSRE_UzRxV3eG76mXD19vw==). It is the NEGOP's one-stop shop for Republican state ballot candidates, plus voter registration and polling-place information. Many county parties also list local Republicans on their websites and Facebook pages, and some mail slate cards to homes. Use all of it.
Step two: reach the people you already know
Scott Petersen, our Republican nominee for Secretary of State, spent years building VoterTree, a simple get-out-the-vote tool for family, friends, and neighbors. It is not specific to his campaign. Anyone can use it. Try it at [PetersenforNebraska.com](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_psxKJhyIO-0_4Eh0omMyEmy9A9qhAbiERxdvpbTf8C8uYPkFYPfpwKUQqQ5q9MlXbVj3nKGJgEnLnOIZZZ2dhsrvgbqZF6RD6EERTI6gw9HDvdoxOA-TsqNll0AraYeWYZIYrqjln9wVDP9noNPatS0T-hXAAYE&c=uraBZjntO-q_r0z2H76EOy8M_DxvF1KCyOABEIgwDkxHl52bu7VICw==&ch=Ppo8A7_s2Qa9vVIeqad3BEvpmphdctfZjSRE_UzRxV3eG76mXD19vw==).
You build your own tree, match contacts to publicly available voter-registration information, and track outreach, voting plans, and follow-up. You can invite others to start trees of their own. It works online or with a printable worksheet.
Privacy is built in. You are not asked for phone numbers or emails for your contacts. Nothing in your tree is shared with candidates or committees. Each person manages a private tree. Details are in VoterTree's Privacy & Your Data policy.
Step three: bring in the people who have been left behind
The cleared-lane strategy only works if moderate Democrats go along with it. Many will not. At the RNC Midterm Convention, Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave an informative and compelling speech on why he left the Democrat Party, or more accurately, how the Democrat Party left him. Nebraska has many moderate Democrats who reject their party's far-left turn. Listen, then share it with one of them: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tKMe6FrLEhE](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_psxKJhyIO-0_4Eh0omMyEmy9A9qhAbiERxdvpbTf8C8uYPkFYPfpwKUQqQ5q9MlNmZ45jLqm267oQI3LVC-fEPVSnn7OyINjlzMlJhSr5GX5eCymbLYF8Fk8x-ciD_nLIsqzTgbvjP76XUy4wVormYbwEVL8eNPZ-x7NPOmanpBm4vMsP6nFg==&c=uraBZjntO-q_r0z2H76EOy8M_DxvF1KCyOABEIgwDkxHl52bu7VICw==&ch=Ppo8A7_s2Qa9vVIeqad3BEvpmphdctfZjSRE_UzRxV3eG76mXD19vw==)
Why it goes all the way down the ballot...
It is easier to keep the far left out of office than to remove them once they are in. That is true at the top of the ticket, and it is just as true at the bottom.
Take the University of Nebraska Board of Regents. Dr. Jeremy Hosein, a Lincoln neurosurgeon, has the intellect, experience, heart for service, and integrity the university system needs. His opponent is a political operative whose business is consulting for Democrat candidates. There is no comparison. Dr. Hosein needs your support and your vote. Don't give his opponent a foothold in office.
Or take Lancaster County. State Auditor Mike Foley found nearly $1 billion in accounting "mistakes" in the Lancaster County Treasurer's office, including about $1.27 million owed to the state and property-tax relief money sent to local taxing authorities instead of where it belonged - the taxpayer. The Treasurer and former Deputy Treasurer are on your ballot. Offices like this are hard to take back once they are lost. Vote accordingly.
To people of faith
Jesus said, "Behold, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves, so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves." (Matthew 10:16) That is exactly what this season asks of us: to see the tricks for what they are, and to answer them without becoming what we oppose.
Paul wrote, "Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it." (1 Corinthians 12:27) Victory belongs to Jesus alone. "The government shall be upon His shoulders." (Isaiah 9:6) But we are still called to be His hands and feet, and to resist the snares of the Enemy. Voting is one way we do that.
The plan
Make a plan. Use [vote.ne.gop](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_psxKJhyIO-0_4Eh0omMyEmy9A9qhAbiERxdvpbTf8C8uYPkFYPfpznoKAHWoEgfec-E3BAXM3QArXAYwg2PUJeA1spSlP863_vcdfdFEdSl1cYNX3PPtaUWsd_X2BgwpyBSFt2H9uKZLqzij6ND5Q==&c=uraBZjntO-q_r0z2H76EOy8M_DxvF1KCyOABEIgwDkxHl52bu7VICw==&ch=Ppo8A7_s2Qa9vVIeqad3BEvpmphdctfZjSRE_UzRxV3eG76mXD19vw==). Build a VoterTree. Talk to the people who trust you. Then vote, all the way down the ballot. Defend the Good Life! Keep Nebraska RED!
Onward to November. Together We Win!
In Liberty and in Truth,

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair | Friends, The midterms are no longer a distant calendar date. Early ballots go in the mail September 28. In-person early voting begins October 5. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Between now and then, this newsletter has one job: give you the Republican candidates, a plan to vote, and a clear-eyed look at how this race is being run against us. Because it is being run against us, and not in the way you might expect. Nebraska is on the board On Thursday, September 17, U.S. Senator John Kennedy (R-LA) said he was heading to Iowa, Nebraska, and Kansas to campaign for Republican Senate candidates. He said he never expected to spend time in states he once treated as "fat guy layups." He now says those races are close. Take him at his word. Nebraska is being treated as contestable, and every trick is on the table. Here are three you should recognize on sight. Trick one: the cleared lane Democrats had a nominee against Senator Pete Ricketts. That nominee stepped aside, and the party did not put another Democrat on the ballot. That cleared a lane for Democrat-supported independent Dan Osborn. Do not treat it as an accident. It is a strategy: run a candidate without the label so voters who would never pull the lever for a Democrat might pull it for him. Trick two: the demoralizing poll Do not take Democrat and Democrat-leaning polls at face value. Many are designed to convince Republicans the race is already lost so they stay home. Look at them with a skeptical eye, then go vote anyway. Trick three: the fake conservative party Do not be taken in by Nebraska's new "America First Party." The website looks conservative. The party was founded and is chaired by John Cartier, a far-left Lincoln attorney. The wrapping is meant to peel Republican votes away from actual Republican candidates. The wrapping covers a stinky fish. Notice the pattern. None of these tricks work by persuading you. They work by confusing you, discouraging you, or splitting your vote. Which means the counter is simple: know the candidates, make a plan, and bring the people around you with you. Step one: know the candidates Start at ==. It is the NEGOP's one-stop shop for Republican state ballot candidates, plus voter registration and polling-place information. Many county parties also list local Republicans on their websites and Facebook pages, and some mail slate cards to homes. Use all of it. Step two: reach the people you already know Scott Petersen, our Republican nominee for Secretary of State, spent years building VoterTree, a simple get-out-the-vote tool for family, friends, and neighbors. It is not specific to his campaign. Anyone can use it. Try it at ==. You build your own tree, match contacts to publicly available voter-registration information, and track outreach, voting plans, and follow-up. You can invite others to start trees of their own. It works online or with a printable worksheet. Privacy is built in. You are not asked for phone numbers or emails for your contacts. Nothing in your tree is shared with candidates or committees. Each person manages a private tree. Details are in VoterTree's Privacy & Your Data policy. Step three: bring in the people who have been left behind The cleared-lane strategy only works if moderate Democrats go along with it. Many will not. At the RNC Midterm Convention, Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave an informative and compelling speech on why he left the Democrat Party, or more accurately, how the Democrat Party left him. Nebraska has many moderate Democrats who reject their party's far-left turn. Listen, then share it with one of them: == Why it goes all the way down the ballot... It is easier to keep the far left out of office than to remove them once they are in. That is true at the top of the ticket, and it is just as true at the bottom. Take the University of Nebraska Board of Regents. Dr. Jeremy Hosein, a Lincoln neurosurgeon, has the intellect, experience, heart for service, and integrity the university system needs. His opponent is a political operative whose business is consulting for Democrat candidates. There is no comparison. Dr. Hosein needs your support and your vote. Don't give his opponent a foothold in office. Or take Lancaster County. State Auditor Mike Foley found nearly $1 billion in accounting "mistakes" in the Lancaster County Treasurer's office, including about $1.27 million owed to the state and property-tax relief money sent to local taxing authorities instead of where it belonged - the taxpayer. The Treasurer and former Deputy Treasurer are on your ballot. Offices like this are hard to take back once they are lost. Vote accordingly. To people of faith Jesus said, "Behold, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves, so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves." (Matthew 10:16) That is exactly what this season asks of us: to see the tricks for what they are, and to answer them without becoming what we oppose. Paul wrote, "Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it." (1 Corinthians 12:27) Victory belongs to Jesus alone. "The government shall be upon His shoulders." (Isaiah 9:6) But we are still called to be His hands and feet, and to resist the snares of the Enemy. Voting is one way we do that. The plan Make a plan. Use ==. Build a VoterTree. Talk to the people who trust you. Then vote, all the way down the ballot. Defend the Good Life! Keep Nebraska RED! Onward to November. Together We Win! __The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports.__

You name it, they are on the wrong side of it.
