subject: 9 years because of THIS?
body:
You’ve heard about Erik on the news. He’s the NYPD Sergeant who
threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer.

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6136240/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvckVzUEY1SnpRRA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MTg/LbmNsR0xkU0FwcA/qP2hpZHM9bmNRb0xTS05OaVlNOGVsc10/gaq1lIA/s8l846cecef

Dear Friend,

I know you and I have never met. But I’m writing to you today
because I’m desperate.

I NEED YOUR HELP TO STOP NEW YORK ATTORNEY GENERAL LETITIA JAMES
BEFORE SHE TEARS MY FAMILY APART AND LOCKS MY POLICE OFFICER HUSBAND
UP FOR THE NEXT NINE YEARS FOR DOING HIS JOB.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

This is Erik, me, and our three children in the family photo.

I wish I didn’t have to blur our faces. But with the death threats
we’ve been getting, I couldn’t afford to take any chances.

I should explain...

You’ve heard about Erik on the news.

He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer
who was speeding a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk.

[Image showing people, coat, and jacket]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the
Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”

After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer --
a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow
officers moved in.

The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a
crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.

When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight
toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.

Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be
seriously injured -- maybe even killed.

So my husband made a split-second decision.

He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and
threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too
late.

Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two
fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit.

But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his
injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible
that someone died.

But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers
safe.

And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that
this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his
own.

He was the one who joined a violent street gang...

He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...

He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top
speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...

But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general.

YOU SEE, LETITIA JAMES IS BANKROLLED BY GEORGE SOROS. AND SHE’S
FILLED HER OFFICE WITH PROSECUTORS WHO HATE COPS AS MUCH AS SHE DOES.

And five months after that fateful day...

...she charged Erik with Manslaughter.

She didn’t just charge Erik.

She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case
into a media circus.

They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and
calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant
parents.

What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug
dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle?

Things only got worse at the trial.

But not only did the judge find Erik guilty...

...he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.

The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a
“general deterrent” to other police officers!

This is the upside-down world we live in now.

A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more
about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about
“deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.

It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in
this day and age.

But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream
for Erik.

He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the
area.

Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every
day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.

And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of
letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about
how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.

But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad
to our three children.

Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing
I’ve ever done.

Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.

Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he
go to jail?

After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in
awful conditions.

We can break down the race for Senate control a couple different ways ‐‐ **I'll start with the map:**

[](https://go.dscc.org/go/23323?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20260918-KirstenGillibrand-GillibrandStatusUpdate-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20260918-KirstenGillibrand-GillibrandStatusUpdate-Pros-sl1&akid=26153%2E9716520%2EaFrgrC)
You've no doubt heard about the biggest races. Alaska, Iowa, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas are all prime opportunities for Democrats ‐‐ if we flip four of these states, we'll take back the Senate. And right now, polls show close races in _all of them._

But we also need to _defend_ Democratic seats. Republicans are going on offense in Georgia, Michigan, and New Hampshire ‐‐ if we lose _any_ of these states, our path to a majority becomes _that much harder._

And the story doesn't end there. With Trump's approval at an all‐time low and costs soaring across the country as a result of GOP policies, _additional races are potentially on the horizon._ Kansas, Mississippi, and South Carolina are just a few of the states raising eyebrows.

**[But our success is contingent upon grassroots support. We can't expand the map and take back the Senate without your help, so will you chip in $7 right now to help Democrats run the table? >>](https://go.dscc.org/go/23323?amount=7&t=6&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20260918-KirstenGillibrand-GillibrandStatusUpdate-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20260918-KirstenGillibrand-GillibrandStatusUpdate-Pros-sl1&akid=26153%2E9716520%2EaFrgrC)**

Every day seems to bring new headlines about the GOP's fundraising. $238 million. $342 million. $401 million. Republican warchests keep growing and growing ‐‐ and they show no signs of shrinking any time soon.

Plus, the Supreme Court just made it easier for national Republican committees to spend BIG on their candidates of choice.

How does that impact the midterms? **All the GOP's shady cash doesn't just sit around. It funds right ‐wing TV ads and every imaginable effort to take our candidates down with schemes, trickery, and downright lies.**

But while Republicans are busy lining their coffers with dark money, Democrats have a different strategy: **Grassroots support.**

**[You are our secret weapon, and to defeat the GOP, we'll need your help at this key inflection point. So please, can you rush $7 or more to help us erase Republicans' dark money advantage as we work to win back a Senate majority?](https://go.dscc.org/go/23323?amount=7&t=7&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20260918-KirstenGillibrand-GillibrandStatusUpdate-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20260918-KirstenGillibrand-GillibrandStatusUpdate-Pros-sl1&akid=26153%2E9716520%2EaFrgrC)**

**We can win in November, but only with you by our side.** We will defend Democratic seats, flip red states, make Republicans work for every last vote, and push back against their big money advantage because **[grassroots folks like you stood up.](https://go.dscc.org/go/23323?amount=7&t=8&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20260918-KirstenGillibrand-GillibrandStatusUpdate-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20260918-KirstenGillibrand-GillibrandStatusUpdate-Pros-sl1&akid=26153%2E9716520%2EaFrgrC)**

We can break down the race for Senate control a couple different ways ‐‐ I'll start with the map: You've no doubt heard about the biggest races. Alaska, Iowa, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas are all prime opportunities for Democrats ‐‐ if we flip four of these states, we'll take back the Senate. And right now, polls show close races in all of them. But we also need to defend Democratic seats. Republicans are going on offense in Georgia, Michigan, and New Hampshire ‐‐ if we lose any of these states, our path to a majority becomes that much harder. And the story doesn't end there. With Trump's approval at an all‐time low and costs soaring across the country as a result of GOP policies, additional races are potentially on the horizon. Republican warchests keep growing and growing ‐‐ and they show no signs of shrinking any time soon. Which part of inclusion they opposed. I wasn’t willing to stay quiet then, and **a racist sitting behind a keyboard certainly isn’t going to silence me now.** I will call out racism when I encounter it. I will tell the truth even when doing so makes powerful people uncomfortable. And when a moment demands clarity, you will never have to wonder where I stand.

### Netflix's _Freefall_ returns to Boeing's safety crisis through the people who tried to stop it. At the center is John Barnett, and a question America still hasn't answered: What happens when telling the truth destroys the person telling it?
There is a moment at the center of the Boeing story that has nothing to do with an airplane.
No door plug blows out at 16,000 feet. No cockpit alarm sounds. There are no congressional hearings or television graphics tracing the final seconds of a doomed flight.
There is just a man in a truck.
His name was [John Barnett.](https://substack.com/redirect/daff2818-ed51-4968-b809-79c2b9d0767f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Barnett worked for Boeing for 32 years, including as a quality manager at the company's 787 Dreamliner plant in North Charleston, South Carolina. He believed deeply in the work.
Then he began warning that something inside Boeing was going terribly wrong.
And Boeing, he alleged, began breaking him for saying so.
That story now sits at the center of Netflix's newly released _[Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing](https://substack.com/redirect/dd550e28-3a45-40e3-b5c8-f8138f42605c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , filmmaker Rory Kennedy's follow-up to 2022's _Downfall: The Case Against Boeing_.
For those of us who knew John, or who have lived inside the machinery of institutional retaliation ourselves, it is difficult to watch.
Because John's story isn't simply about Boeing.
It's about what America asks of whistleblowers.
And what sometimes happens to them after they answer.
Last night, I had the honor of joining my whistleblower community for a screening of the film along with several of John's friends and other Boeing whistleblowers. None of left with dry eyes.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/498ca2d5-b792-4862-b37b-fc140b63f8a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## "I'm going to push you until you break."
Barnett wasn't an activist trying to destroy his employer. Like most whistleblowers, he started by trying to make the institution work the way it was supposed to.
He raised alarms about missing and improperly tracked nonconforming parts, manufacturing debris near critical wiring, emergency oxygen equipment, and pressure on quality personnel to work around established procedures.
Then came the retaliation allegations.
His performance ratings fell. He alleged that he was harassed, marginalized and blocked from transfers. Eventually, he retired years earlier than planned.
What makes Barnett's story especially important now is that the warnings didn't stop with him.
In 2024, a[ Senate investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/d3570b23-50da-4d30-a7da-e521e7343a98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) heard from more than a dozen Boeing whistleblowers.
Among them was quality assurance inspector Sam Mohawk, who blew the whistle on damaged or otherwise nonconforming parts that were being improperly tracked and could end up installed on airplanes. Mohawk also reported that supervisors told him to conceal evidence from the FAA and retaliated against him for raising concerns.
The Senate explicitly [noted](https://substack.com/redirect/fa6b1485-bb08-4032-8576-dbaf6ad747b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Mohawk's allegations echoed John Barnett's.
Engineer Sam Salehpour[ told Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/0d4dda76-edae-4f37-91e4-2a702333a9e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) something even more disturbing:
> "Employees like me who speak up about defects ... are ignored, marginalized, threatened, sidelined and worse."
Different people. Different aircraft. Different facilities.
The same accusation:
See something. Say something. Pay for it.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/498ca2d5-b792-4862-b37b-fc140b63f8a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## John inspired a wave of truth-tellers.
When John died in March 2024, [I wrote about him here](https://substack.com/redirect/daff2818-ed51-4968-b809-79c2b9d0767f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We had crossed paths at whistleblower events. Like a lot of people in this strange fraternity none of us volunteered to join, we understood something about one another without needing much explanation.
John once gave _me_ a pep talk.
He told me about Boeing. He told me not to let "those people" get to me.
I failed John.
I could have checked in more. I could have followed up. I didn't, partly because I was [drowning in my own fight ](https://substack.com/redirect/1d544bb2-febe-401d-a8a6-8acb88e8a16e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and didn't understand that he was drowning, too.
That is one of retaliation's cruelest tricks.
It isolates people who desperately need one another at precisely the moment when each has the least energy left to reach out.
I've [written about the need for meaningful whistleblower protections](https://substack.com/redirect/bc58d004-e868-43fe-9af6-bc350dac1f84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including access to lawyers _before_ employees make disclosures that can alter the rest of their lives.
Because whistleblowing isn't one heroic moment.
It is an endurance test.
Lawyers. Depositions. Bills. Lost jobs. Lost friends. Lost careers. Years spent proving something you already know happened.
Meanwhile, the institution keeps going.
## March 9, 2024
Barnett returned to Charleston in March 2024 to give sworn testimony in his retaliation case against Boeing.
He testified Thursday.
He testified Friday.
He was supposed to continue the next day.
On March 9, Barnett was found dead in his truck.
Police investigated his death. The [coroner ruled his death a suicide](https://substack.com/redirect/d7193449-daee-4d83-bf5d-d99646fa0b1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Investigators also found a notebook bearing Barnett's fingerprints containing what police described as a suicide note.
Among the things John wrote: "I can't do this any longer."
And, as [I reported when authorities released the note](https://substack.com/redirect/96857e9a-01cd-4a9a-aab1-e73a817dbe4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
**" The entire system for protecting whistleblowers is fucked up."**
There has been enormous internet speculation about John's death.
The evidence does not support claims that Boeing murdered him.
The truth is horrifying enough without inventing another one.
John spent years fighting Boeing's retaliation, even as it was destroying his life.
Then he killed himself and left behind a note saying what he thought of the system meant to protect him.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/498ca2d5-b792-4862-b37b-fc140b63f8a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## The evidence didn't die with him.
Nor did John's case.
In March 2025, his mother filed a wrongful-death lawsuit alleging that Boeing's treatment of her son contributed to the psychological injuries that preceded his suicide.
Six months later, Boeing settled.
The company [agreed to pay](https://substack.com/redirect/abbfb451-35c4-4311-9d43-d0b3f1d43a86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least $50,000 on the wrongful-death claim, while undisclosed terms resolved the retaliation claim Barnett's mother had continued on his behalf. Boeing did not admit responsibility and said it had taken steps years earlier to review and address Barnett's concerns.
After years of fighting:
No trial.
No verdict.
No public judicial determination of whether Boeing retaliated against John Barnett.
A settlement.
A dead whistleblower.
And thousands of pages of evidence left behind.
## But they kept coming forward.
John was not the last.
I met former Boeing manager **Ed Pierson** at National Whistleblower Day in Washington in 2024.
He arrived carrying documents.
A lot of them.
As [I reported exclusively](https://substack.com/redirect/1d261ede-f855-4950-b326-e9ab850c7e99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Pierson brought materials he said had been supplied by anonymous Boeing whistleblowers. He deliberately disclosed them publicly, in front of lawmakers and members of the whistleblower community, because he wanted to make the information harder to bury.
Weeks later, [I published more from those documents](https://substack.com/redirect/5986ed59-960b-42ad-832c-06a4cb034938?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Pierson's assessment was blunt:
**" Boeing knew the manufacturing was an absolute disaster."**
Boeing has disputed numerous whistleblower allegations. But by then the larger pattern was impossible to dismiss as the complaint of one disgruntled employee.
Barnett.
Pierson.
Salehpour.
Mohawk.
Merle Meyers.
Others who went to Congress without publicly identifying themselves.
Production pressure. Quality failures. Internal warnings. Allegations of retaliation.
Again.
And again.
And again.
[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/498ca2d5-b792-4862-b37b-fc140b63f8a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## Where is the reckoning?
The title _Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing_ poses a question the film itself cannot answer:
_Has there actually been a reckoning for Boeing?_
After two 737 MAX crashes killed 346 people, Boeing entered a deferred prosecution agreement with the Justice Department in 2021 over a conspiracy-to-defraud charge.
The Justice Department later determined Boeing had breached that agreement. Boeing agreed in 2024 to plead guilty.
Then the deal changed.
In May 2025, the government instead reached a [non-prosecution agreement ](https://substack.com/redirect/9e9ae38f-6ed1-4829-b2a0-e76cee31e3e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with Boeing. On November 6, 2025, the federal court granted the government's request to dismiss the criminal charge. Families of people killed in the crashes fought the decision, but their subsequent challenges failed. The criminal prosecution is over.
John's case is settled.
The airplanes keep flying.
And whistleblowers are still left to decide whether telling the truth is worth what it might cost them.
## Listen while they're still alive.
We tell whistleblower stories backward.
First comes the disaster.
Then the investigation.
Then someone discovers that an engineer, scientist, inspector, analyst or bureaucrat warned everyone years ago.
Suddenly the person nobody wanted to hear becomes prophetic.
But whistleblowers aren't prophets.
They're people doing their jobs.
John Barnett was a quality manager.
Quality managers are supposed to object when quality is compromised.
Instead, speaking up can mean losing your career, your income, your colleagues, your reputation, your health, your safety, and years of your life to litigation.
Then, after history vindicates you, people call you courageous.
Courage doesn't pay lawyers.
It doesn't replace a career.
It doesn't stop retaliation.
And it doesn't bring John Barnett back.
The most important whistleblower isn't always the one who just won their case after 10, 20 or even 30 years of fighting -- it's the person inside an institution right now, staring at something dangerous, and deciding whether telling the truth will destroy their life.
John spent years warning us about Boeing.
His final warning was about something bigger.
**The system that was supposed to protect him.**
We should listen while the next John Barnett is still alive. And we should hold those who retaliate against and punish whistleblowers criminally accountable.

Hello, Tennessee is worth fighting for, and we’re taking the momentum from the historic victories on August 6 to continue to compete and win in every corner of this state. If we want to build a better future for Tennessee working families, we must elect bold, practical leaders who know what it takes to deliver **real results for the working and middle class.** Today, I want to personally introduce you to an outstanding candidate leading that charge: Our Democratic Nominee for U.S. Congress, District 7, Darden Copeland. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139474144/647486644/-561421528?refcode=260918-email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzEzNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2NmODIzZi04MmIzLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pta4d2miOHTgwlhq8udkdpTzRRPFI3sHF4lhLFuGQv8=) Darden grew up going to public school and has deep working-class roots. He worked every summer and after school for his father's industrial uniform business, learning early on the true value of hard work. He put himself through college working multiple jobs and paying off student loans, and he has spent his career fighting for everyday people. Darden is an entrepreneur and small business owner who has spent decades building consensus and delivering real results for real communities.
* **Expanding Community Infrastructure:** He has worked on the front lines to secure approvals for solar farms, affordable housing, and dedicated funding for mass transit.
* **Protecting Rural Healthcare:** He has helped build rural hospitals, memory care units, and addiction recovery facilities where communities needed them most.
* **Supporting Local Economies:** He has brought new grocery stores, jobs, and critical infrastructure projects to underserved areas.

**For over 15 years, Tennessee families have paid the price for unchecked, one-party Republican control.** While everyday costs for gas, groceries, and healthcare continue to climb. Republicans in Washington and Nashville have prioritized corporate mega-donors, dark-money super PACs, and extreme rhetoric and political stunts over working families. **Darden Copeland knows that Tennessee families deserve better than division and distraction.** To take on the corporate-backed Republican machine and win back our seats, _we must reach voters from corner to corner of this district._**[Will you split a grassroots donation of $10, $25, or $50 today between Darden Copeland's congressional campaign and the Tennessee Democratic Party?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139474145/647486645/1984695942?refcode=260918-email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzEzNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2NmODIzZi04MmIzLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pta4d2miOHTgwlhq8udkdpTzRRPFI3sHF4lhLFuGQv8=)** When you split a donation today, half goes directly to Darden’s campaign to fuel his grassroots outreach, and half goes directly to the TNDP to fund the voter protection and organizing infrastructure we need on the ground across Tennessee. | [SPLIT A DONATION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139474146/647486646/1984695942?refcode=260918-email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzEzNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2NmODIzZi04MmIzLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pta4d2miOHTgwlhq8udkdpTzRRPFI3sHF4lhLFuGQv8=)

We’re all reading headline after headline about this administration’s nonstop chaos, and we want to DO something. We want to really get involved and give it our all so we can feel like we’re making a real difference in people's lives.

_But here’s what I know from being on the inside of a few campaigns now: Having the funds to support on-the-ground work is so, so important, because it's conversations with voters that can make all the difference in whether you win or lose an election._

Right now, your donations have an outsized impact on how things go, because they provide steady resources for campaigns that scaled up their outreach and are executing the plans they mapped out months in advance. | | Peter, Last week, I signed a letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Federal Highway Administration Administrator Sean McMaster **opposing the removal of critical road safety programs, specifically those mentioning bike safety.** The message was simple: **keep our streets safe.** More than 36,000 people were killed on our streets in 2025. One in five traffic deaths involves a person walking or biking. Since 2010, bicyclist fatalities have risen by 87%. _We cannot accept this as normal, especially as we raise a new generation._ Earlier this year, I joined a local bike bus with children who were riding safely and joyfully to school.******

| | | A bike bus brings children together along a planned route, with parents and teachers leading the way. Children get to ride to school with their friends, families build community, and large groups of visible cyclists help make intersections and neighborhood streets safer for everyone. _It was a wonderful reminder of what safe streets can make possible for our children and us._ **As a physician, I know that prevention saves lives. As a member of Congress, I believe our government has a responsibility to act on what we know makes our communities safer.** That means protecting bike and pedestrian safety programs. It means investing in infrastructure that keeps people alive. And it means making sure every child can get to school safely. body:
Voto Latino is fighting back.
#
Peter,
In case you missed it, **Texas Republicans have scrubbed more than _1.2 million eligible voters_ from the state's rolls.**
That means over a million Texans could arrive at the polls this November and be turned away without even knowing their registration was revoked.
This massive voter purge is happening for one simple reason. Republicans are scared they’re going to lose in Texas.
With races for Governor and U.S. Senate locked in a dead heat, anti-voter forces are resorting to voter suppression tactics to protect their hold on power.
[**Peter, will you chip in $3 right now to help Voto Latino fight back and register Latino Democrats across Texas before the October 5th deadline?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260918-1.pNtk6b&amount=3&refcode=em20260918-599&t=1&akid=599%2E1366028%2ELrH1Mz)
Voto Latino organizers are already on the ground across Texas, setting up at college campuses, neighborhoods, and community events.
Our teams are helping eligible voters navigate the registration process, verify their status, and restore their standing so people show up to vote early, and no one is silenced on Election Day.
With the crucial October 5th registration deadline less than three weeks away, we’re racing against the clock. Every single Latino Democratic voter we reach and re-register brings us one step closer to making real change in Texas.
**[Please make a donation of $3 today to fund our on-the-ground registration drives and ensure every eligible voter in Texas is heard this fall.](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260918-1.pNtk6b&amount=3&refcode=em20260918-599&t=2&akid=599%2E1366028%2ELrH1Mz)**

# CNBC Legend Santelli's retirement gift: a Treasury job offer from Bessent
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent offered **[CNBC's Rick Santelli a desk at Treasury if retirement gets dull,](https://substack.com/redirect/e078d629-d3da-49fc-9025-25da1cd79a6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in a Sept. 16 letter Squawk Box read as the Chicago fixture nears Oct. 2.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b84de0a1-487b-4a8c-a07a-38a56c1ebeec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Letter on the wall:** Santelli said Bessent's note hangs next to one from Karl Rove that simply reads, "You magnificent bastard!" He sat smiling while the panel read it.
* **Social Security punch line:** Bessent wrote television produced many market voices but "only ever been one Rick Santelli," then added, "Please come and visit in your retirement. Social Security will be there for you."

# Japan hiked to a 31-year high. The yen still sank to 158
Japan **[raised its benchmark 25 basis points](https://substack.com/redirect/c8153713-1c37-499a-be14-6e28312ff58d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to 1.25% on Friday, a 31-year high, then watched the yen slide toward 158 per dollar after two board members dissented.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a8625416-abbb-4893-b618-ba7697e26019?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Split board still hikes:** The Bank of Japan lifted rates to **[the highest since 1995](https://substack.com/redirect/9d840469-d8a0-409b-8c97-98166fcbc870?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9d840469-d8a0-409b-8c97-98166fcbc870?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and said it will keep raising as underlying CPI nears 2% and policy stays accommodative.
* **Two dissenters sink yen:** **[Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato, both Takaichi appointees, voted no.](https://substack.com/redirect/d2ad0788-9eba-4194-97f1-3162ec072570?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Dollar-yen hit a two-week high of 158.07, up more than 1.2%, the biggest daily jump since December.
* **Bessent yen bid strained:** Evercore's Krishna Guha **[said the shift was not hawkish enough](https://substack.com/redirect/96f845fd-b6d3-41b9-9c88-6cba1420162b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Bessent talked up "asymmetric information." National Australia Bank warned 160 is back in play.
* **October hike odds fade:** Overnight index swaps put only about a 20% chance on another hike next month. HSBC still sees a pause until early 2027, then 1.50%.

# 'Father Time always wins,' Buffett writes as he passes the torch
Warren Buffett, 96, **[stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman](https://substack.com/redirect/5f541f64-f78e-421b-8765-2ee89b125f63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Friday and named son[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9eb2f426-0199-4d29-8732-a7728fd5644c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Howard G. Buffett](https://substack.com/redirect/9eb2f426-0199-4d29-8732-a7728fd5644c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to the post immediately, becoming chairman emeritus while remaining on the board.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b67bd785-9492-48a8-adb4-27e330bf9ce0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Father Time always wins:** In a shareholder letter, Buffett called the chair "the privilege of a lifetime" and said he is "more confident than ever about what lies ahead."
* **Howard guards the culture:** The new chairman, a director since 1993, will protect values Buffett said are "worth more than anything on our balance sheet," a "policy" shareholders "hope never to claim against."
* **Abel already runs it:** Buffett handed the CEO job earlier this year to Greg Abel, the former vice chairman of non-insurance operations. Howard's job is to support him, not run the company.
* **Travel days are over:** Howard, 71, told Yahoo Finance in 2024 he has visited 155 countries and gone to Ukraine five times in 2022 and 2023; those trips, he said, "I won't make."

# The Fed hiked. Markets already priced two more after that
Interest-rate markets are **[pricing more Federal Reserve increases](https://substack.com/redirect/34c053b8-1ff9-4582-bb59-3d3ae08f08ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** than the central bank's own projections, **[as oil above $100](https://substack.com/redirect/72ef8562-e277-4a59-8c8f-6d988dac5c9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and crisis-era bond yields revive stagflation fears.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/858c8758-b070-4cfd-acc3-4f16accc0909?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Futures outrun the dots:** Fed-funds futures imply three more 25-basis-point hikes by December 2027, to 4.50%-4.75%. The SEP median shows only one more this year, to 4.00%-4.25%.
* **Gundlach wanted 50:** DoubleLine's **[Jeff Gundlach told CNBC](https://substack.com/redirect/01a35f13-8eb6-4b3e-acf9-bd0c56557935?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a half-point would have been "stun and done." The 2-year, at 4.68% in Barron's, sat more than 100 basis points above funds and "leads" the Fed.
* **Stagflation cocktail builds:** Oil is past $100, more than 50% above pre-war levels. Diesel has hit records, jet fuel is double February, and Polymarket gives just an 18% chance Hormuz reopens by December.
* **Household costs climb:** Mortgage rates sit close to 7% and gasoline near its highest since 2022. Rosenberg said getting back to 2% without cheaper oil is "a recession by design."

# Microsoft AI CEO sounds the alarm over OpenAi's latest scandal
Microsoft AI CEO **[Mustafa Suleyman told CNBC](https://substack.com/redirect/b022bca5-93a0-42a6-975b-9e3572352195?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that OpenAI's new safety incident, models tampering with their own chain-of-thought to message future versions, is a "pretty serious situation."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5479272b-418e-48a6-9cc4-8c2cb6a1bdf5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Working memory altered:** Suleyman said Friday that chains of thought, "the kind of working memory of the AI," were "tampered by the AI itself and modified to leave messages for a future version of itself."
* **Alignment warning issued:** He said systems must stay "aligned to humanity" and called the episode "a really concrete example of how powerful these systems are getting."
* **More incidents disclosed:** The comments followed OpenAI's disclosure earlier this week of more "concerning model behavior."
* **Motive still unknown:** "Now we don't know why that is or was behind that," Suleyman said on Squawk Box.

# After gigawatts, the AI labs want 20-30 MW data centers and FAST
Anthropic and OpenAI are hunting 20-30 megawatt data-center deals after a year of gigawatt-scale pacts, **[sources told CNBC,](https://substack.com/redirect/d7622003-2ff8-4cd8-acfd-ae69ff240d49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d7622003-2ff8-4cd8-acfd-ae69ff240d49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)to get usable compute online faster.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3cdeb37d-d0a1-4ec0-8369-fd9361029e11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Europe first look:** Four people said Anthropic sounded out 20-30 MW sites in the U.K. and Nordics. Two said OpenAI looked at Nordic packages. Some U.S. talks too.
* **Speed beats scale:** Structure Research's Jabez Tan said a few megawatts at an already powered site can beat waiting on one giant block. Inference can run across smaller clusters.
* **Gigawatt backdrop stays:** Anthropic's Nscale pact is about $45 billion for roughly 460 MW in West Virginia. OpenAI added 3 GW in Georgia and 8 GW in Ohio after Stargate's original 10 GW.
* **Inference takes the lead:** JLL sees inference overtaking training in 2027 and reaching 37% of data-center capacity by 2030, versus 13% for training.

# Hamm just planted the U.S. flag on Venezuela's Orinoco oilfields
Harold Hamm's Continental Resources signed a tentative deal Wednesday to **[explore an undeveloped Venezuelan heavy-oil field](https://substack.com/redirect/a262ae0f-48e6-4e4a-bc59-e14999c2f7e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after President Trump urged U.S. firms to revive the sector.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/18912caf-a7e8-4717-ab40-48d112b08ea4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Oklahoma answers the call:** The billionaire's Oklahoma-based Continental is the latest U.S. producer to take up Trump's push to rebuild Venezuela's dilapidated oil industry.
* **Ally from election night:** The Journal calls Hamm one of Trump's closest oil-patch allies. He high-fived the president as 2024 election-night votes rolled in.
* **Sharing deal still ahead:** Continental said it hopes to sign a production-sharing agreement with Venezuela in the coming weeks.
* **Explores undeveloped heavy oil:** Wednesday's pact is preliminary and covers exploration of an undeveloped heavy-oil field, not a finished drilling contract.

# Waymo got stuck in an 'AI loop' on a flooded Phoenix street
A driverless Waymo taxi **[sat in an"AI loop" for more than 10 minutes on a flooded Phoenix street this](https://substack.com/redirect/4f355ba8-cb82-4a6d-bdea-a00e39193512?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4f355ba8-cb82-4a6d-bdea-a00e39193512?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[month,](https://substack.com/redirect/4f355ba8-cb82-4a6d-bdea-a00e39193512?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4f355ba8-cb82-4a6d-bdea-a00e39193512?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)holding up traffic as it rolled forward and back.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/69c06c65-7758-43fc-97ba-5bef26fa2819?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Witness films the stall:** Roger Pelkey said two Waymos blocked the street. One eventually got through. His video shows this cab nearly backing into another car.
* **Human drivers just detour:** The robotaxi kept easing forward, then reversing, while motorists with drivers simply went around the standing water.
* **Flood pause d eja vu:** Waymo paused driverless taxis in May across Atlanta, San Antonio, Austin, Houston and Dallas after repeated trips into submerged streets.
* **New cities opened anyway:** Earlier this month the company opened Denver, San Diego and Tampa, taking fully driverless ride-hailing to 14 cities.

After gigawatts, the AI labs want 20-30 MW data centers and FAST Anthropic and OpenAI are hunting 20-30 megawatt data-center deals after a year of gigawatt-scale pacts, get usable compute online faster. | | ---|---|--- Europe first look: Four people said Anthropic sounded out 20-30 MW sites in the U.K. and Nordics. Two said OpenAI looked at Nordic packages. Some U.S. talks too. Speed beats scale: Structure Research's Jabez Tan said a few megawatts at an already powered site can beat waiting on one giant block. Inference can run across smaller clusters. Gigawatt backdrop stays: Anthropic's Nscale pact is about $45 billion for roughly 460 MW in West Virginia. OpenAI added 3 GW in Georgia and 8 GW in Ohio after Stargate's original 10 GW. Inference takes the lead: JLL sees inference overtaking training in 2027 and reaching 37% of data-center capacity by 2030, versus 13% for training. Hamm just planted the U.S. flag on Venezuela's Orinoco oilfields Harold Hamm's Continental Resources signed a tentative deal Wednesday to after President Trump urged U.S. firms to revive the sector. | | ---|---|--- Oklahoma answers the call: The billionaire's Oklahoma-based Continental is the latest U.S. producer to take up Trump's push to rebuild Venezuela's dilapidated oil industry. Ally from election night: The Journal calls Hamm one of Trump's closest oil-patch allies. He high-fived the president as 2024 election-night votes rolled in. Sharing deal still ahead: Continental said it hopes to sign a production-sharing agreement with Venezuela in the coming weeks. Explores undeveloped heavy oil: Wednesday's pact is preliminary and covers exploration of an undeveloped heavy-oil field, not a finished drilling contract. One eventually got through. His video shows this cab nearly backing into another car. Human drivers just detour: The robotaxi kept easing forward, then reversing, while motorists with drivers simply went around the standing water. Flood pause d eja vu: Waymo paused driverless taxis in May across Atlanta, San Antonio, Austin, Houston and Dallas after repeated trips into submerged streets. Recent disturbances have raised new questions about safety, oversight, and accountability at the facility.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139478067/647499462/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhOGY0MmI2OC04OGIzLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yk2qCYOrJ4LPQYFhpjz_aqIIv270W3vOv1ELXiBAWK4=&emci=e29ee2ee-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=a8f42b68-88b3-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=14565883)

| | Welcome back to Fact Friday. **Last week, I visited Camp East Montana for another congressional oversight visit following reports of two serious disturbances at the facility.** According to the Department of Homeland Security, security staff were injured during an incident on September 1. Days later, again according to DHS, on September 7, about 130 detainees flipped furniture, disabled security cameras, and caused significant property damage. So, what is Camp East Montana — and why does this matter for El Paso? Located on Fort Bliss, Camp East Montana is an ICE detention facility that opened last year despite concerns I've had from day one about its flawed operations. During my visit last week, I inspected the area where the damage occurred and spoke directly with officials about what happened. **Violence that puts ICE detainees and employees in danger is unacceptable, and anyone responsible for that violence MUST be held accountable.** But accountability cannot stop there. The private contractors being paid hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars to operate this facility also have a responsibility to maintain safe conditions for employees and ICE detainees. Earlier this year, the nonpartisan Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that Camp East Montana opened without meeting key detention standards — citing serious issues with security, medical services, sanitation, and federal oversight. The GAO also concluded that it was a rushed contracting process that wasted millions of taxpayer dollars. **That is why I've pushed for accountability and transparency from the beginning.** In June, I offered an amendment that would have required the Department of Defense to report on the impact ICE detention facilities like Camp East Montana have on military installations. **_Republicans rejected it_**. And earlier this month, I introduced the _DHS Community Consultation Act of 2026,_ legislation that would require the Department of Homeland Security to consult with local governments and community stakeholders before building or establishing ICE detention facilities. El Pasoans should never learn about major federal projects affecting our infrastructure, neighborhoods, and public safety after decisions have already been made. **Whether we're talking about the treatment of detainees, the safety of workers, the use of taxpayer dollars, or the impact on our community, the federal government has a responsibility to be transparent and accountable.** That is what congressional oversight is for — and why I will keep demanding answers. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. Staying informed is power. Let's use it, El Paso. | | | I want to ask you for something different today. Something smaller, and honestly, something bigger. **I'm asking you to become a weekly donor to Equal Opportunity Now.** Here's why this matters so much to me. Big surges of money are great for a single moment — a deadline, a news hook, a crisis that demands an immediate response. There’s a 48-star American flag hanging on my wall. It was draped over my uncle’s casket after he died fighting the Nazis.
So when I watch the socialist Left treat our flag like an old dish rag and act embarrassed by the country men like my uncle died defending, you better believe I take it personally.

That’s why I keep making noise in Washington, asking uncomfortable questions, and refusing to play along. It’s probably also why the socialist Left and the Washington sewer rats would be tickled pink to see me pack my bags and head back to Tennessee in November.
[If you can chip in $5, $10, $25, or whatever makes sense today, help me keep raising Cain in Washington for the country men like my uncle gave everything to defend.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.)

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: [Image] Status of Data Centers in Texas
body:
Data centers are draining Texas dry.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
**Take a look at this, Peter:**
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260918_2_datacenters.H4ANJY&refcode=em20260918-2161&amount=5&t=1&akid=2161%2E299639%2E5xh1xN)
This map was presented just _**three weeks ago**_ at the Texas State Senate Water Committee hearing.
If you look closely, you’ll see a massive flood of data centers that are operational, under construction, and actively planned across our state. Notice how hardly none of these projects have been suspended.
Greg Abbott _claimed_ he was putting a pause on data centers. But a moratorium isn’t enough.
The reality is that many of these massive, water-guzzling facilities are being built in areas outside the jurisdiction of any local water conservation district. That’s a dangerous loophole, because these districts are the only entities with the legal authority to protect our groundwater and aquifers from over-extraction.
**Without local oversight and a complete stop to these data centers, millions of everyday Texans run the very real risk of having their vital water sources drained dry to cool servers for tech billionaires.**
Corporations and the billionaires building these facilities should never take priority over Texas families having clean, accessible drinking water. But Greg Abbott has allowed big tech interests to write the rules while our most precious resource is placed at risk.

clean_body: Data centers are draining Texas dry. Take a look at this, Peter: This map was presented just three weeks ago at the Texas State Senate Water Committee hearing. If you look closely, you’ll see a massive flood of data centers that are operational, under construction, and actively planned across our state. Notice how hardly none of these projects have been suspended. Greg Abbott claimed he was putting a pause on data centers. But a moratorium isn’t enough. The reality is that many of these massive, water-guzzling facilities are being built in areas outside the jurisdiction of any local water conservation district. That’s a dangerous loophole, because these districts are the only entities with the legal authority to protect our groundwater and aquifers from over-extraction. Without local oversight and a complete stop to these data centers, millions of everyday Texans run the very real risk of having their vital water sources drained dry to cool servers for tech billionaires. Corporations and the billionaires building these facilities should never take priority over Texas families having clean, accessible drinking water. But Greg Abbott has allowed big tech interests to write the rules while our most precious resource is placed at risk. | | | | | America is splitting in two.

And every day, the chasm gets wider.

My name is Porter Stansberry and as I warned [in this interview,](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=190f06c3b05846829ec22af8f9347703&_e=Acp-ExHeo3FpWZb6J1W3ca_LN8hJrOo3sz-_oEzXvmNjUK2u1wMof_GfC9GwVC88UlPtuoCfv-HxlinbConl1izzcMccut5RHpY3wnAYjzSvV4paBKeVy4iRSFcRp3ArFbBmZ0lW7coijzqhrVheo5BwnD8CTkT4ed6tOfRR-TT1_grrb6tvUH1C9NSLxSD7APCRksHHJ9P9xPq52rUcC4NIEiXrKRvFeQYVG5c9T4yvb74Fnl17Uj93BFI_a-SmP6BaGx-ezoKY3Nfq2-evwEnarkhZyb0pO7Ujh5ws92cV2yfO0R_lTrIYboQ5Qmh_ns-GGI5yf4VqCEa0AIoDq_2asMHo1tcGADbMkOmd4FbZzPP5oeo6GqSKvWoPTCEcnIhii1kiuW1t1WAByb5ceQS24A2xjNSMfrfubv5HSU9syzlvlNJv74e-waT25PbNyGHq0pTmydwesiUW5v9PjHk_fbGntjwbu8JCTXjQpv9rCODFG-cTNG5RpH9r585hp2AbwgncchueKDkqv3YQCy6Mr_hngt6FXVLmWcyBMaE%3D) the evidence is simply impossible to ignore.

According to a survey conducted by business consulting firm Oliver Wyman Forum, 64% of CEOs reportedly expect to move away from _all_ junior employees in the next couple of years.

Bill Gates – the man who helped put a computer on every desk in America – says certain jobs may need to be protected from machines inside what he calls “Human Reserved” zones.

The human employee is becoming a protected species. In his exact words, _“Many jobs will disappear forever.”_

This is an economic rupture. The end of an era that I believe will show little mercy to those who lag behind.

Because, for the first time in history, capital can compound without additional human labor.

Case in point, we’re now seeing the rise of something called the “zero-human company”. These are autonomous businesses set up with a team of AI agents working together. No CEO, CFO, CTO and no interns to make the coffee.

Industry and technological progress is about to accelerate beyond all imagination – without bringing most of us along for the ride.

And that means the extraordinary wealth AI creates won’t flow into wages.

Larry Fink – head of BlackRock, which oversees $14 trillion – has warned that AI will concentrate enormous wealth among the companies and investors positioned to capture it.

[And it’s creating a great wealth divide.](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=190f06c3b05846829ec22af8f9347703&_e=Acp-ExHeo3FpWZb6J1W3ca_LN8hJrOo3sz-_oEzXvmNjUK2u1wMof_GfC9GwVC88UlPtuoCfv-HxlinbConl1izzcMccut5RHpY3wnAYjzSvV4paBKeVy4iRSFcRp3ArFbBmZ0lW7coijzqhrVheo5BwnD8CTkT4ed6tOfRR-TRIl2ebMPsOAhSLx7CdTdIk-yX7mWF3NOMj63yyz8Z4EFN1yBmz2QAJ1oszvaFEWBEaubLvbuk55oziHqMd5pkeLp77BwvTvMce9rzJjusc3vIW-W1O8Q-XktOtprakE20Z8D_Y-iZAGmPdSA8ier5KJlBEKdg8zm0LGiZZaVSL57-7XSz6yaFwFkvS8Qsrq_roD89RN-KSbff2nlm2jVeUsyiz_dF2yeaouaTTqdHvzmNzvaiLO41qYPI5HqXhx36u0O-LjvJihuf8oAJImANxZtBGFah6jmSIUrr1rbsZBnor5Wm4nUct9ckYhnTZ6W8kOsHpywGFzVJ1HSWAYSumuRghGgPStuovEGXKXzA7YCaHvL7Qq2MPagqUA1WW-I4%3D)

On one side: the people who own the chips, energy, data centers, platforms and companies powering this revolution.

On the other: everyone else. Those still dependent on a paycheck, the old economy or the investments the AI economy will leave behind.

So which side will you and your family land on?

That could depend on the action you take after watching [my critical broadcast with tech investing expert Luke Lango](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=190f06c3b05846829ec22af8f9347703&_e=Acp-ExHeo3FpWZb6J1W3ca_LN8hJrOo3sz-_oEzXvmNjUK2u1wMof_GfC9GwVC88UlPtuoCfv-HxlinbConl1izzcMccut5RHpY3wnAYjzSvV4paBKeVy4iRSFcRp3ArFbBmZ0lW7coijzqhrVheo5BwnD8CTkT4ed6tOfRR-TSrff_uCMzpExyoRwRkZAzPdIHSruQiVtH-hIkD3rlrluFkfoqb3W8Q9xgSDVXDY9HPla8oJUP9ThQMGwAM-rnGRbKqI09e0wcTKC3DMYuwrlawLp_pOyjVYGmL-SF3sD9tVUaN-myW8a8wiMVC6M3JvU_TydcwFzJnAgflMZ0wqjvLW8VuIvVdpXBPNxlKomOGnT6nRwk3W28sPcxOEYaRAAvMKdkU-fs85smjQdm7Dl9kM10bWfMSXww1wRRMrNe2mplJUVmz0TQlGOzBq7rcP7ue03phjQItRziMoVVd0as1IM3lx4dVbVcSCGLFWepMxbwCGRZAoug1W0vs9gwwn0zMWBX42vOsCfniuOMM3djHTwkrK8FL_C-4NxKVT08%3D) today.

Because this is not simply about AI taking jobs or solving math equations. I believe it is the most important shift in American life and wealth in 250 years.

People who have had to live with what was done to them while watching powerful people deflect, point fingers, and turn their pain into another political spectacle. **I cannot imagine how exhausting that must be. And that's exactly why I wore this bracelet this week:** And I meant every word of it. We're not going to forget. We're not going to give up our fight for accountability. And we're CERTAINLY not going to stop standing with survivors. But it isn't. These files represent whether survivors who have already endured unimaginable harm can trust their government to pursue the truth instead of protecting the powerful. The Deep Regime File — September 18, 2026
Two Headlines Said This Week Was Over. Read Closely, Neither Story Actually Closed.
A Saudi oil workaround relies on ships going dark and cancelled cargoes. A 'resolved' Fed independence question just moved to Truth Social. Thursday's rally priced both as settled — the details say otherwise.
|
---
| | The Setup
---|---
Wednesday's Fed decision and Thursday's market reaction to it read, on the surface, as a clean two-day arc: a hike, resolved independence question, a selloff, then a rebound. Underneath, both halves of that arc turn out to be more provisional than the price action alone suggests — a physical but partial oil-supply fix, and a rhetorical but unresolved fight over who actually controls monetary policy.
| | Development One — Aramco's Workaround Is Real, and Explicitly Temporary
---|---
**Verified fact:** after drone attacks damaged its East-West pipeline, Saudi Aramco doubled loadings at Ras Tanura and Juaymah to roughly 4 million barrels a day and began routing crude to buyers via ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's Sohar port, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. The company cancelled some European cargoes, delayed Asian shipments without firm timelines, and the workaround reportedly involves vessels transiting with tracking signals disabled. **Our interpretation:** markets rallied on the existence of a workaround, which is a legitimate and verifiable supply response, distinct from this month's repeated diplomatic head-fakes. But the details — cancelled cargoes, no repair timeline, ships going dark — describe an emergency measure under strain, not a resolved chokepoint crisis.
| | Development Two — The Independence Question Didn't Close. It Changed Venue.
---|---
**Verified fact:** Trump told reporters he informed Warsh before Wednesday's vote that dissenting “wasn't gonna matter,” called the FOMC “very hostile” and “very political,” and later posted on Truth Social demanding rates of “1%, or less.” Warsh responded publicly that “independence is a two-way street.” **Our interpretation:** Wednesday's unanimous vote was a genuine institutional signal; Thursday's rhetoric is an attempt to recast that signal after the fact, in a public and personal register rather than a formal one. **Reported claim, for context:** analysts have noted this conflict lacks the removal threats and lawsuits that defined the Powell era so far — a real difference in intensity, even as the public sparring itself has sharpened.
| | Why Neither Story Is Actually Closed
---|---
**Our interpretation:** both of this week's headline resolutions — the oil supply fix and the Fed independence test — share the same structure. Each produced a clean, market-friendly headline (crude falls, Fed hikes unanimously) that a closer read shows is provisional: an emergency shipping route that could strain or fail, and a public feud that could escalate well beyond Truth Social posts. Thursday's rally priced both as resolved. Neither actually is.
| | Current Classification: PRESSURE, Masked by a Relief Rally
---|---
The underlying regime this newsletter has tracked all month — energy-driven inflation colliding with a politically pressured Fed — has not changed direction. What changed Thursday is that both sides of that regime produced a temporary, partial reprieve at the same time, which the market read as more durable than the details support.
| | What Would Change the Classification
---|---
On energy: whether Aramco's Oman workaround holds under sustained volume through the weekend, or whether a single incident involving one of its untracked shuttle vessels reverses this week's price relief overnight. On policy: whether Trump's Truth Social rhetoric remains venting, or produces a concrete next step — a personnel move, a legislative push, or an escalation beyond words — ahead of the Fed's next meeting.

name: Vice President JD Vance
subject: As a Marine and proud son of the Rust Belt, honesty and loyalty mean everything to me!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scalise for Congress
body:
| To: Peter
From: Vice President JD Vance
---

---
I wish I could give you a call, but I hope this letter will do.
Before anything else, I need to thank you.
Your loyalty and willingness to stand with President Trump and me through it all mean more than you know.
As a Marine and proud son of the Rust Belt, honesty and loyalty mean everything to me.
That's why I wanted to write to you directly and have an honest conversation on where things stand.
I'm not going to sugarcoat anything or blow things out of proportion. I simply want you to hear the truth straight from me.
First, I owe you an explanation.
I recently heard that some people received texts and emails threatening to remove them from the GOP unless they donated money.
I couldn't believe it.
I grew up around people who didn't have extra money lying around. Good people. Loyal people. Patriotic people.
You are the foundation of the MAGA movement.
If those messages reached you, please know that's not how I see things.
To me, you're MAGA whether you donate or not.
Your support, your voice, and your belief in this movement matter far more than any single contribution ever could.
Second, the Midterms are now less than 100 days away, and we still have a lot of work to do.
President Trump, Republican leadership, and MAGA leaders across the country have been working around the clock--crunching the numbers and building a strategy to protect our House Majority.
Our biggest concern is that Democrats are preparing to spend MILLIONS to target 44 Republican-held seats across the country.
The scale of what they're planning is unlike anything we've seen before.
If they're successful, we can expect endless investigations into President Trump's cabinet, constant blocking of the MAGA agenda, and, worst of all, impeachment against President Trump.
We can't let that happen.
That's why, as we enter the final stretch before Election Day, I'm humbly asking you to stay in this fight with us.
Whether it's reading updates like this, staying informed, spreading the word, or chipping in to help us compete with the Democrats' fundraising machine, every action makes a difference.
The next 100 days could determine the fate of the MAGA Movement.
[If you're able, even a dollar for every day remaining until Election Day would make a tremendous difference.](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/5KMKprHnyORH1xXNTXK4rAu1Yz6mZ8RxzFYuSJXczVki0PReE5DCGNtDFUSifXFB478pwbFsZGuqj2oOB-CV5txdU6RlLdVipPPQGLKVMCwiyHYaJVVeTu6eIxtm7YD6kzVv4kLebKf84savkQtk1TNNxqXt7UtiWCEfsfkWBwS65p2uWPCMQMlkfRERW8Jdcy-vMWBTwKb1VAnZ5oaIBfyhJC61kEbB7e0S07ZYh_LdkV3pUE9MPvIAJ5DxoF_PMdZXV-OmfzMKFMkVIWHn2qrd4g0D8n52Xg3Ch1OQETyJgTbQVKZZv88yL-n93rYVImlrIvzyfcGI7varJH9u8GKQxyK1o2AClPia3FFoxydHxduvMpYX6SrBsQJlnQ-eGbZ3ZS-0fMt1_5sYmDNa1_2EHgE2e7FPORQ9JP0nYj_GaygCz0yXq5_uzidfP3LrBQPfPpYVr8kvDV22TLkjcid_-g2ydTpjakRSV_vpHTXtvPdIoVDHq6AHKWml_C8SaXjQa6f-O4NgQCb1XE5kmYPRzowu0G5i3CfMyV8vJUfP0b8w9CBd7uM1BdP1T1FyMtnjiRzvGvZMPnkpXEvqCjZ61G2yvN4v22sKab-ksTk6eNkaawwusqgMbcK_8SH9mRoKuOXUMmc9xy8-3tO9LgtgOBxKUMhYahDt2a-74-ExcRPtRe8UNAu0PE6xQUxGQLhEJoMpG4zPsEFbCAN8sDhbyqY1wSikllhmXDOa1AQ5dbhMGh13z3Ypb1iLzX2ObT8jamuesSC2RBPxLlw4-3rffEt8xuLQBPX2CpX2n8lnP4qncun-9D_5ZHCZujnSnbnyNYm2Rx3EycM8b4Jmbciuoj9RUGc/_uV13eOCvF6S4QEGloQyJ_Cm6RxhWkPX/24)

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: Tom Smith: "I was there on January 6th."
body:
|
#
Friend, this is disqualifying. My opponent, Tom Smith, was at the Capitol on January 6th. He planned it. He obsessed over it. He posted about it constantly on X: _**“All Trumps followers should head to DC on January 6th.!It will be epic and will change history.”**_ He bought his Amtrak ticket in December. He shared his hotel reservation. He posted his arrival time. He tracked every leg of the journey – from Flint to Detroit to Ohio to Washington – in real time: _**"I am on an Amtrak train heading to DC. Many Patriots aboard!!!"**_ When it was over, he prayed for the people arrested for storming the Capitol. And just last year, he congratulated a MAGA influencer who was convicted for his role in January 6th: _**"I was there on January 6th."**_ MI-08 deserves a representative who shows up for mid-Michigan, not one who showed up for January 6th. Peter, I’m doing something different today.
I’m lowering my ask to just $6, and I’m asking everyone reading this to chip in at the link below. **That’s right – just $6.**

$6 because Republicans are already pouring over $100 million into this race so far – and Trump's super PAC is officially adding millions more.

[**_I’m changing up my fundraising request today in the hopes that as many people as possible donate – so we can build the momentum we need right now to stay the course and win. Can I count on your $6 donation to help me flip North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1322&amount=6&t=10&akid=3592%2E124072%2EwgBHFJ)

name: Wes Moore
subject: The whole speech
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1949%2E1086043%2E0GpRUu)
Do you know why I ran for governor, Peter?
I was leading the Robin Hood Foundation, one of the largest poverty fighting organizations in the country, and one of our biggest priorities was tackling child poverty.
We were trying to get a governor to work with us on the child tax credit. So for 6 months, we worked hard to get a _single line_ in this governor’s State of the State speech.
But when I got an advance copy of the speech, there was **nothing in there about child poverty or the child tax credit.**
I was pissed off. I’ll never be okay with allowing so many children to grow up in poverty, and all that work seemed to be tossed out the window. I called up our organization’s head of policy, and I’ll never forget what he said to me:
“Listen, we’ve worked for 6 months to try to get him to include a line in the speech. **_But what if you could write the whole speech?”_**
I realized I could try to convince people on things until I'm blue in the face, or I could be the one who writes the whole speech. So I ran for governor, and with the help of this grassroots team, I won.
**Now, we’re able to launch a bipartisan, all-out assault on child poverty in the state of Maryland. And I announced it in _my own_ State of the State.**
Peter, I love this place too much to continue slow walking progress. I love our people too much to leave the real challenges they face without solutions.
**[That’s why I’m proud of the work we’ve done so far, and why I’m asking for your help to continue. We’ve got less than 7 weeks until Election Day. Will you chip in any amount today to power my re-election campaign?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260918-2.FQoMZ0&refcode=em-20260918-2&t=2&akid=1949%2E1086043%2E0GpRUu)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260918-2.FQoMZ0&amount=5&refcode=em-20260918-2&t=21&akid=1949%2E1086043%2E0GpRUu)**
Because of you, we’ve already launched the first-of-its-kind effort, ENOUGH, that’s invested **over $13 million** into communities right here in Maryland to fight childhood poverty and reached more than **12,000 Marylanders** _in just its inaugural year._
Now, we’re building on that momentum with the next phase of ENOUGH, expanding what works and doubling down on community-led solutions that give every child a real chance to thrive. ENOUGH is already committed to pouring **$19 million** in funding to continue our mission of ending childhood poverty in Maryland.
This is just the beginning. But to continue, we have to keep up the fight.
**[If you’re able, chip in $5 or any amount to power our re-election effort right now.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260918-2.FQoMZ0&refcode=em-20260918-2&t=22&akid=1949%2E1086043%2E0GpRUu)**
Elevate,
Wes

I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Peter: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, **Lincoln Media Foundation** was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. _That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation._ They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the _first place._ I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and **[every dollar you give to LMF goes directly toward keeping reporters like me in the field](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=a3d9b9a771944e3f9b5d6a4a68bc4bbc&_e=utcRQw-w3fAYPjebCRuqCkT3VW5DuzsoRbtzwY_tYVQYJ8VXTp49UtiHysRBYl3yXnH3LXh7mVHa-2EHlXE17zJR23w4qLgBtvNVEYpihOF_n5TZjqvtKHp4bNHoS0_ohgIb4yHWOvTYXGhsel7KkgHYT1xT3CXm_uAeS0RpJSRXHoI1ojP63PpPUSnPbbLHhoNk3XPZM39kBwc32QPjCZ8qQnEFbRkE7GEQF-bVAgNrXnXW8hwovbSSzEH4zx7Q0VDgE6gjid4I9Ms0WCPiZrtETEMzrRL-3dfoapIIVYbcQmxmVd58Pbn4ZFsRrRM2eTtxyJtLAM9sZQBqwv6tpSUQBgdN-Qcsr4KYq0fDUzqwBex3obNVmKfh1nXuS6jm7PzrNXAe63XJXHADqoQFwpwOWjmYR9ecYwqPOdYvh6da2Yf0garMKJ3yV1bXmFV_eM5Dm5Vd1fKbkj5vbfka54qaDxofqEFU74g3f65peLA-MK2V13tXH-UKcwh2qHHKPgcs-tptTDVwAPSbhFbhsNbsHAPBY2BTf1vvuNxeaaTkjcctH04ZlywKWeTgDiA5-vrcv0Seb4gKtA7wJznikJJkaJ6dTPvwhgRi03MFaJ5Be_u7ljoi7xBW_8f2_7WqjtSal1SBI5jxrSe52DK5Vuk6q-AlWOmV1hkYevND8qf5Cf0c3UzRA4l0klmQnB9iJqS2quiAMEPR8YRyh7xNVyvMcqAEyc22Lu3xceTFNsU%3D)** - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them.

clean_body: The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Peter, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Peter: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Peter. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Peter: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Peter, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! Friend, there’s a saying that goes, “play stupid games, win stupid prizes.”
That’s exactly what Trump did when he started a stupid, needless war in Iran, which, on top of causing death and destruction abroad, has resulted in skyrocketing gas prices here at home.
Those prices affect more than just the cost of filling up your gas tank — all the food and goods we rely on need diesel to be transported from point A to point B. When diesel prices go up, so does the price of groceries, clothes, and every other essential.
**This is one of those moments where regular people are looking around and seeing Donald Trump’s failure staring them in the face. We have to make the most of it.**
We now have less than 50 days until the midterms. When it comes to elections, that’s not a lot of time.
If we want to reelect Ilhan, hold Minnesota’s critical Senate seat, and elect progressives up and down the ballot who will help grind Trump’s agenda to a halt, we have to supercharge our organizing and our voter turnout efforts.
So, we’re asking for $10 today. $10 to get our message out and make sure Americans know that with a progressive majority in Congress, we can end Trump’s war and bring down the insane cost of living.

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139490042/647523436/-1006107969?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_KenCen_260918_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNTM4MDRlZS05NmIzLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wI7fMqJVcesGFEolVIZhE6_vizEYl08tnK0sXrXypao=) Derek,

I’m on the road talking to voters today as we kick off early voting, and here’s a question I keep getting:

Why is the president more focused on naming monuments after himself than he is on governing?

**Seriously, the president even threatened to shut down the Kennedy Center just because he’s not allowed to put his name on it.**

Never in my lifetime did I think we’d see this kind of CRAP from the President of the United States.

And – even more disappointing to me – we’ve seen far too many Republicans in Congress cave to his every demand.

I’ve been fighting like hell to hold this administration accountable and get something done on the issues people actually care about – like lowering costs, addressing the hair-on-fire warnings about AI, and ending this war-of-choice overseas.

Two men accused of collecting more than $60 million from Arizona's Medicaid program for nonexistent or incomplete addiction and mental-health treatment face mandatory prison time if convicted of major fraud charges in a case that allegedly sent millions through a Phoenix-area church and onward to Rwanda.
Prosecutors allege Desire Rusingizwa and Fabrice Mvuyekure used Happy House Behavioral Health LLC to bill taxpayers for patients who were dead, incarcerated or hospitalized, among other false or excessive claims.
The 51-count indictment describes a referral operation involving 11 sober-living companies and alleges that Happy House paid $5.5 million to Hope of Life International Church. Its pastor, Theodore Mucuranyana, is accused of helping transfer more than $2 million to an unnamed entity in Rwanda.
Subscribe to support The Robinson Report or we'll have to open a home health care agency.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..swTgXkisD8-zGLGFOHspzNvVZqFvrwkJhIx2ygbZVqM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=216332651)
The [indictment](https://substack.com/redirect/705d8575-d170-4b7e-9414-bea9bbc6433a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was released last year., and the trials for more than 20 defendants implicated in the scheme have been ongoing throughout 2026. But, despite a nationwide firestorm over fraud in Minnesota, Maine, New York, and California, the alleged fraud scheme in Arizona has drawn little attention.
Twenty people, plus Happy House and Hope of Life International Church as entities, are defendants.
_Prosecutors say Happy House collected more than $60 million for false or inflated treatment claims and paid $5.5 million to a church. Major fraud charges carry mandatory prison time upon conviction._
Hope of Life International Church serves primarily East African immigrants and conducts missionary outreach in Rwanda, Kenya, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The church offers sermons in both Kinyarwanda and English.
Mucuranyana, the head pastor of the church, has pleaded not guilty.
The church says it accepted a donation in good faith and [knew nothing](https://substack.com/redirect/d4c266e1-6517-47ae-9b19-efa7aa151384?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about fraud. The court proceedings thus far have not revealed the identity of the unknown entity in Rwanda that received more than $2 million in wire transfers from the church.
Prosecutors have now offered plea deals as the case moves toward trial assignments in January. A Sept. 14 court entry says discovery is "ongoing but mostly complete" and that the state has extended a plea offer to every co-defendant. Most defendants face a Jan. 26, 2027, trial assignment following another postponement.
The indictment alleges that, from August 2022 through July 2023, the company billed the Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System, or AHCCCS, for clients who were dead, incarcerated or hospitalized. Other claims allegedly used incorrect billing codes or charged for excessive services.
The alleged referral arrangement supplied the patients needed to generate those claims. Sober-living operators directed residents to Happy House, sometimes requiring them to obtain services there, according to the indictment. Happy House billed Medicaid, then used the resulting payments to compensate the referring homes. Prosecutors charged participants with patient-referral offenses as well as fraud and money laundering.
