This man in a women's Navy uniform has been a "leader" in your government.And the person standing next to Levine? That's Sam Brinton. He's a man in a dress who was a Biden-Harris nuclear official until he got caught stealing luggage at Ronald Reagan Airport filled with ladies clothes. Then consider that 11 states and counting, plus the District of Columbia, are transgender "sanctuary" states. That means in some of them, minor children can flee there and get transgender services -- even sex change operations -- without their parents' permission.And did you know Medicare now covers sex change operations?It just goes on and on... This evil is widespread.Or maybe you're thinking like so many, "Riley, adults are free to do whatever they want. And children should be kept away from this evil by their parents."As for the transgender adults, your generation used to call these people perverts, predators, and pedophiles.Should they be representing our government? Alone in classrooms with our children?And as for parents, I agree this problem would have less traction if parents just said, "No."But parents in Maryland had their child taken away because they refused to let their son transition to a "girl." Parents in states like Vermont and Colorado saw their foster care licenses revoked because they admitted they would not help a child who may be assigned to their home get puberty blockers or have sex change surgery.Parents in California got themselves elected to the school board, passed guidelines to protect their children from the transgender movement, and now the state of California is suing them. Even with President Trump's temporary Executive Orders attempting to ban men from women's sports and bathrooms, and halt grotesque medical procedures for children... you can see, the radical transgender movement has parents backed into a corner.I'm sorry I've gone on so long detailing the transgender threat. But when I'm speaking around the country, I meet so many seniors who say, "I wish someone had told me about this sooner."But the good news is that right now, you still have a chance to help stop the radical transgender movement before they push us down their slippery slide.And today I'm writing you on behalf of a group that is doing more work to block the transgender movement than anyone I know.It's the legal non-profit the Center for American Liberty. And your gift is going straight to help them.With the help of patriots like you, the Center for American Liberty fights the transgender movement in the courts because that's the only way to stop them.And the Center for American Liberty is attacking this evil from all sides with their comprehensive three-pronged approach.#1. They 're fighting radical schools.I know it may sound crazy to you but in today's taxpayer-funded schools, teachers, and counselors encourage young children to socially "transition" at school and then facilitate the "transition" by giving children new names and even giving them new clothes so they can dress as the opposite sex. And they keep it all a secret from parents!You probably remember a time when kids needed a note from home just to get an aspirin at school!The Center for American Liberty is taking these radicals to court in multiple cases. And they already have one major win! When you give, you're making sure PARENTS have the final word in guiding their children -- not school radicals!#2. They 're fighting radical doctors.My fellow conservative, I hope you love and trust your doctors. There are lots of good ones out there. But there are also doctors who mutilate children for profit in the name of transgender "care." They use their "expertise" to convince even conservative parents that if they oppose "transition," their child will commit suicide.Then these doctors pump children full of dangerous puberty blockers and perform gruesome surgeries to remove children's healthy breasts and other parts. Again, I apologize for the graphic description, but this is the pure evil we're facing.Maybe you've seen a girl named Chloe Cole on Fox News. In a landmark case, the Center for American Liberty is helping her sue the radical doctors and hospital that gave her a double mastectomy at age 15. President Trump signed an Executive Order aimed at protecting children from these grotesque doctors but a Biden-appointed federal judge has already blocked its enforcement.The best way to protect children is to contribute to help Chloe and the Center for American Liberty win their case to make sure this never happens to another child! #3. They 're fighting for your right to speak out against this heinous evil.You'll be happy to know that fighting for Freedom of Speech is one of the Center for American Liberty 's specialties.They've notched plenty of victories in this space including fighting for an 82-year-old grandmother who got banned for life from the YMCA. This grandma raised the alarm that a grown man dressed in a women's bathing suit was in the women's locker room "helping" two little girls get ready to use the bathroom.And she was the one punished!But thanks to supporters just like you, the Center for American Liberty fought back and won! And when you give, you're helping them win all their critical cases confronting the evil of the transgender movement. I know you'd probably love to fund an entire court case on your own after all I've told you, but all I'm asking you to do is renew your support with a tax-deductible gift of $30, $50, $75, $100 or even $250 or more. Please donate whatever amount is right for you whether it's smaller or larger. The Center for American Liberty needs and appreciates every dollar that comes in. And because I believe so strongly in the work they're doing - and because they are one of the few groups who've stood shoulder-to-shoulder with me in this fight...It will be my honor to send you my new book "Swimming Against the Current: Fighting for Common Sense in a World That's Lost Its Mind" as my free gift when you donate $50 or more to the Center for American Liberty. Before I go, please let me share one last thought with you.Every morning as a competitive swimmer, I would get up and think of this verse:For I consider that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be compared to the glory that is about to be revealed to us. (Romans 8:18) I applied it to my swimming: work hard now and wins come later. But now I see that God has a much bigger plan for my life just as He does for yours.This battle isn't about a swimming victory. It's about Kingdom victory. I will never stop fighting to protect God's Truth and I think you feel the same way.Thank you for reading my letter all the way to the end. I'm praying for you, and I hope you'll pray for me too. | | | Sincerely,Riley Gaines P.S. I'm so grateful that President Trump signed temporary Executive Orders aimed at stopping the radical transgender movement. But the Left is launching attacks in the courts to undermine him and we must fight back.God made man and God made woman. The attempts to deny those basic truths, are attempts to deny the truth of God. Your help is so critical to the Center for American Liberty 's work, when you donate $50 or more, as my personal "Thank You," I'll send you my new book, "Swimming Against the Current: Fighting for Common Sense in a World That's Lost Its Mind" for free. Please hurry. It's getting hard to hold back this evil without you. I don't want you to look back a year from now and say, "I wish I had done something when I had the chance." Fellow Patriot,

Pat Ryan wants you to think he is an independent voice for the Hudson Valley. But his record tells a very different story. Here is what he is not telling you.

**He wants to stop Elon but his largest stock holding is Tesla.** Pat Ryan has publicly attacked Elon Musk and his influence in politics. But his own financial disclosures show Tesla is one of his largest personal stock holdings. He is against Elon Musk in public and invested in him with his own money. You cannot make this up.

**He attacks AI oligarchs while standing to get rich from AI.** Pat Ryan warns publicly about the dangers of uncontrolled artificial intelligence. Meanwhile he holds a private stake worth between $100,001 and $250,000 in Socure, an AI company with vast government contracts that could pursue a public offering. **Pat Ryan is positioned to profit from the industry's growth while pretending to regulate it****. We call him PatGPT for a reason.** [**DONATE NOW TO DEFEAT LYING PAT >>**](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=710e6e29d3454b2e9e7860fbd14cd0e6&_e=sqDKRYL0sOJiwvD6nQ600-btObtzZ5ZcCga4stWg-7FJTZzvQRylYejXOrMoc1hPNH2eH4S4UHXgCnR2lsRofzYtidQ5dDZz_OxP-AKX9l1QQCZ9z2YIDQ84vv5Rgquwk-9WK4etDp83A_Rv1ky3r3nJtfscvCMhwj01vU5b3-neUVtYDavRKe0bDEAbcooSRBwKctr7xR3jfbb0R0pKVLZqlAiVtrkmL3UdDPUEVm5saVRv8M_N3gHP3BJ7g1vlvbPfcAB7Mj0I9FisCm7qz0W7HMTQXw6hDcd_48uqATkQGtkZzBLKDOcIPt-JxlN1kvstsuNMAwVHO_0elRKBojysOyJYOMhPHkrp8jOrx0Wt80NB71kr9c-pwqUAJ5-zlcyTjHFxUDskzTtO2I-EWcJg0a-zGT3nd9Xyvh3VtNjCv9KxsDTnOyUb9fE8w1vl00xxUUH5AtEovMO_mL_SjD71Q1SUqWzTCGRHO8qy9AsOc0H-nE3RY_ur1QyM7WX-HElOc3OvYZ1FIbn3Ot7WVOa0mJot5fUHUge4C4WY_27Fxy3aMQjM_6xu0WiU8FbX7PKUECSuVsD0JlHFJb1g24oRLyMF-vhKk4-JEu2oYGfPlbMlHZyPM4N67qtJ_2W2ojN8G7m62CReKprL2Qi8OHMyqln-HBNM1doBzqWgTeIEfhtoTtTEZN7rK6eKgPeS581B99njuo7DVTg7aFzaQvQslDH0gGAIj2unl1pcv30%3D)
**He voted against the bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act.** A rare moment of genuine bipartisan agreement to protect children from the dangers of AI and the internet. Pat Ryan voted no. _He chose the tech industry over the safety of Hudson Valley kids._

**He voted against stopping congressional insider trading.** Congress passed a bill to stop members from trading individual stocks while voting on laws that affect those same companies. Pat Ryan voted no - while personally holding a six-figure Tesla investment and a private AI stake worth up to $250,000. He voted to keep enriching himself at your expense. I recently wrote an [op-ed](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139491201/647527121/266883760?ms=260918_dr_oped&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTM1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYmQyMTZkOS05YWIzLWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hctJSKA8ow8LjtWB5US7t1du7Qmft8ib2ElnQZN-y_Q=&emci=9d155f4d-23b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=cbd216d9-9ab3-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=29434467) in Fox News — yes, you read that right. It was about data centers. I understand that not everyone on our side will love the fact that I published there, but I've always believed that if you actually want to move the needle on an issue — especially one this consequential — you have to be willing to make the case to people who don't already agree with you. Data centers are one of those issues. Here in HD-28, we know what's at stake better than almost anyone. Loudoun County is the data center capital of the world. What happens here shapes national conversations about energy use, land use, jobs, tax revenue, and quality of life. I hear from constituents on every side — from families worried about power grids and noise to workers who depend on these facilities for good-paying jobs. There are strong opinions on this issue, but one thing we can all agree on is this: we need a real plan that puts the interests of working families first. That means looking at the facts before we decide on sweeping bans. It means giving local governments the room to decide what's best for their own communities. And it means being willing to have hard conversations, even in rooms where our arguments aren't always welcome. That's what my op-ed was about. clean_body: Here's what I said and why | | Peter, I want to share something with you. I recently wrote an in Fox News — yes, you read that right. It was about data centers. I understand that not everyone on our side will love the fact that I published there, but I've always believed that if you actually want to move the needle on an issue — especially one this consequential — you have to be willing to make the case to people who don't already agree with you. Data centers are one of those issues. Here in HD-28, we know what's at stake better than almost anyone. Loudoun County is the data center capital of the world. What happens here shapes national conversations about energy use, land use, jobs, tax revenue, and quality of life. I hear from constituents on every side — from families worried about power grids and noise to workers who depend on these facilities for good-paying jobs. There are strong opinions on this issue, but one thing we can all agree on is this: we need a real plan that puts the interests of working families first. That means looking at the facts before we decide on sweeping bans. It means giving local governments the room to decide what's best for their own communities. And it means being willing to have hard conversations, even in rooms where our arguments aren't always welcome. That's what my op-ed was about. | | | **** **Corporate PACs' checkbooks have been coming up short lately, Peter.** Turns out money can't buy every election — not when there's a movement of people knocking doors, making calls, and talking to voters one on one. The latest proof: a new Data For Progress poll1 showing WFP champion **Mai Vang** leading establishment Democrat Doris Matsui by 4 points (32% to 28%) for California’s 7th congressional district, without taking a dime of corporate money to get there. And it's not hard to see why corporate special interests are rattled. Mai is running on affordable housing, health care, and child care for working families who've been priced out and let down by leaders beholden to corporate donors. No corporate PACs, no lobbyist money — just a fight for the people Washington keeps forgetting. But Mai’s lead didn't happen by accident, and it won't hold on its own. clean_body: | | | ** Corporate PACs' checkbooks have been coming up short lately, Peter. Turns out money can't buy every election — not when there's a movement of people knocking doors, making calls, and talking to voters one on one. The latest proof: a new Data For Progress poll1 showing WFP champion Mai Vang leading establishment Democrat Doris Matsui by 4 points (32% to 28%) for California’s 7th congressional district, without taking a dime of corporate money to get there. And it's not hard to see why corporate special interests are rattled. Mai is running on affordable housing, health care, and child care for working families who've been priced out and let down by leaders beholden to corporate donors. No corporate PACs, no lobbyist money — just a fight for the people Washington keeps forgetting. But Mai’s lead didn't happen by accident, and it won't hold on its own. Mai is running because she's watched too many families in Sacramento get priced out, pushed aside, and let down by leaders who were supposed to have their backs. She knows what it's like when the system is stacked against you — and she's not interested in politics as usual. Which might explain why her own party turned on her. In the primary, Doris Matsui funnelled money to a Republican just to keep Mai out of the top two.2 Apparently, when an establishment incumbent sees a real threat, party loyalty only goes so far. And Mai is giving the establishment plenty to be nervous about. She won't touch corporate PAC money, and she won't take a dime from companies doing business with ICE. Matsui can't say the same — she's cashed checks from ICE and defense contractors, and the same donors bankrolling Super PACs to crush candidates like Mai all over the country. 3 So, Peter, here's the choice: another Congress bought and paid for by corporate donors, or someone who actually answers to us. Help us drown out the corporate money — from AIPAC to ICE contractors and beyond — widen Mai's lead, and send a champion for working people to Congress this November. # **Pentagon wants to write Fluidstack a $5 billion AI infrastructure check**
The Pentagon is talking a $5 billion Office of Strategic Capital loan to Fluidstack. OSC's book jumped from $984 million to more than $210 billion, and Director David Lorch wants $1 billion to $5 billion tickets. Washington just joined the civilian AI **buildout as a co-banker. Capex is not slowing. The loan is not closed.**
* **Winners?** Fluidstack plus TeraWulf, Hut 8, and Cipher Digital the miner land banks already feeding Fluidstack sites. Cheap Pentagon capital turbocharges whoever owns the dirt and the megawatts.
* **Losers?** The old OSC equipment crowd that begged for $10 million to $150 million crumbs. That window is dead. Late neoclouds without a Pentagon stamp get priced out.
* **Next?** No rate, maturity, or project named. Watch OSC ink the first $5 billion ticket. Then every miner-backed copycat stampedes the window.

I called **[the spend not slowing](https://substack.com/redirect/320d9aed-7ef3-49ec-900e-b60b552b4f6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[the compute squeeze.](https://substack.com/redirect/8c0b287c-3e58-4389-99b0-6812931b3cb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **The**** Pentagon just joined that tape. Trump's July 2025 order waved through anything over 100 MW or $500 million. Defense cash is cheap equity now.

# **Congress chats up ChatGPT while the rulebook stays blank**
NBC asked Congress how it uses AI while it still refuses to write the rules. The lede is GOP Sen. Tommy Tuberville, running for Alabama governor, talking to ChatGPT in the car about Medicare and Medicaid. The headline promises bills and birthday songs. The institution still cannot pass a statute. That's the joke. That's the whole joke.
* **Winners?** The labs. Every member playing with ChatGPT is unpaid product marketing. OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic get a focus group with gavels and zero new law.
* **Losers?** Voters who thought the hearings were about guardrails. Midterms freeze the calendar. Trump already called the scare a "hoax." Congress makes noise then asks Chat GPT what to say next.
* **Next?** More sermons on TV, nothing signed before November. California's two-month memo will outrun Congress. Load the infra. Fade the regulators.

This is the safety-theater loop **[I called](https://substack.com/redirect/15398f8e-1fda-435f-be71-f1890c7f168d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. CEOs beg for a cage. Washington takes the meeting. Nobody turns the key. Tuberville asking ChatGPT about Medicaid on a drive across Alabama is the tell. They use the product. They will not price the risk.

# **Musk sells safety on stage and kills the referee in private**
Elon spent a week agreeing with Dario Amodei and Sam Altman that frontier labs should slow down, then huddling with Jensen Huang and Mark Zuckerberg to tell Donald Trump an industry-funded regulator is a nonstarter. Trump called runaway-AI fears a "hoax." Musk's All-In line: regulation is a "one-way ratchet." That's not confusion. That's a two-track bet.
* **Winners?** SpaceX and xAI. Anthropic now pays SpaceX up to $1.25 billion a month for Memphis compute. The hug printed cash after Musk called them "misanthropic and evil" in February.
* **Losers?** Anyone buying the sermon. Musk sold Grok to the U.S. military for "2,000 munitions to 2,000 distinct targets within 96 hours," then sued Minnesota and California to over product rules.
* **Next?** Trump keeps the "hoax" line through the midterms. Labs keep begging for a cage they can design. Self-testing theater wins. Real statute loses. Load the compute landlords.

This confirms the "pause-as-moat" **[theory](https://substack.com/redirect/15398f8e-1fda-435f-be71-f1890c7f168d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. Sermons don't fund clusters. Rent checks do.

# **NASA writes SpaceX another $946 million ISS check**
NASA just locked SpaceX into three more crewed Dragon flights, Crew-15, Crew-16, Crew-17, through 2030 for $946 million lifting the Commercial Crew Transportation Capability contract to 17 operational missions and $5.92 billion all-in. Government cash still feeds the listed empire.
* **Winners?** SPCX and Musk. Crew-13 flies October, Crew-14 next spring. Boeing's Starliner stays uncrewed for months and crewed only in Q3 2027. NASA has one working taxi.
* **Losers?** Boeing. Starliner remains the "second unique partner" on paper while SpaceX banks the seats. Dragon is being wound down for Starship. Boeing is showing up late to a bar that already called last call.
* **Next?** The ISS dies around 2030. These three flights carry NASA to the funeral. Starship has to work or the government-revenue pillar of the SPCX IPO story wobbles. Unless Boeing does a Blue Origin.

I said this, twice: **[government cash feeds the listed empire.](https://substack.com/redirect/a3e66295-bb06-455c-afa1-41c908457746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Now it's confirmed. The $1.77 trillion IPO needed reusable rockets plus xAI fused. **[NASA just bought four more years of pillar one.](https://substack.com/redirect/ffe1d4f3-2b6a-4edb-b60e-701dab24176c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ffe1d4f3-2b6a-4edb-b60e-701dab24176c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Starship still has to print.

# **Newsom slaps a kill switch on California AI and calls it leadership**
Gavin Newsom signed an executive order Friday to "rein in AI before it's too late." Experts get two months to draft stronger California safety laws, third-party plans for frontier labs and a mandated "kill switch." He calls Washington an "abject failure" and notes "AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation."
* **Winners?** Texas, Florida, and any lab already packing boxes out of Sacramento. Trump's "hoax" line just got a campaign foil. Consultants who will bill California for kill-switch paperwork.
* **Losers?** California AI employers staring at a kill-switch statute. Every CEO who begged for rules just handed Newsom the sermon script and he's running with it. Capital that hasn't left the Bay yet.
* **Next?** The two-month memo lands before midterms. Expect "kill switch" language, auditor mandates, and more labs quietly dual-incorporating in Texas. Newsom shops this tape to Iowa if he gets into 2028 properly.

I **[called this movie.](https://substack.com/redirect/5c26f00e-d419-42f5-accd-44e0aecca403?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The exodus accelerates **[when Sacramento punishes success.](https://substack.com/redirect/15398f8e-1fda-435f-be71-f1890c7f168d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/15398f8e-1fda-435f-be71-f1890c7f168d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Safety theater becomes a cage. Kill switches print speeches, not tokens.

# **Wendy 's biggest franchisee taps out after six quarters of pain**
Meritage Hospitality, one of Wendy's largest U.S. franchisees, filed Chapter 11 on Thursday. It runs 314 Wendy's stores across 15 states, plus one Bojangles and five independents. Store-level EBITDA cratered 48% in 2025 on beef costs and discounts. Wendy's same-store sales have fallen six straight quarters. The stock has lost two-thirds over three years.
* **Winners?** Landlords reclaiming boxes. McDonald's and the value chains eating Wendy's traffic. Distressed buyers circling $10 million to $50 million of assets against matching liabilities.
* **Losers?** Wendy's. Quality Is Our Recipe LLC sits as top unsecured creditor on a $24.9 million deferred-fee claim. Six quarters of negative comps is not a weather problem.
* **Next?** Meritage keeps 314 stores open through the case. Wendy's still prints negative comps. The next franchisee filing tells you if this is isolated pain or system rot.

This is what happens when a brand forgets value and a franchisee eats 48% EBITDA destruction. Assets and liabilities both stamped $10 million to $50 million. That's not a giant imploding. That's a coupon war with a courthouse ending. If you can't win lunch, you don't deserve the drive-thru.

* * *
# **Orion180 slumps 4.2% after a $240 million IPO built to cash out the founder**
Orion180 priced 20 million Class A shares at $12 after marketing $15 to $17, raised $240 million, then slumped 4.2% toward $11.50. The Melbourne, Florida specialty home insurer listed at about $1.14 billion. Founder Kenneth Gregg already took a $55 million dividend this month and $151 million in May. That's an exit dressed as an IPO.
* **Winners?** Gregg and pre-IPO holders who already banked $55 million this month and $151 million in May off a credit line the IPO may repay. They got paid first.
* **Losers?** Public buyers of OIG at $12 after a $15 to $17 dream. They funded the dividend machine in a $187 billion homeowners market where traditional carriers already ran from the weather.
* **Next?** Bamboo Insurance lists next week with CVC selling up to $700 million. Another slump slams the E&S homeowners window. One clean print and the copycats sprint.

Operating tape is real: $13.2 million profit on $80.1 million revenue in the first half versus a $3 million loss on $50.4 million, plus $601 million of premiums through June 30. Fine business. $12 after a $15 to $17 ask says the Street will not fund founder dividends.

The Melbourne, Florida specialty home insurer listed at about $1.14 billion. Founder Kenneth Gregg already took a $55 million dividend this month and $151 million in May. That's an exit dressed as an IPO. Winners? Gregg and pre-IPO holders who already banked $55 million this month and $151 million in May off a credit line the IPO may repay. They got paid first. Losers? Public buyers of OIG at $12 after a $15 to $17 dream. They funded the dividend machine in a $187 billion homeowners market where traditional carriers already ran from the weather. Next? Bamboo Insurance lists next week with CVC selling up to $700 million. Another slump slams the E&S homeowners window. One clean print and the copycats sprint. Operating tape is real: $13.2 million profit on $80.1 million revenue in the first half versus a $3 million loss on $50.4 million, plus $601 million of premiums through June 30. Fine business. $12 after a $15 to $17 ask says the Street will not fund founder dividends. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/9x2Wi1lDZnn?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

Folks, it’s JB Pritzker.
**Chris Pappas is officially the Democratic nominee for Senate in New Hampshire, and I’m proud to support his campaign.**
Now we are in the sprint to Election Day with just 46 days to get Chris elected and stop national Republicans from buying this seat.
His Republican opponent John Sununu isn’t some fringe candidate – he’s from a political dynasty and has the full strength of the MAGA money machine _(including Elon Musk)_ on his side. They’ll do whatever it takes to flip this seat.
**[If you’re with me and ready to support Chris in this critical battleground Senate race, will you chip in any amount today?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260918_2.-CNu9p&refcode=em20260918-2&t=2&akid=8994%2E582294%2EPS04XO)**
If Republicans win in New Hampshire, Democrats will lose their shot at taking back the Senate. _Really._
The choice before us is clear: We can help elect Chris – who has dedicated his life to public service, taken on Big Pharma, and delivered for Granite Staters – or we can let a yes-man for Donald Trump swoop in and snatch this seat.
With the GOP and their allies outspending Chris 3-to-1 and recent polls showing Sununu in the lead for the first time this campaign, we need everyone to step up right now.
I know Chris Pappas can win this toss-up race – he did it four times in his district – but he needs our help if he’s going to defy the odds.
**[So please chip in $5 to get Chris through this final sprint, keep New Hampshire blue, and flip the Senate. Every donation counts in a race this close.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260918_2.-CNu9p&refcode=em20260918-2&t=3&akid=8994%2E582294%2EPS04XO)**

body:
I wish I were emailing under better circumstances.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3855%2E21716%2EbtTdj0)
Hi. It's Sarah.
Last night, I intended to debate my Republican opponent for the first time since I became the official Democratic nominee for Delaware’s at-large Congressional seat.
But what I’d hoped would be a spirited debate about the issues turned out to be something completely different:
**My opponent sought to disrespect me because of my gender identity.**
It wasn’t a slip-up. _He did it repeatedly — until organizers of the debate asked him to leave._
Let me be clear: I am not here to play their game. I won’t stoop to their level. And I refuse to let this nonsense distract from the real harm they’re trying to do at the expense of Delaware families.
Allowing a Republican to flip this seat means we’d have no chance at holding this administration accountable — and that’s an outcome I refuse to see happen. I treat every single day I serve in the halls of Congress as a privilege, and as an opportunity to do right by working Delawareans. I believe I owe that to the people who elected me in the first place, and there isn’t a day that goes by that I take your support for granted.
My vow to you is this: **petty politics like what occurred last night will never distract me from the work I signed up for.** I show up in Congress to deliver real results for Delawareans, not play performative politics for attention.
[**If you’re with me in this fight, please rush $5 or whatever you can today. Let’s show them that every cheap shot makes us stronger. Every attack they throw at us makes me more determined to win this election in just 46 days.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260918-1.a2aAEc&refcode=em20260918-3855&amount=5&t=2&akid=3855%2E21716%2EbtTdj0)

# **RPVI Endorses Raymond James for Senate**
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/uVt09Gmc6eX?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
| |

Dear Friends,
Last week, we introduced Derrick Callwood and shared the priorities he is bringing to voters across the Virgin Islands.
**Today, the Republican Party in the Virgin Islands is proud to endorse Raymond James for Senate in the St. Croix District.**
For years, the refinery supported some of St. Croix’s best-paying jobs and generated $25 million in annual tax revenue. When its gates closed, St. Croix lost jobs, economic activity, and revenue that supported roads, schools, and essential services. Raymond believes St. Croix deserves a seat at the table as Washington looks at expanding American refining capacity. He supports working directly with the White House, federal agencies, Port Hamilton, and potential investors to determine what it will take to reopen the refinery safely and responsibly.
A lifelong Virgin Islander, small businessman, and former Assistant Attorney General, Raymond brings experience in law, public service, and business. His background has given him a practical understanding of how government operates and what it takes to strengthen public institutions, protect public resources, and create economic opportunity.
Raymond’s priorities extend beyond the refinery to healthcare, agriculture, stronger public institutions, and greater accountability in government. His proposals include strengthening hospitals and elder care, supporting local agriculture, restoring horse racing through a transparent and competitive process, and ensuring St. Croix has a stronger voice in major decisions affecting its future.
That is the kind of practical, accountable approach our Legislature needs.
For decades, Virgin Islanders have heard promises about infrastructure, healthcare, economic opportunity, and basic government services while too many of those problems have remained unresolved. Raymond will bring a different voice to the Senate focused on stronger oversight, economic opportunity, and making sure St. Croix is represented when decisions about its future are made.
We invite you to read our new profile of Raymond and learn more about the experience, priorities, and commitment to St. Croix he would bring to the Legislature.
---
| [LEARN MORE ABOUT RAYMOND ](https://us.list-manage.com/18UsJ8czotM?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
---
| |
More competition means more accountability, which creates a better government for all of us.
Onward!John Yob
Chairman

body:
JD Vance is coming to Iowa
---
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-turek-split?refcode=em_20260918_9265_fr&amount=20&refcode2=9265_22930333_zjjzfs&akid=9265%2E22930333%2Ezjjzfs) If you’re wondering why JD Vance is coming to Iowa today, it’s not because he cares about farmers, union workers, veterans, or seniors. Nor is he here to soak up the local culture. National Republicans put him on a plane to my hometown of Council Bluffs with orders to save Iowa’s open Senate seat. I’ll explain why they’re so rattled in just a second. But Vance’s visit will bring a ton of scrutiny to Iowa. [**Will you split a $20 donation to help my campaign and the DNC show the world that our momentum is unstoppable??**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-turek-split?refcode=em_20260918_9265_fr&amount=20&refcode2=9265_22930333_zjjzfs&akid=9265%2E22930333%2Ezjjzfs) **[SPLIT $20](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-turek-split?refcode=em_20260918_9265_fr&amount=20&refcode2=9265_22930333_zjjzfs&akid=9265%2E22930333%2Ezjjzfs)** National Republicans know how vulnerable Ashley Hinson really is. They’ve been pumping cash into Iowa to keep her lackluster Senate campaign afloat since the start. They know we have the wind at our backs, too.
* Polls keep showing this open Senate seat is a dead heat.
* We won our primary by a huge margin.
* We just earned a Toss-Up ranking from Cook Political Report.
* Nate Silver ranked our race as the closest Senate race in the nation.
* This is a once-in-a-generation election that could alter the balance of power in Washington.

So it’s no big mystery why Vance is coming here. It’s because his billionaire bosses are terrified that their grip over Iowa is slipping — and with it, their narrow Senate majority. **But most of all, they’re terrified that a guy like me — a guy without family connections, from a working-class background, who’s fought and scraped for every ounce of success he’s had — could soon be rolling down the halls of power.** Since Vance won’t say this, I will: Iowans deserve so much better than a politician who gets filthy rich while they clip coupons. One thing we know for sure: wherever Vance goes, MAGA money will follow. We’re already facing $55 million in GOP money, and Elon Musk is increasingly targeting this race. [**Since we don’t take corporate PAC money, I’m counting on you to hit back. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Three reasons
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3026%2E4032634%2EOyGPg6)
---
Did you see the news that Trump's super PAC announced they're spending at least _**$49 million**_ on ads in key battleground races — in Michigan, Ohio, New Hampshire, and more? We knew September and October would be when campaign spending really ramped up, and now we're seeing exactly what we're up against — or just the start of it. If Democrats are going to hold the line and actually win back power in November, we need to match that firepower right now: [**I’m asking if you can please pitch in to support our campaign so I can keep fighting for working families in the Senate.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3802?t=8&akid=3026%2E4032634%2EOyGPg6) **I want to share three reasons why your support is so critical right now:** 1\. Our campaign has contributed over $1 million to state parties and committees on the front lines of these midterms. That money is hiring organizers, training canvassers, and contacting voters in competitive races across the country. But we need to do more in the final stretch — and we can't do it without grassroots support. 2\. I've endorsed fighters like Abdul El-Sayed, Angie Nixon, and Troy Jackson in their races — and I’ve been on the road to rally voters in Michigan, Maine, North Carolina, and Georgia. With the support of this team, we'll do everything we can to win these important, competitive races in November. 3\. At the same time, I’m keeping up the fight for the policies America desperately needs. A wealth tax. Universal child care. Banning stock trading by members of Congress. These aren't fringe ideas — they're the backbone of a government that actually works for working people, not billionaires and corporations. And we can actually get this done with a strong Democratic majority. [**Democrats can win this. But not if we get outspent. Not if we let Trump and his mega-donors have the field to themselves. If you’re able, will you please pitch in $28 or anything you can to help support this movement and guarantee Democrats beat MAGA Republicans in the midterms?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3802?amount=28&t=9&akid=3026%2E4032634%2EOyGPg6) This is our chance to put a real check on Trump's power before 2028. If we win back the House and Senate, we stop the worst of his agenda. We block his extreme judges. We hold him accountable. And we can use our power to pass plans that will actually support working people. But we have to act now. September and October are make-or-break months. I'm taking this fight seriously. I hope you'll join me. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

Somewhere in America, a political revolution was supposedly born in New York. It wasn't. Washington State has been the Democratic Socialists of America's proving ground for a century -- and the 2026 cycle only makes the case harder to deny.
The roots came first. On February 6, 1919, Seattle workers launched the first citywide general strike in American history -- 60,000 strong, they shut down a major city for five days and ran it, through their own workers' committees, better than the newspapers could bear to admit. The Everett Massacre of 1916 and the Centralia Massacre of 1919 put Wobbly blood in the state's soil. DSA wasn't founded until 1982; Washington's socialist tradition is two generations older. This isn't an import. It's a homeland.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/236fdda2-1a65-411b-941b-7a8e0a491914?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The wins came next. In 2013, Kshama Sawant -- Socialist Alternative, not DSA, but the same Seattle soil -- became the first socialist on a big American city council in decades and served a full decade, surviving a recall attempt and everything Amazon's money could throw at her. Seattle DSA grew into one of the organization's largest and most battle-tested chapters. In 2024, DSA member Shaun Scott won the 43rd District House seat long held by Frank Chopp -- the Democrat who wielded the speaker's gavel for a generation -- becoming the first self-identified democratic socialist in the Washington Legislature, then took 68 percent of the general-election vote. In November 2025, democratic socialist Katie Wilson won Seattle's mayoralty, the second self-described socialist to lead the city (Seattle DSA never even had to endorse her -- the soil produced her anyway), days before Zohran Mamdani won New York. Washington was governing as socialist before the "Mamdani moment" had a name.
And Jayapal paved the road beneath all of it. Pramila Jayapal, the congresswoman from Washington's 7th District and the first Indian American woman in Congress, never carried a DSA card -- she didn't need to. As chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus from 2021 to 2025, she made Medicare for All, a living wage, and climate justice the caucus's baseline demands rather than its distant dreams. She converted "socialist ideas" from heckler's rhetoric into the standing agenda of the largest progressive faction in Congress -- the very agenda every one of those DSA primary winners ran on. The pipeline from progressive to democratic socialist runs straight through her district, where she has been re-elected by landslides since 2016 without ever drawing a competitive race. In Seattle, the "radical" agenda isn't fringe. It's the water.
The Oregon contrast proves it. In May 2024, Susheela Jayapal -- Pramila's sister, both born in Chennai, India, a Multnomah County commissioner, endorsed by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez -- ran for Earl Blumenauer's old seat in Portland, arguably the most left-leaning big city in America. She was the early frontrunner. She lost anyway, taking barely a quarter of the vote against Maxine Dexter, the establishment alternative. Progressive Oregon drew a line that Washington voters have never drawn. If the Jayapal school of politics couldn't clear a primary in Portland but has dominated Seattle for a decade, the conclusion is unavoidable: Washington is more fertile ground for democratic socialism than the Northwest's other progressive capital. The movement loses next door -- and governs here.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c6830490-f12c-49b6-b512-781ef846c94f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Evergreen State College: where socialism was never a phase. If Seattle DSA is the movement's engine room, then Evergreen, perched in the evergreens above Olympia, has long been its breeding ground -- a campus founded in 1967 on a radical experiment in education itself: no grades, no majors, no letterheads of the ordinary sort, just seminars where consensus and collective decision-making were the pedagogy, not the protest. Students didn't learn about participatory democracy at Evergreen; they practiced it every quarter. That culture made the campus a reliable node in Washington's leftist infrastructure long before "democratic socialism" polled well -- the kind of place where Rachel Corrie's memory is honored, where Olympia's antiwar and port-blockade activism recruited heavily, and where the 2017 "Day of Absence" protests, whatever one thinks of the aftermath, confirmed to the nation that this little Thurston County college had never once flinched from its convictions. Thurston County votes like a pocket Seattle -- among the most left-leaning counties in the state -- and Evergreen is a big reason why. In a state that leads the country in socialist electoral politics, Evergreen is the greenhouse: the place where Washington's DSA pipeline germinates, where a generation learned that organizing is a curriculum, and where socialism isn't a rallying cry borrowed from New York. It's homework.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3cd187a3-6817-4c04-ab2e-dc33679fade1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
https://www.resiliencestudiesconsortium.com/the-evergreen-state-college.html
The national payoff bears Washington's fingerprints. By DSA's own count, 68 of its members won Democratic primaries -- straight races against other Democrats -- in a single cycle, the movement's biggest harvest ever. And the 2026 season has multiplied it: New York's June sweep sent two more socialists to Congress and elected the largest socialist bloc in that state Legislature's history; Colorado Democrats dumped Rep. Diana DeGette for a DSA-backed challenger; Angie Nixon upset her way to Florida's Democratic Senate nomination; DSA member Janeese Lewis George won the District of Columbia's Democratic mayoral primary. Wherever the model lands, it looks like the one Washington built first: canvass-built, labor-allied, and unafraid to actually govern.
Other states are riding the wave. Washington built the beach. From the general strike of 1919 to City Hall in 2025, from Jayapal's caucus gavel to Scott's legislative seat, no place in America has stood more consistently at the forefront of democratic socialism. The Evergreen State didn't join the movement.
The movement, eventually, caught up to it.

body:
Shapiro wants government officials to enter your home without a warrant. Tell him no.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/oR9B6n3oLob?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | |
Peter,
I took an oath to defend the Constitution of the United States. I took it when I put on the uniform. I take it seriously.So when I read that Josh Shapiro’s Department of Health is proposing regulations that would allow government officials to enter your home without a warrant, I didn’t just disagree with it. I was appalled.**The Fourth Amendment is not optional. It is not negotiable. And it does not have a public health exception.** Shapiro’s proposed regulations — buried inside more than 500 pages of bureaucratic language — would give his Department of Health the power to enter private residences and businesses to investigate disease outbreaks. No warrant. No judicial oversight. Just a government official at your door.This is the same administration that wants to access your confidential medical records without consent, interview your children at school without telling you, and reimpose mask mandates by regulation.And all of it bypasses the legislature — because Shapiro knows elected representatives would never vote for this.In 2021, Pennsylvanians amended their own constitution to limit the Governor’s power to do exactly this. The voters were clear. Shapiro is ignoring them.**The public comment period closes September 21. Tell the state that the Fourth Amendment still applies in Pennsylvania:**
---
| [SUBMIT YOUR PUBLIC COMMENT](mailto:RA-DHCHAPTR27PROPREG@pa.gov?subject=Rulemaking%20%2310-242%3A%20Communicable%20and%20Noncommunicable%20Diseases%3B%20IRRC%20%233490&body=)
---
| | | | | |

Tell them these regulations should be withdrawn and that policy this consequential belongs in the legislature, not in a 500-page regulatory filing.**Pennsylvanians said never again in 2021. Let’s make sure he hears it.**
– Stacy

Speaker of the House Mike Johnson is coming back to Washington to support John Braun in one of the most closely watched congressional races in the country.
Just weeks after joining John in Vancouver, Speaker Johnson is returning to headline a special fundraising roundtable and reception in Olympia on **Tuesday, September 29**.

His return underscores the national attention surrounding this race. Washington’s 3rd Congressional District is one of a small number of competitive seats that will determine which party controls the U.S. House next year, and national leaders are investing their time here because they know John can win this seat.
This is a unique opportunity to hear directly from **Speaker Johnson and John Braun** about the stakes in WA-03, the fight for control of Congress, and the work ahead in the final weeks before Election Day.
**Tuesday, September 29, 2026**
**5:30–6:15 p.m.**
**Olympia, Washington**
_Address provided to confirmed guests prior to the event_
**Private Roundtable: $3,500/person**
**Reception: $1,000/person** _**For security purposes, we must receive payment before the event to confirm your RSVP and registration.**_
[Space is limited, and advance RSVP is required.](https://us.list-manage.com/dHfSZ8r8ZjN?e=90b300faf9&c2id=62222c63d51e1bc08f3d4aa9538aea5e) We hope you’ll join us for this special opportunity to support John and hear directly from the Speaker of the House.
(Federal law allows up to $3,500 per individual and $7,000 per couple.)

Hey folks,
John Fetterman says he's not becoming a Republican. But after everything we've seen lately, I have some serious questions about what exactly he thinks being a Democrat means.
In this episode, I dig into Fetterman's increasingly close relationship with Republicans--from attending an exclusive Fox News retreat at Rupert Murdoch's Montana ranch to appearing by video at the Republican midterm convention to praise GOP Senator Dave McCormick. Fetterman insists he's staying in the Democratic Party, even as speculation about his political future keeps growing.
* [**00:01:35**] Fetterman's trip to an exclusive Fox News retreat at the Murdoch family ranch--and why I think it matters.
* [**00:03:39**] Fetterman insists he isn't leaving the Democratic Party, but I break down why his recent behavior has created so much anger and distrust.
* [**00:05:20**] Dave McCormick explains how Fetterman ended up introducing him at the Republican midterm convention--and I have some thoughts.
* [**00:08:02**] We get into Fetterman's foreign-policy positions, his refusal to join fellow Democratic senators on an Iran-related letter, and the episode's claims about his relationship with Israeli officials.
* [**00:10:07**] What Democratic leaders should do about Fetterman going forward--and why control of the Senate makes this fight bigger than one senator.

This one gets heated because it's about something bigger than John Fetterman. It's about trust, accountability, and what voters should be able to expect from the people they send to Washington. Fetterman says he remains a Democrat; I walk through the record that has me deeply skeptical about where this is headed. Friend, I want to share an experience I had on the doors recently. I was in a deep red part of the district when I came across a gentleman watching Fox News as I knocked on his door. After we talked,_**he agreed to vote blue. **_ He said he liked my opponent as a baseball player, but admitted: "He's not coming knocking on my door." That conversation reminds me why I’m doing this and what this campaign is all about: showing up for people. Our team has been hitting the streets hard, even in triple-digit heat, knocking doors to reach voters. So far we’ve hit six of our nine counties, including Kerrville where a large group of first-time volunteers knocked 500 doors in a single day! We’ve also been registering voters all across the district. In San Antonio this week, I registered someone my age who has never voted before. She was motivated because she saw I was showing up for families. Meanwhile, Republicans in this race keep skipping town halls and public forums, with less visibility, less accountability, and fewer chances for voters to ask real questions. That's exactly why I'm calling for a debate. If you believe in this race, voters deserve to see both candidates answer for themselves in public. I was in a deep red part of the district when I came across a gentleman watching Fox News as I knocked on his door. After we talked,he agreed to vote blue. That conversation reminds me why I’m doing this and what this campaign is all about: showing up for people. Our team has been hitting the streets hard, even in triple-digit heat, knocking doors to reach voters. So far we’ve hit six of our nine counties, including Kerrville where a large group of first-time volunteers knocked 500 doors in a single day! We’ve also been registering voters all across the district. In San Antonio this week, I registered someone my age who has never voted before. Asking for your voice today
#

[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260918-AI-Committee-em/?source=em260918-1-90&refcode2=4205.734936.fDo1CB&akid=4205%2E734936%2EfDo1CB)
Peter – I don’t know if you’ve been following this story, so give me a moment to explain what’s going on right now:
Leaders in American AI development have come out over the last few days and claimed that their technology is profoundly unsafe.
They’ve said it could _end the human race._
It is clear that unregulated AI could represent one of the greatest threats we have ever faced as a country. If these CEOs are to be believed, it could be one of the greatest threats in human history.
We can’t wait on Tech CEOs to do the right thing, we certainly can’t wait for the President, and we don’t even have time to wait for the midterms.
This merits a massive bipartisan response in Congress, because failure is not an option.
[**Peter, sign my petition calling for the creation of a Select Committee on AI to give Congress the tools to protect the American people. Congress must act now, before it is too late.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260918-AI-Committee-em/?source=em260918-1-90&refcode2=4205.734936.fDo1CB&akid=4205%2E734936%2EfDo1CB)
[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260918-AI-Committee-em/?source=em260918-1-90&refcode2=4205.734936.fDo1CB&akid=4205%2E734936%2EfDo1CB)
If you want Congress to act with the seriousness this situation requires, I need you to join me and make sure they hear us.
Thank you for adding your voice to mine.
Semper Fi,
Ruben

#### **BREAKING:
Brand-New Poll Shows North Carolina's Senate Race Is Now Within the Margin of Error**
There's been a huge development in this race. Let me explain.
**As I write this, the GOP is going all in to defeat me.** President Trump has endorsed my MAGA opponent, Michael Whatley, and personally attacked me on social media. Stephen Miller went on Fox News to rant and rave about me. Super PACs are putting hundreds of millions behind baseless ads lying about who I am and what I'm fighting for.
They're coming after me so hard because they know the truth: If they're able to defeat us, it won't matter what happens in other swing states. If the GOP wins North Carolina, that's the ball game - they'll likely keep U.S. Senate control until 2029.
**Unfortunately, these attacks are working. A brand-new poll out this morning shows this race is now within the margin of error - and Whatley and the GOP are officially outspending us.**
They're pouring more than $100 million so far into North Carolina to defeat me, and with Whatley in striking distance of taking the lead, these investments are clearly paying off.
I need your help. Without your immediate grassroots support, we could put our shot at flipping this seat at risk. **[If you care about winning in North Carolina and retaking the Senate, making a well-timed donation of $5 to my campaign today is the best thing you can do to help me fight back and win. clean_body: The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Peter, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Peter: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Peter. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Peter: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Peter, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! clean_body: | Please don't take my appreciation for granted, Fellow Conservative.The love I have for you, for Minnesota, and for this country. How many people can say they've put everything on the line and have been within striking distance of making history by flipping Minnesota - a Democrat stronghold - to the Republican column?Not many. Because this isn't easy. It's an absolute dogfight, and you have to love the fight, really love it, to keep pushing when the odds are stacked against you.That's exactly what I've done. And I'm not backing down now.I've dedicated everything I have to flipping the US Senate seat in Minnesota, and there is no question in my mind that this is the right choice when I've seen first-hand what Peggy Flanagan and Tim Walz have done. All the rampant fraud that took place here occurred under Peggy Flanagan's nose as much as under Tim Walz. It's time to drop the axe, show Peggy the door, and restore common sense to Minnesota for good. , I didn't reach the top of my industry by pulling my punches. I put in the work. I never backed down. And I kept fighting, no matter what the naysayers said.That's why I'm humbly asking you for $15. Not $500. Not even $50. This is going to be one of the MOST IMPORTANT races in the entire country. Hey Peter,
---
I was born and raised right here in Lee County. I'll always have a special connection with the people here and the community that has played a huge part in shaping me into the person I am today. The farm that I live on has been in my family for generations. Each person who lives here has left something behind that shows who they are and the mark they've made on the community. For me, it's quite a few things because I like to stay busy. When I was younger, I gathered grafts from heirloom apple trees from a farmer up the road, and planted an entire orchard out back. My mom’s legacy reaches far beyond our home. She was a pillar of this community. Her kindness spread throughout our community, and her volunteer work helped uplift many of our neighbors. Having her as a role model taught me who I needed to be as I grew up. Now’s my chance to make a difference and continue her legacy. I’m running to represent NC-13 because it is my home, my neighbors, and my community. I know we deserve better than the lies and empty promises we keep getting from Washington year after year. But I can’t say the same for my opponent, Brad Knott. He has been representing a district and a community where he doesn’t live. He lives in Raleigh, not in the district. His communication and community involvement are practically invisible as far as we can tell, so how can we believe he knows what we need? It’s simple. **_He doesn’t._** That’s why he has voted time and time again to cut funding for the programs that many in our community rely on, backed wars that increase prices for virtually everything, and refuses to actually face constituents in the district. Brad still hasn’t done an in-person town hall in the district after almost two years. We need someone who is willing to get out in the district, and who is ready to make a difference. And I believe that I can do that for us. It’s not going to be easy, though. Brad is being funded by corporate PACs, lobby interests, and his own family's money in this race. I am relying on my community's support through grassroots donations from supporters like youPeter.

clean_body: | | | | | Patriot , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. Thank you for listening, and I hope I can count on your help. | | — John James Republican Nominee for Governor | | Paid for by John James for MI | | 35744 Van Dyke Avenue, Sterling Heights, MI 48312 The use of John James' military images, uniforms, or personnel does not imply endorsement by the Department of War or any branch of the U.S. military. |

name: Swing Left
subject: Why early voting matters
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
We’re in the home stretch.
#
Hi there,
Today marks the start of early voting in South Dakota, Idaho, and two of Swing Left’s target states: Virginia and Minnesota. Soon, voters will be able to early vote in 47 states across the country.
We’re asking you to join these voters in voting early, if it’s accessible to you. Here’s why:
Once voters have already voted, campaigns don’t need to spend valuable time and resources trying to turn them out. Instead, they can focus resources, and volunteers (like us!) can focus organizing efforts on the people who still need to vote.
Making your voting plan now is the best thing you can do to help the candidates in your district and state. Once you’ve voted, you can spend the remaining weeks of this election helping reach the voters who haven’t.
[**Will you take two minutes right now to check whether you have an early voting location near you and make your plan to vote?**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2372?utm_source=em20260918-2825&t=1&akid=2825%2E1562180%2E16wlyy)
**[Make a Plan](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2372?utm_source=em20260918-2825&t=2&akid=2825%2E1562180%2E16wlyy)**
Today marks a turning point. As voters begin to cast their ballots, we’re officially in get-out-the-vote season, which means **we're in the home stretch of a high-stakes election that will shape not just January 2027, but also lay the groundwork for 2028, 2030, and beyond.**
Democrats can flip the House, win back the Senate, and gain ground in key state races across the country this November—but it will require you and the entire Swing Left community working together to have the thousands of necessary conversations with swing district voters through Ground Truth, our innovative deep canvassing program.
Thank you for voting early and powering our ground game.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260918-1&t=3&refcode2=2825_1562180_16wlyy&akid=2825%2E1562180%2E16wlyy)

## She Bit into an Apple and Solved a Diamond Heist
This October, one of France's rarest gemstones will go on [public display at a major exhibition for the first time in 100 years](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQRp_GdLMyhrC4oEhDd9OmRLP2GE-uf5CZ7GrfPiJKnuA204z0naPz82P7QE5c9h-YaQl72CTUrdDrTCRCbfOMuRbv-XT1Se2dUVzM-Mmb0WYCbaGfN3TCT9q-dX4JRIaGjpb-Ptv7ZLUeu7jMLiCOkzV6HEKPzoYw95M1w52mEHrseLnmtO1nY_RgzG2y86jR9Xp0j0mTU6Mmz1Lb7VflIpFCel9CN1dzl5Yocpxq-K7Mqsz62Xy9HsqsVISaIJdMRZRZXSlwyjuRMuuFVGbV9v9BiL_L3t7gIuYHtYzs4cECXKQCFsDjSARYPERKB3k4a3oSIETeI7y4EfwLBpH4vIBdW_zx4pT4nO5q1HtGTn-t5eu9n4v5EwAA__9__pd1) at the Chateau de Chantilly near Paris. It's there at all thanks to a hungry chambermaid named Suzanne Schiltz, who swiped an apple from a hotel guest's suitcase during her rounds in December 1926, bit into it, and nearly shattered her teeth. Lodged inside was a pink gemstone the size of a lima bean: the Grand Conde diamond. Two months earlier, a pair of amateur thieves had used little more than tall ladders to steal the 9.01-carat diamond and more than 75 pieces of jewelry from the chateau's museum. Police assumed the culprits were seasoned professionals. They were former aviators in their twenties who couldn't sell the loot because the diamond was [too famous for anyone to touch](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHOnDAQRk9julkZL2ugoEhD96dNiQZ7wJO1DTITVtw-IkpOkGaakb739H58TV_IkfP6HRMNy7pMsmxTps8RSYTK5BnTlr3nw20nlSuhuJDwzZPRxoLuoe4mdMInTa_KDwuRoWdFQ912fWt7rZsqDIvtF6zppVu0XYve9a-2m5cZHc52JlvxcM_pvu6M0U9jHrbvGo2u1o2brSanGk2eZSuPnxtnCbTE6xZ6uC1VcQgi-6Ge35QZlRnfJ-P9UGakLFQEOSfKoszocoZDrkjKjDdSmVH3_w5C-JXXcoELmGYqCdnDzAKcZQPMgPseCTB7CBR38nBs8SRACLwG-HAh-BsMAvFxA6sy-P3DMfJhW9XoNSHHP9by_73PwfwOAAD__2_vmDE). When police confronted one of the thieves, they asked, "_Do you like apples?_ " He answered, "_Why?_ " The officer replied, "_You have one with queer seeds in your case_." A team of gemologists has now created a scientific ["identity card" for the stone](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0EGSnSAQxvHT6K4t5DEqCxbZuJtss7RaaLAzCBYSLW-feqncYC7w1f_7_fpcPpEjp_ATdzI--KX6vCS6z0i1Ulkc456Tc3zafFF5dqx22_GLFynkAEJDPy1oK1-0fLTOeCJJr5ZMP056HLQQqt2M1cLpafSrUhZpfGktRilX36vVT-5DtWzec0L3k5TiJWU36EkJtL1Qdh0E2UYJclxz6X5nTnUjH593UGfz3kaz1XqczetHI-dGzvd9dyFn9_6RqN65fHW5hEbOCNufFMoDNhImTgEiugdWrsCpZsAEeByRAJODM8eLHNSNwOJJkD1ECpQclgf-w8BGfNZGzm0x7rg5Rj6HsVEi7MjxX139vutl5N8AAAD__-lTkjE) designed to help identify it if it were stolen. The exhibit runs from Oct. 17 through Jan. 3. "_Diamonds are quite particular_ ," said Mathieu Deldicque, the museum's chief curator. "_You can't enjoy them through pictures, videos, photographs and so on_ _. Their color, their light, their presence are actually so strong that you have to see them in real life._ "
## Three Generations of Nurses, One Hospital
Pat Pendleton was 40 when she enrolled in nursing school. Her husband had been diagnosed with cancer, and she needed a way to support their three children. She earned her degree and [spent the next 25 years as a nurse at Antelope Valley Medical Center](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAUhE9jOiNjs4ALF2noNm1K9NZ-hpf1zwo7oL19RK6QZjTSSJ8-zdd9uQMFSusnRDR-9Uv1eUl4loC14r44gpiTc1RsPnB_R6h2i_CkRQo5cKF5Ny1gKx243BpnPKJE1aDpxkmPgxaibzbzkGoUWo2jHByoh9fg-xuiszB06oa2IXPhhO4mKYWSsh301AuwnejtYxBoWS_QUc17-50p1Q19eF9Crc2xCWar9VWY-mByZnI-z7M96wHXyOR8oZmchb7iajkh9xApvLniKybcoVJOhaefvWDhGxR-5v2JjheIyLdcXlQhMDk3u3Gvk0KgMoysF2sECn8S9f_3HUb-BgAA__8i3IYe) in Lancaster, California. Her daughter, Terryl Call, watched her mother's transformation and followed the same path, enrolling in nursing school at 22 and later joining the hospital staff. "_Watching my mom go through all that and then seeing the pride that she was experiencing, I decided I was going to go to nursing school, and I did_ ," [Terryl said](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DluwzAQheHTSB0NckRrKVikcee0KYUxOZQm5iKQjA3fPnCukPoBDx_-r-t6RQ6ctk-MZPzm1-bzmuhZA7VGZXWMMSfnuNr8oPKK2Owe8c4rSBiFXISaV7SNH7See2c8EdDQk1HTvEzjIqXud0N-1la52-CniRC0knaCgUblPciBdM_mfScXNQPIAeA0LrOWaJXU9jZKsp2W5LjlcvrOnNpOPrzeoJPNsQ9mb-2o3fDRwaWDy0H5CPSeOrgMYqNEBRvnVEX2Iv2USlX4kqPIiYTHyOElnrncyQlsou0kKkYSFgP7XBKj2HM9uGEQCpTS52Xsi3HHk0PgOk6dlltEDn-a9v-ODwO_AQAA__9BrIsC). She now serves as a senior operations leader at the center. Then came the next generation. Terryl's daughters, Tayler Rodriguez, 31, and Amanda Starler, 25, [both work in the hospital's emergency department](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ_GdEaLIYALF2noLm1KtGcvsDn_nLADubePyCukGY000qdP83mbb8ie4_qBgcyyLnNZ0hzpzJ5KoX12jCFF5zjbdND-CljsFvDBswLVS9CyGWe0hQ-a3ypnFiJFbUWmGUY99BqgqzbT0aBosAo06K6nO2DrGntvWosaEWzF5sKBbkaloFWq7vXYAdoGOnvvgazogByXtNdfiWPZaPGvS6i2KVTebKU8s2jfhZqEms7zrJf000A5rl2o6aILNYG-4mopklwwsH_JVq4UacfCKWYZv_dMWW6Y5Zn2BzmZMZDcUn5yQS_UVO3GPU_2nnM_iA7WgOz_PMr_HzyM-g0AAP__eEWG3A). They see their mom at work every day. "_We work nights, so we get to see her for maybe an hour. She always comes down and says hi_ ," Tayler said. "_It's just the best thing_." Pat, now 72 and retired, says she never pushed anyone into nursing. "_I don't know that I encouraged them_ ," she said. Terryl's response: "_You never said I had to be a nurse, but I think you led the way._ "
## Drone Ranger Reunites 122 Lost Pets
Michael Parziale, 64, owns a restaurant on the Jersey Shore. He also flies 18 high-tech drones, including models with thermal imaging cameras, and has used them to locate [122 missing animals](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO2zAURE8jdd-gvhlaKlSkcbdpUwoUOZS4S5EG-deGbx_YOcK2M4PBw_v7sXzYmGLe_tgDc9jCIqEsGY-WIIK6-GiPkr2PzZU76vOw4vbDfsWFFRtSEw3jYp3EO5ZfvZ8DwDj3mIfLOF3MpJTu95m1nqyB0QyL1btJmbAGjcu4BhjDfZxfd2oaRmZ1Zj6ZadTKukFptxoF12kFH6XU02eJWXaE9HwBnVw5-jTvIrfWnX93fO34Kjsyqm9i2_4avKPYyH97UC3uq1HGgz5RG57ka8mgavOGSt8NjUIChEqgYfzfNpJCa415o4GZUmlCN0ijvRzo-NrX2d8eMaXYzKXTajtsTG80-bnU-8z_AgAA__8woJBp) across New Jersey. Dogs, cats, and at least one runaway cow. Michael's nonprofit, the Unmanned Search and Rescue (U.S.A.R.) Drone Team, started after he used a drone to help find a missing man in a swamp near Toms River. Someone asked if he could find a lost pet next. Then another. "_It just developed into animals because I became really good at that,_ " [he said](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb8GM6awUUYDgk3MZtMNLQZa7R0EC_qNNX__yvcLL-mk65469_57zA9HkdL61-1ol3WZeclzwrNGZMYyB3J7TiFQ9fmN5bM79tvuXjSDAiPVKNthdp7pjXPfBLsgAuoGbXsfxrsZleqazfY9aD9qHVpUfYBgjDbQ974z-NSdDw3ZC6fGdgBQGuBmxqFTzreq80-j0ItOYSDO5fY_U-INl_i5hG4-7020G_NRhf4jYBIwpc-RK18vAdMFFjCp9jpawPRV5VVQwBRKTigPipklF-dfVYZ8JrlTrZRWeSBXueQil-ISk5f5TFiuZFNsOE6Kkaq5i06tu6P448K_X_Ft4TsAAP__DDSIDw). He works alongside his two sons and a rotating group of volunteers, and finances pet searches for elderly owners through a GoFundMe page. One rescue shows how effective the technology can be. After a 5-month-old puppy named Shade went missing on a cold February night, her family searched for more than 24 hours. Parziale was called in and [located Shade in 41 minutes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3upCAUxZ9GO8316igUFNvYzbZbmitchVmQCRCNb79xX-HfneQk5-P35728yXl37L8psNr2bSlbXA6-sudSOC3GUYiHMS7reHK6AxVtA_11CwKODcimEwvp4k5eXrVRGzNyX7PqJiGnUQIMtVVTByTEpoUcV00opWaCXovXsK5sAGunnjiQnUCEHrEdpRiAdAeDXkdgXQ3AxpWY2k90R7G8-fsZ1OoYaq9sKd9c9b8qnCucr-tqb7IxPm6F8_OnwplScdrzIz-cMt9NtjFxY1I8uEl07JyaTCebpuu7FwAMfWtL8HVS5ns5710ep2qAPZDz_5vLz5mdCv8FAAD__2Rwgy8), curled up in a wooded area, cold but safe.

The Regime Open — September 18, 2026
A Rally Built on a Workaround and a Truce That Isn't One
Stocks rallied hard Thursday on an emergency Saudi oil reroute and a Fed fight that only look resolved — one is a temporary patch, the other just moved from the podium to Truth Social.
|
---
Thursday answered two questions this newsletter flagged as open on Wednesday, and both answers cut against the more alarming read. **Verified fact:** the S&P; 500 rose 1.14% to 7,637.72, the Dow gained 0.62% to 51,779.85, and the Nasdaq jumped 1.69% to 26,418.30, as the 10-year Treasury yield fell 7 basis points to 4.934% and oil dropped — WTI down 1.70% to $100.70, Brent down 2.07% to $103.60 — after Saudi Aramco began routing crude around its damaged pipeline via ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's Sohar port. Separately, President Trump confirmed he told Chair Warsh before Wednesday's vote, “you might as well vote with the Board because it's not gonna matter,” then escalated on Truth Social, demanding rates of “1%, or less.”
| | Regime Signal 01 — The Chokepoint Found a Workaround, Not a Fix
---|---
**Verified fact:** Aramco doubled daily loadings at its Gulf terminals to roughly 4 million barrels a day and is shuttling crude to waiting vessels off Oman, sometimes with tracking signals switched off, while cancelling some September cargoes to European buyers and delaying Asian shipments without firm timelines. **Our interpretation:** markets read this as enough good news to unwind Wednesday's selloff, but the underlying description — ships with transponders off, cargoes cancelled, no repair timeline for the pipeline itself — is an emergency workaround, not evidence the chokepoint risk that drove three weeks of this newsletter's coverage has actually resolved.
| | Regime Signal 02 — The Independence Fight Didn't End. It Went Public and Personal.
---|---
**Verified fact:** Trump called the Fed committee “very hostile” and “very political,” while Warsh, asked directly about presidential pressure, said “independence is a two-way street.” **Our interpretation:** Wednesday's unanimous vote and Warsh's “stay in our lane” comment looked like a clean resolution; Thursday showed the fight simply moved from a press conference to Truth Social. Notably, unlike the Powell era, there is no reported talk yet of removal or lawsuits — a meaningfully lower-intensity conflict so far, even if the rhetoric has sharpened.
| | Regime Signal 03 — A Rally Built on Two Fragile Foundations
---|---
**Current classification: Both PRESSURE and CONFIRMATION are still live, depending on the lens.** Thursday's rally confirms markets will reward any credible signal of de-escalation, on energy or on rates. But an emergency shipping workaround and a public presidential demand for near-zero rates are both, by nature, unstable equilibria. **What remains unknown** is whether either holds through next week, or whether Friday and beyond reverse today's optimism once the details of both stories are digested further.
| | Today’s Confirmation Point
---|---
Watch whether Aramco's Oman workaround scales or strains under sustained volume this weekend, and whether Trump's Truth Social escalation produces any concrete administration action beyond rhetoric in the days ahead.

# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260918-1&t=1&akid=4036%2E587540%2EFv_uMZ)
Peter,
Recently, I was on NPR with Michel Martin to talk about the DNC, the future of the Democratic Party, and what direction we should be going in.
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260918_1_genuine.1r1zgi&refcode=em20260918-4036&amount=5&t=2&akid=4036%2E587540%2EFv_uMZ)
Here’s what I said: **the best way to win back the voters we lost in 2024 and gain trust with the American people is to offer them a _genuine_ opposition party.**
Too many politicians are more committed to keeping the status quo in place than they are getting our party into winning and fighting shape, and Republicans are more than happy to watch us stay exactly where we are.
**That’s why real change isn’t going to come from the top of the party.** It’s going to come from our bold and fearless candidates who are leading the way on issues people actually care about — because they know exactly what it’s like to live that reality and have policy shape their daily lives. It’s going to come from embracing new ideas, and not offering people the same tired old messengers with the same tired old talking points.
It’s going to come from LWD endorsed leaders like State Senator Molly Cook who was elected by just 62 votes last cycle, and hasn’t stopped knocking doors even after she was elected. Every month, she’s out with her team talking to thousands of people in her district, asking them what they’re struggling with and finding ways for her office to help. Molly isn’t up for reelection until 2028, but she knows that you can’t gain the trust of your constituents or make a real impact in their lives if you only show up when it’s time to vote.
This is exactly what we need to be doing more of — not just telling people we care, but proving it by literally showing up and asking them how we can help.
Peter, voters don’t want a party that tells them over and over again who they’re not. They want a party with a clear plan that stands in direct opposition to what Trump, Republicans, and their rightwing billionaire allies are doing to this country. **A party that fights hard and wins.**
That’s the work we’re doing at Leaders We Deserve, one young, bold candidate at a time. We’re building a movement that can actually beat Republicans in competitive races and win back voters' trust.

Thank you,
David Hogg

They want a party with a clear plan that stands in direct opposition to what Trump, Republicans, and their rightwing billionaire allies are doing to this country. A party that fights hard and wins. That’s the work we’re doing at Leaders We Deserve, one young, bold candidate at a time. We’re building a movement that can actually beat Republicans in competitive races and win back voters' trust. Thank you, David Hogg
